# Exposition of the Great Prophet Abbot 
# Joachim on the Apocalypse.

## This celebrated work: Golden: namely: and an 

explanation of the Apocalypse by Abbot Joachim <note>Joachim of Fiore (c. 1135–1202) was a mystic and theologian who proposed a "theology of history" divided into three ages.</note>—far loftier and deeper than all others—concerning the universal state of the Christian commonwealth. And concerning the carnal church <term>Ecclesia carnali; a term often used by Joachim to describe the worldly, institutional church in need of spiritual renewal</term> to be reformed in the near future and restored to its original age: though first to be struck by a triple scourge:

->Soon thereafter, the conversion of all<-
->unbelievers to the faith of Christ,<-
->buried for so many centuries:<-
->but now, as the time for fulfillment<-
->approaches, for the benefit<-

and consolation of the faithful (uncovered and unlocked by divine will) it comes to light for the first time.

### To which are added:

The same author's *Psaltery of Ten Strings* <note>original: "psalteriū decē corday"; a major work by Joachim relating the Holy Trinity to the structure of a ten-stringed musical instrument</note>, a work truly divine.

Also a summary index, gathering all the most beautiful passages.

# To the Most Reverend Father in Christ, Lord Egidio, Cardinal-Priest of the Title of Saint Matthew. His devoted son, Brother Silvestro Meuccio of Castiglion Fiorentino (a hermit and professor of the Augustinian family), offers eternal commendation.

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial 'C' featuring a heraldic coat of arms. The shield displays a tree, possibly an oak or pine, surmounted by a cardinal's hat with its distinctive tassels. The shield is set within a rectangular frame decorated with classical foliate scrolls and scrolls in the corners.</image-desc>

Since it happened several years ago (after your mission to Spain and many other provinces was completed) that your Most Reverend Lordship returned to the City <note>Rome</note> by way of Venice—where you were greatly and deservedly honored by that Most Illustrious Senate—I sought you out, moved by a desire to see you. Having shown you such reverence as I was able, you soon asked me to bring you certain short works by Abbot Joachim, which you had heard were printed through my care. When these were brought and you had read for a little while, you were not a little delighted. You encouraged me, saying that I would do something wonderfully pleasing to you if I would see to the printing of other works by the same author, and especially his work on the Apocalypse. Because I realized this—since I strive day and night to do what is pleasing to your Most Reverend Lordship—by my faith, I would have done it as soon as the printers <term>Calchographi; literally "copper-writers," a term for early printers or engravers</term> could have managed it. 

But now (since a favorable opportunity has arisen), I have wished for this work to come into the light under your distinguished name, protected by your coat of arms on the front and dedicated to your Most Reverend Lordship. I did this partly because your Most Reverend Lordship requested this work from me; partly to further declare my devotion to you; and partly so that the present work might go out into public more honorably, possessing both the grace of novelty and authority among readers. Furthermore, it seemed to me that no one else was more worthy than you to have this famous work addressed to them. For (to omit the innumerable virtues of your wise mind), you far excel all others in the study of the best and most noble disciplines. You have emerged as a most shining light, not only in human affairs but truly in divine ones as well. 

What shall I say? For it is said that you shine not only in Latin literature (the height of which you have remarkably attained) but no less in foreign languages, such as Hebrew, Greek, Chaldean <note>original: "Caldayeis"; usually referring to Aramaic or Syriac, which were essential for biblical studies</note>, and Arabic; so much so that it is not easy to find your equal in this age of ours. You also preserve the holy religion of our true faith with a pure heart. You always display the greatest piety toward all, proven character, the highest equity, justice, and a certain divine clemency of soul. Finally, you are one who, most observant of the Platonic precept, loves all scholars and guides them with a singular and ample patronage. This is especially true since I have no doubt that our entire family of Hermits <note>The Augustinian Order (Order of Saint Augustine), to which both the editor and the Cardinal belonged</note> is being reformed for the better every day under your protection and leadership. Add to this that the same Abbot Joachim celebrates this order with pious honors and increases it with praise beyond others, so that in the final age of the world, the order... <note>The sentence is interrupted by the page break; "ordi" likely continues as "ordinis" or "ordinem".</note>

<summary>A dedication letter from the editor Silvestro Meuccio to Cardinal Egidio da Viterbo, praising the Cardinal's immense learning and explaining how his encouragement led to the publication of Joachim of Fiore's works.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the dedication by Silvestro Meuccio to Cardinal Egidio da Viterbo. The previous page established the context of their meeting in Venice and the Cardinal’s request for Meuccio to print the works of Abbot Joachim of Fiore, particularly his commentary on the Apocalypse. This page focuses on Joachim’s prophecies regarding the "Order of Hermits" (the Augustinians) and their role in the coming renewal of the Church.</meta>

<sig>A 2</sig>

...that the Order of Hermits <note>original: "Eremitagen"; referring to the Order of Hermits of St. Augustine, to which the author and the Cardinal belonged</note> itself, supported by the power of divine grace, would bring about the faith of Christ (glowing like a burning fire in zeal and the love of God) and that the collapsed Church would be reformed and all things restored. For so he <note>Joachim of Fiore</note> says in chapter 14 in the explanation of this work: "There shall arise an order that seems new, but is not. Clothed in **black garments** and girded above with a **leather belt**. These will grow and their fame will be spread abroad; they will preach the faith, which they will also defend until the end of the world, in the spirit and power of Elijah <note>Elijah was considered the prototype of the monk and hermit</note>. This will be the order of Hermits, imitating the life of angels. Their life will be like a burning fire in the love and zeal of God to burn up thorns and thistles—that is, to consume and extinguish the ruinous life of the wicked—lest the evil abuse the patience of God any longer."

So says Joachim; and the Lord Archbishop of Florence <note>Saint Antoninus of Florence (1389–1459), a famous Dominican theologian and historian</note> recites this same passage literally in the last title of the third part of his historical work, where he treats our aforementioned order. Lord Ulrich of Weimar <note>likely Henry of Friemar the Elder (c. 1245–1340), an influential Augustinian author whose name was often variants of Ulrich or Henry</note>, an eminent doctor of our religion, also mentions this in his treatise on the origin of this order, adding: "And just as by the strength of the root, the branches are naturally brought forth high and wide, so by the virtue of the Institutor and Founder, and of the other succeeding fathers (who were of distinguished holiness and the primary founders of this order), it is most likely to be presumed that a copious blessing will descend upon their sons and descendants through divine mercy."

For the order itself was founded by our father **Blessed Augustine**, from whom it received its rule and form of living; nor can this be turned into doubt. Indeed, Joachim himself testifies to this in the introductory part, saying: "The Order of Hermits was founded by Blessed Augustine in Africa. But the Order of Canons Regular was founded in the western parts by Blessed Rufus <note>Saint Rufus of Avignon, traditionally associated with the Canons Regular</note>, although they also hold the rule of Augustine himself."

Likewise, on Jeremiah chapter 1, he says: "Although a new order of preachers <note>original: "ordo praedicantium"; while this eventually became the name for the Dominicans, Joachim uses it here for a prophesied spiritual group</note> then—that is, in the future tribulation itself—may seem to arise for the Church, nevertheless it was initiated first by the prophets, then by the apostles, and finally by the doctors of the third ecclesiastical period: beloved, known, and chosen by God, signified in Isaac and John the Baptist. From which order indeed came the Order of Monks, and from these two, the other orders afterwards emerged. These two orders are to be revealed again through their new and astounding reformation, so that they seem to arise anew. For just as Elijah lived in the fourth age of the world, leading a hermit's life (at which time likewise Elisha and the sons of the prophets inhabited the deserts) and is to be revealed again in the sixth age, so also the Hermits (who correspond to him by agreement and type) existed and flourished in the fourth ecclesiastical time, and likewise are old and yet to be revealed (in the manner aforesaid) and propagated until the end of the age. They shall enter the times of justice and abundance of peace, and shall see the breaking of the statue <note>A reference to the statue in the Dream of Nebuchadnezzar from the Book of Daniel, representing the fall of worldly kingdoms</note>, and shall overcome the nations and kingdoms with the sword of the divine word, once the truth of the faith has been recognized."

Wherefore Joachim himself continues in the same 14th chapter, saying: "I think that in that time after the ruin of **Babylon** (that is, the carnal church), the life of monks will be like rain to water the surface of the earth in all perfection and justice of fraternal charity. But the life of Hermits will be like a burning fire in the love and zeal of God to burn up the thistles..."

<summary>Silvestro Meuccio uses the prophecies of Joachim of Fiore to argue that the Augustinian Hermit order is divinely ordained to lead the coming reformation of the Church. He links the order to the biblical figure of Elijah and the historical foundation of St. Augustine, positioning it as an ancient institution that will appear "new" in the final age of history.</summary>

...and thorns: so that neither the grace of God for salvation be lacking to the good, nor the impious abuse any further the patience of God. These men (at the prompting of the Spirit) will rebuke the sins of transgressors more harshly, as if in the spirit and power of Elijah <note>Elijah was traditionally seen as the prototype of the monastic and eremitic life</note>. These and similar sayings (concerning the two aforementioned orders) fill his entire small works, so that it can be clear to all reading them. 

These few things out of many, my most Reverend Lord <note>original: "mi Dn̄e. R."; refers to Cardinal Egidio da Viterbo</note>, concerning the Order of Hermits itself, have compelled me to bring forward and insert here. First indeed: because certain of our modern friends, thinking and asserting that wherever this author speaks of these two orders (which will perform such and so great wonders for the faith of Christ), he wants it to be understood as referring to their own orders. How far this differs from the truth is apparent from what I have brought forward. Another reason driving me to this was so that it might not remain hidden from your Reverend Lordship <note>original: "R.D. tuam"</note> what this author felt concerning our Order of Hermits. Since they assert that he possessed the gift and spirit of prophecy, no small faith is to be attributed to him. 

I have also added his *Psaltery of Ten Strings* <note>original: "Psalteriū decē cordaꝝ"; one of Joachim’s three main works, using the ten-stringed lyre as a symbol for the Trinity</note>. In this, he beautifully investigates the supreme Trinity and its distinction. He treats the number of the psalms and their secret and mystic senses; the nature of psalmody; and the manner and use of singing, as well as the nature of those who sing. These uses and mysteries shall flourish most greatly after the ruin of Babylon <note>In Joachite thought, "Babylon" often represented the corrupted state of the Church or the world</note>, now that peace has been given everywhere to the lovers of Christ and his church has been renewed (like the youth of an eagle). 

I have added also a very clear reading on the Apocalypse itself by a most famous doctor of our sacred order, namely [videlicet] Master Philip of Mantua <note>Filippo da Mantova, an Augustinian theologian</note>. He spoke so learnedly and clearly that I have seen no one as his equal. Lastly, I do not doubt that I shall be excused by your Reverend Lordship for my lack of skill in the faculty of speaking and writing, since you have known my ignorance of such an art almost from my early youth. 

Wherefore, best Prelate, this work (by its own right) both attaches and vows itself to you. Receive it therefore; and read it with a grateful soul. And cherish and love me, who am devoted to you through these very small labors. Farewell, most bright ornament and protection of our religious life. 

At Venice, in our island retreat of Saint Christopher of the Peace <note>San Cristoforo della Pace, a monastery in the Venetian lagoon</note>, on the Kalends of February, 1527.

For a greater understanding of the mysteries contained in this and other small works (by this author), those things must be set forth which the author himself sets forth in his exposition on Isaiah: namely, he first sets forth:

¶ The three states of the world <note> Joachim’s famous "Three Status": the Age of the Father (Old Testament), the Age of the Son (New Testament), and the approaching Age of the Holy Spirit</note>, beginning from Adam and proceeding until the end of the world. Then certain concordances and agreements or combinations; and the meanings and the signified things of diverse times.

¶ He sets forth also the mystery of the church, which is revolved annually (inserted into prayer), beginning from its head: namely [v̄] from Septuagesima <note>The liturgical season of seventy days before Easter, representing the Babylonian captivity</note>. Through this are declared and signified the tribulations and pressures which the church has suffered and will suffer until the end of the world. And therein are found consolations and divine aids.

¶ He sets forth the time before the law, the time under the law, and the time of grace, along with their sacraments.

¶ The Trumpet and its figure and meaning; the Seals and their openings.

¶ He sets forth the dragon of a different figure, having seven heads designating seven universal tribulations or wars: namely, the evils which the church herself and her members have suffered and will suffer throughout seven periods of time.

¶ He sets forth the *Psaltery of Ten Strings*, in which one is instructed to flee, to conquer, and to overcome the snares of that spirit and ancient enemy. This was prefigured in David who, by singing, drove away the evil spirit agitating Saul.

¶ He sets forth also the mystery of the Wheels <note>Referring to the vision of Ezekiel</note>, through which in a wondrous and ingenious way he distinguishes the multiple senses and understandings of the divine scripture. Or rather, he elucidates this far more subtly and clearly in the treatise of the *Psaltery of Ten Strings* itself, where he posits twelve senses of the sacred page.

¶ We have said these things would be certain preliminaries for understanding many mysteries and sayings of this author, for this reason: in almost all his works he uses such figures and terms, and without the knowledge of these, many of his sayings cannot be understood.

He provides a list of essential symbolic concepts, such as the Three States of the World and the Seven Seals, which serve as a key for readers to decode Joachim's complex mystical theology.</summary>

# UPON THE APOCALYPSE

->**[PROPHETIC DIAGRAM]**<-

| | | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **First circle:** Moses and Aaron. 1st state; the twelve sons of Israel. They departed from Egypt. | **Second circle:** Paul. Uzziah 2nd state; the twelve elect were established. | **Third circle:** Benedict. 3rd state. Twelve [shall go] through the land. | **Fourth circle:** Two witnesses, apostles or orders. Revelation 11. Men who entered the mission. Joshua 4. |

<margin>Exodus 4; Genesis 2, 46</margin> <margin>Genesis 2; Matthew 1; Luke 1</margin>
The first state of the world <note>original: "status seculi"; Joachim’s famous "Three Ages" theory—Age of the Father (Law), Son (Grace), and Spirit (Monasticism)</note> shone forth from Abraham: its beginning was from Adam, and its end was in Christ. The second state shone from Zechariah, the father of John the Baptist, in whom the priesthood of the Law fell silent; its initiation was from Uzziah, King of Judah, and it is predefined to last until the year 1260. <margin>3rd part 14, 26</margin> The third state begins to shine in our own days: its initiation was from the blessed Benedict <note>St. Benedict of Nursia, founder of Western monasticism</note>, and it shall reach its completion at the end of the age. <margin>1 Maccabees 1; Ibid.</margin> Truly, the first state was led to its end by Antiochus, the "root of sin," who came out of the land of Kittim (that is, Greece). The second state will be given its end by that "planting of the roots" of Frederick <note>A reference to Emperor Frederick II, whom Joachimites often identified as an Antichrist figure</note>: his offspring or the "arms" proceeding from him shall occupy the heights of authority, as is read in the book of Isaiah. <margin>Isaiah 9; Revelation 12</margin> "Each of them," it says, "after their leader, divided the Macedonian land freely, and placed crowns upon their heads, and evils were multiplied on the earth." <margin>Daniel 8</margin> To the third state, however, an end shall be given by the prophet teaching lies, the Antichrist, as if in the tail of the dragon; although he is to reign for only a short space of time, he will nevertheless devastate the entire world beyond what can be believed. <margin>Joel 2; Job 28; Matthew 2</margin> Hence, Joel says: "A devouring fire is before his face, and behind him a desert solitude." And Job: "The land from which bread arose has been overturned by fire in its place." For although Christ, the true bread, arose from the Synagogue, and <margin>Isaiah 6; Luke 4; Genesis 46</margin> always flows from the Roman Church through teaching, that Church is nevertheless burning with the great fevers of avarice <note>Greed or corruption within the Church hierarchy</note>; therefore, let her beware, lest her Lord overthrow her even now in this first tribulation.

Those who entered Egypt designate the apostles.

<margin>Joshua 3; Acts 19</margin> Those who were chosen in the desert signify those upon whom Paul laid his hands.

<margin>Acts 13</margin> Those who carried the cluster of grapes from the Promised Land on a pole prefigure the two future orders <note>referring to the Dominicans and Franciscans, or more generally to new monastic reformers</note> who will be witnesses; there is no doubt they represent the truth of the Gospel. <margin>Revelation 11; Acts 1</margin> "You shall be," He says, "witnesses for me in Judea, and Jerusalem, and Samaria, and even to the end of the earth." "Judea" signifies the Latins; "Jerusalem" signifies the clergy; "Samaria" the Greeks; and the "end of the earth" the peoples who are to be converted to the Lord. <margin>2 Timothy 3; Acts 8; Acts 13</margin> Just as Jannes and Mambres <note>The legendary names of Pharaoh's magicians</note> rose against Moses and Aaron, and as Simon Magus and Elymas rose against Paul and Peter, so shall the Patarenes <note>term for medieval heretical groups like the Cathars</note> and other heretics rise up against the two future witnesses; these heretics are prefigured by the two horns of the beast, as is read in the Apocalypse. <margin>Revelation 11; Revelation 13</margin>

The time of the sons of Jacob (the Patriarchs) signifies the time of the Apostles.
The time of the Judges signifies the time of the Martyrs.
The time of the Prophets signifies the time of the Confessors.
The time of the sons of the Prophets signifies the time of the Hermits and Virgins. <margin>Genesis 49; Joshua 1</margin>
The time of Joshua (who uprooted idolatry) signifies the time of the Church when Pope Leo the Sicilian shattered the heresies. <margin>Psalm 136</margin>
The sixth time, in which the Jews sat by the rivers of Babylon, represents this present time, in which both the clergy and the people are everywhere fornicating <note>metaphorically straying from faith</note> away from God. <margin>Hebrews 4</margin>
The seventh time, however, will be the time of those converting to Christ. Whence it is said: "A Sabbath rest remains for the people of God," regarding the quiet of liberty according to the Spirit and the turning toward the sacrament of faith. <margin>accomplished: Luke 3:21</margin> Whence Luke says: "It came to pass when all the people were baptized," which has not yet been fully completed in the Church. <margin>Romans 11</margin> It will be completed, however, under the seventh angel, as the apostle says: "When the fullness of the Gentiles has entered in, then all Israel shall be saved." To this state it is said in the Song of Songs: "Your hair is like flocks of goats ascending from Mount Gilead," <margin>Song of Songs 6</margin> which is the head of Lebanon—that is, the mountain of incense.

It uses biblical typologies, such as the entry into Egypt and the two witnesses of Revelation, to predict the rise of new monastic orders and the eventual conversion of all peoples.</summary>

For a greater understanding of the mysteries contained in this and other short works of this author, those things must be placed first which the author himself sets forth in his exposition on Isaiah <note>original: "Esayam"</note>: namely: first he sets forth the three states of the world <note>The "Three Ages": the Age of the Father (Old Testament), the Age of the Son (New Testament), and the Age of the Holy Spirit (Future Monastic Peace)</note>, beginning from Adam and proceeding until the end of the world. ¶ He sets forth a dragon of another figure, having 7 heads, designating 7 universal pressures or battles: the evils which the church itself and its members have suffered and will suffer through seven periods of time.

# ON THE APOCALYPSE

</margin>

The **first state** <note>original: "status"; Joachim of Fiore’s term for a great era of world history</note> of the world shone from **Abraham**; its beginning was from **Adam**, and its end in **Christ**. The **second state** shone from **Zechariah**, the father of **John**; in this era, the priesthood of the Law became mute <note>A reference to Zechariah being struck dumb in the Gospel of Luke</note>. Its beginning was from **King Uzziah** of Judah, and it extends until the year **1260**. The **third state** must begin to shine from our own days; its initiation was from the **Blessed Benedict**, and it will reach its end in the consummation of the age. Truly, **Antiochus**, the "root of sin" coming out of the land of Kittim <note>original: "Lethym"; a biblical term for the Greeks or Romans, here glossed as Greece</note>, brings the first state to its end. To the second state, that "planting of the roots" of **Frederick** <note>Refers to Frederick II, the Holy Roman Emperor, whom many Joachites identified as an Antichrist figure</note> will give its end; his offspring or "arms" coming forth from him, and his high offices of power—as read in the book of <term>Maccabees</term> <note>original: "mach."; two books of the Bible detailing the Jewish revolt against the Seleucid Empire</note>—will occupy the world. Each of them (it says), to whom the land was divided after the Macedonian leader, placed crowns upon their own heads, and evils were multiplied on the earth.

But to the third state, the **Antichrist**—that prophet who teaches lies—is going to bring the end, as if in the tail of the dragon. Although he is to reign for only a short space of time, he will nonetheless devastate the universe beyond what can be believed. Hence **Joel** says: *A consuming fire is before his face, and after him a lonely desert.* And **Job**: *The earth from which bread originated was subverted by fire in its place.* For although the true bread [Christ] rose from the Synagogue in time, and always flows out from the **Roman Church** through doctrine, yet the Church now burns with the great fevers of avarice. Therefore, let her beware for herself, lest her Lord subvert her already in this first tribulation.

Those who entered **Egypt** designate the **Apostles**. Those who were chosen in the desert signify those upon whom **Paul** laid his hands. Those who carried the cluster of grapes on a pole from the Promised Land prefigure the **two future orders** who will be witnesses—there is no doubt of this evangelical truth. *You shall be witnesses to me* (He says) *in Judea, Jerusalem, and Samaria, and even to the ends of the earth.* **Judea** signifies the **Latins**; **Jerusalem**, the **clergy**; **Samaria**, the **Greeks**; and the **ends of the earth**, the peoples who are to be converted to the Lord.

Whence it is said: *A Sabbath rest is left for the people of God,* regarding the quiet of liberty according to the Spirit and the conversion regarding the sacrament of faith. So says **Luke**: *It happened when all the people were baptized,* which has not yet been completed in the Church. It will be completed, however, under the **seventh angel**, as the Apostle says: *When the fullness of the Gentiles enters in, then all Israel shall be saved.* To this state it is said in the **Song of Songs**: *Your hair is like flocks of goats ascending from Mount Gilead,* which is the head of **Lebanon**, that is, of "providence."

# PREFACE

...and without thorns: <note>original: "sine spinas"; the catchword from the previous page completes this phrase, likely referring to the "pure" word of God</note> so that the grace of God for salvation is not lacking for the good, nor do the impious further abuse God’s patience. These people (at the Spirit’s prompting) will rebuke the sins of the delinquent more harshly, as if in the spirit and power of **Elijah**. His small works are entirely full of these sayings and similar ones (concerning the two aforementioned orders), as can be clear to all who read them. These few things out of many, my **Reverend Lord R.**, regarding the **Order of Hermits** <note>The Augustinian Hermits, the religious order of the editor</note> itself, have compelled me to bring and insert them here.

First, indeed, because certain of our modern friends think and assert that wherever this author speaks of "two orders" (who will perform such great deeds for the faith of Christ), he intends it to be understood as referring to *their* own orders. How far this is from the truth is apparent from what I have presented. Another reason driving me to this was so that it would not remain hidden from your **Reverend Lordship** what this author felt concerning our **Order of Hermits**. Since he asserts that he possessed the gift and spirit of prophecy, no small amount of faith should be granted to him.

I have also added his ***Psaltery of Ten Strings***. In this work, he beautifully investigates the supreme **Trinity** and its distinctions; the number of the psalms and their secret and mystical senses; psalmody; and the manner and use of singing, as well as those who sing. The use and mysteries of all these things—after the ruin of **Babylon** <note>In this context, a prophetic reference to the corruption of the worldly Church</note>—will flourish greatly, once the peace of Christ is given everywhere to His lovers and His Church is renewed (like the youth of an eagle).

I have also added the "Peaceful Lecture" on the **Apocalypse** by the most famous doctor of our sacred order, **Master Philip of Mantua** <note>Filippo da Mantova, an Augustinian scholar</note>. He spoke so learnedly and clearly that I have seen no one to be his equal.

Finally, I do not doubt that I shall be excused by your **Reverend Lordship** for my lack of skill in the faculty of speaking and writing, since you have known my ignorance of such arts almost from my youth. Therefore, best of prelates, this work (by its own right) adds and vows itself to you. Receive it, therefore; read it with a grateful soul. And cherish and love me, who am devoted to you for these few labors. Farewell, father and brightest glory of our religion.

At **Venice**, in our island monastery of **Saint Christopher of Peace**, on the Calends of February <note>February 1st</note>, 1527.

***

For a greater understanding of the mysteries contained in this and other works by this author, certain things must be presented first which the author himself presents in his exposition on **Isaiah**:

¶ First, he presents the **three states of the world**: beginning from **Adam** and proceeding until the end of the age.

¶ Then, certain **concords** <note>original: "concordias"; Joachim's method of matching Old Testament figures to New Testament history</note> and agreements or combinations; and the meanings and things signified by different times.

¶ He presents the **mystery of the Church**, which revolves annually (inserted in prayer) beginning from its head and from **Septuagesima** <note>The period of seventy days before Easter</note>; through this are declared and signified the tribulations and pressures which the Church has suffered and is to suffer until the end of the world. It contains consolations and divine aids.

¶ He presents the **time before the Law**, the **time under the Law**, and the **time of Grace**, along with their sacraments.

¶ The **Trumpet** and its figure and significance; the **Seals** and their openings.

¶ He presents the **Dragon** of another figure, having 7 heads, designating 7 universal pressures or battles: namely, the evils which the Church itself and its members have suffered and will suffer through seven periods of time.

¶ He presents the ***Psaltery of Ten Strings***, in which one is instructed to flee, conquer, and overcome the snares of the impious serpent and ancient enemy; this was prefigured in **David**, who, singing to the spirit, put to flight the evil spirit agitating **Saul**.

¶ He also presents the **mystery of the wheels**, through which he distinguishes the multiple senses and understandings of Holy Scripture in a wondrous and ingenious way—though he elucidates this more specifically, and far more subtly and clearly, in the treatise on the ***Psaltery of Ten Strings*** itself, where he posits **twelve senses of the sacred page**.

We have said these things to be general points for the understanding of many mysteries and sayings of this author; truly for this reason: that in almost all his works, he uses figures and terms of this kind, without the knowledge of which many of his sayings cannot be understood.

# Index of the Exposition on the Apocalypse by Abbot Joachim

### Here begins the Index of the principal sayings of the venerable Abbot Joachim in his exposition on the Apocalypse.

**That** Abbot Joachim commands that all his small works be presented for the examination of the Church; at least after his death, if it cannot be done before. Folio 1, column 2.
**Concerning** the brief of admonitions of Pope Clement <note>original: "Clementis pape"</note>: that as soon as Joachim himself has completed the exposition on the Apocalypse, he should wish to present it to him, so that it may be for the benefit of the faithful. Folio 1, col. 2.
**How** Rebecca bore the foreshadowing <term>type: a biblical person or event seen as a precursor to a later one</term> of the Church. Folio 2, col. 1.
**That** the author says he is bound by the authority of the Pope to wish to explain the book of the Apocalypse. Folio 2, col. 2.
**That** he says he is able to show by certain and necessary proofs that tribulations <note>original: "pressuras"</note> are at hand. Folio 2, col. 2.
**That** the angel of Daniel predicted that the words were not to be closed and sealed until the end of the world, but until a pre-defined time. Folio 2, col. 3.
**That** he who cannot believe is unable to understand. Folio 2, col. 4.
**That** the author calls the first book the "Introductory," in which the material of the entire book and work is contained. Folio 2, col. 4.
**How** the books of the entire Old Testament are divided. Folio 2, col. 4.
**Why** the book of the Apocalypse is called "sevenfold" and concerning its special status. Folio 3, col. 2.
**How** Sacred Scripture is called "living waters." Folio 3, col. 2.
**That** the Apocalypse is the prophecy of all other prophecies and encompasses all others. Folio 3, col. 2.
**How** in each individual part a recapitulation <note>a summary or retelling of previous points</note> always occurs. Folio 3, col. 3.
**That** John the Evangelist is called the chamberlain <note>original: "camerarius," an official in charge of a household or treasury</note> of heaven. Folio 3, col. 2.

<column-break/>

**That** the Old Testament from Abraham until Christ was wrapped in seven seals. Folio 4, col. 1.
**Concerning** what the seven wars of the Hebrews denote. Folio 4, col. 1.
**That** the books of the Maccabees are not in the official list of scripture <note>original: "in canone"</note>. Folio 4, col. 2.
**How** the sixth period is seen to be divided into two parts. Folio 4, col. 2.
**Concerning** the three and a half hours Christ hung suspended on the cross. Folio 4, col. 3.
**That** the Jews converted to Christ will sing and praise the Lord. Folio 4, col. 1.
**How** in the sixth period there ought to be two persecutions. Folio 5, col. 1.
**How** the three states <term>status: Joachim's famous theory of three ages of history</term> of the world or the Church are to be understood. Folio 5, col. 2.
**How** the surpassing brilliance of Saint Benedict is to be expected near the end of the world, namely in the time of Enoch and Elijah; and that the Jewish people will be converted. Folio 5, col. 2.
**How** it appears that the literal meaning of the prior Testament belongs to the Father; that of the New Testament to the Son; and the spiritual understanding which proceeds from both literal texts belongs to the Holy Spirit by a certain similarity. Folio 5, col. 2.
**How** just as the order of the married seems to belong to the Father, and the order of preachers to the Son, so the order of monks—to whom the final times are given—belongs to the Holy Spirit. Folio 5, col. 3.
**What** the time under the literal Gospel is: of spiritual understanding and manifest vision; and how all times are five. Folio 5, col. 3.
**That** the mystery of the Trinity is declared in the Patriarchs. Folio 5, col. 3.
**How** from Adam until Moses sin was not imputed because of the lack of law, and how this is understood. Folio 5, col. 4.
**How** the three periods are ascribed in different ways to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Folio 5, col. 4.
**That** after the resurrection our bodies will be spiritual and temples of the Holy Spirit, because nothing corruptible will remain in them. Folio 6, col. 1.
**How** such a rule of mysteries in Divine Scripture is frequently used by the Fathers or holy doctors. Folio 6, col. 2.

# Index to the Exposition on the Apocalypse

**Division** of the states <term>status: Joachim’s "states" or "ages" represent major eras of salvation history—the Age of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit</term> regarding the extension of time. Folio 6, column 2.
**Concerning** the harmony and connection to one another of the two testaments. Folio 6, col. 3.
**Concerning** the opening of the seals in the prior or Old Testament. Folio 6, col. 3.
**Likewise** concerning the opening of the seals of the New Testament. Folio 6, col. 3.
**How** the Eastern Church is compared to the ten tribes of Israel. Folio 7, col. 3.
**The Empire** of the Romans is compared to the empire of the Chaldeans, and that of Egypt to the ungodly empire of Constantinople. Folio 7, col. 3.
**In the kingdom** of the Greeks are contained, in spirit, Samaria and Egypt; and in the kingdom of the Latins, Jerusalem and Babylon. Folio 7, col. 4.
**How** the German emperors <note>original: "imperatores alamannorum"</note> strive to take away the liberty of the Church, especially in temporal <note>worldly or political</note> matters. Folio 7, col. 4.
**The destruction** of Babylon is compared to the destruction of Rome. Folio 7, col. 4.
**An explanation** is given of that saying about the seven kings in the Apocalypse: "of whom five have already fallen," etc.; and how, while the sixth still exists, the seventh will come. Likewise concerning the ten kings who are to come after them, the worst of all. Folio 8, col. 1.
**How** the New Babylon <note>Often referring to the corrupt worldly Church or Rome in Joachim's theology</note> is soon to be struck, and this by several kings. Folio 8, col. 2.
**How** the people of Mohammed <note>original: "mahumeth"</note> will fight against the New Babylon. Folio 8, col. 3.
**Concerning** Mohammed and his followers, it is said: "The beast that was and is not," and how that beast is to rise again from the abyss. That is, the people of the infidels will do this, especially at the suggestion of the other beast rising from the earth and from the false prophet; after which the infidels will be converted. Folio 8, col. 3.
**That** under the sixth opening <note>of the seals</note>, the New Babylon is to be struck; and just as after Antiochus an end was given to the Old Testament, so also after Gog will be the consummation of the age. Folio 9, col. 1.
**That** the year 1200 was the end of forty generations. Folio 9, col. 3.
**That** the "end of the age" in the Holy Scriptures is understood in both a broad and a strict sense. Folio 9, col. 3.

<column-break/>

**That** the time of the first state was from Abraham until John the Baptist; of the second, from him until the present; and of the third, from the present time until the end of the world. Folio 9, col. 4.
**How**, once the pressures from the infidels which are soon to come are finished, there will be a blessed time; and the earth will be full of the knowledge of God, so much so that scarcely anyone would dare to deny that Christ is the true Son of God—excepting only certain nations which the devil will bring forth against the faithful at the very end, namely: Gog. Folio 9, col. 4.
**Just as** at the end of the first state the last king, namely Antiochus, was more cruel than the rest, so at the end of the second state, which will be very soon, that seventh king is to come of whom it is said here: "and one has not yet come." Folio 10, col. 1.
**That** at the end of the third state, namely at the end of the world, another who is the worst of all will come, namely Gog, who will himself be the Antichrist, the one of whom it is principally spoken. Folio 10, col. 1.
**What** were and will be the seven heads of the dragon; and which was the first, second, etc. Folio 10, col. 1.
**How** that phrase is to be understood: "five kings have fallen, and one is, and one has not yet come." Folio 10, col. 1.
**How** Daniel and John agree in the Apocalypse regarding the beast, the horns, and the kings, etc. Folio 10, col. 1.
**That** there will be a seventh head of the dragon, and concerning his tail; that there will be another and final king coming in the power and spirit of the former, just as John [the Baptist] came in the spirit and power of Elijah. Folio 10, col. 2.
**That** the Devil desires nothing so much as to be found in all things contrary to the works of the Creator; and an example is given. Folio 10, col. 2.
**That** he who is called in the Apocalypse the king and the seventh head will be that Great Antichrist who will deceive an infinite multitude of Jews and Gentiles, so that few will escape his craftiness, wickedness, and cunning. Just as Christ is called King, Priest, and Prophet, so will he lie <unclear>about himself</unclear> <note>original: "mentiet"</note>.

The first was joined to the Father through fear; the second was joined to the Son through humility; the third was united to the Holy Spirit through devotion. Folio 18, column 2. <note>original: "Sarra... Rebecca... Rachele" — Joachim uses the wives of the patriarchs to symbolize the progression of the Church through history.</note>

Folio 19, column 1. <term>New Babylon: Joachim's term for the corrupt worldly systems or institutions that must fall before the spiritual age of the Holy Spirit begins.</term>

How the Church is called "Jerusalem" in a threefold state: the first is likened to and designated in Sarah; the second in Rebecca; the third in Rachel. The first was joined to the Father through fear; the second was coupled to the Son through humility; the third was united to the Holy Spirit through devotion. Folio 18, column 2.

That in the beginning of the <term>second state</term> <note>Joachim divided history into three "states" or "ages" (status): the Age of the Father, the Age of the Son, and the Age of the Holy Spirit.</note>, the Son and the Holy Spirit were sent. Folio 18, column 2.

That the human race is divided into three states: the first, of the married, was created in the image of the Father; the second, of the clergy, was established in the image of the Son; the third, of the monks, in the likeness of the Holy Spirit; see the illustration. Folio 18, column 2.

That the order of the married continued from Adam until Christ, and is called the first state of the world; the second is from Christ, in which is the order of the clergy; the third is after the destruction of the <term>New Babylon</term> <note>Joachim used "New Babylon" to describe the corrupt world or a worldly Church that must be purified.</note>, in which is the order of the monks, dedicated to the Holy Spirit. who, although they hold the rule of the Blessed Augustine, were nevertheless established by Saint Rufus in the western regions. Folio 19, column 2.

How monasteries of virgins were established by holy doctors; this religious life is signified in Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid; born as a son to her is the order of Greek monks, designated in Dan. Folio 19, column 2.

That whenever Christ Jesus is narrated to have received anything from the Father in time, or to have performed anything in the "form of a servant," we must remember that apostolic manner: namely, "Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery [to be equal with God]." Folio 26, column 2.

Christ Jesus, insofar as he is man, received this book—namely, the Apocalypse—from the Father, and not insofar as he is God. Folio 26, column 2.

The Son of God became man by being born; he became the "Title" <note>The "Titulus" refers to the inscription placed above Jesus on the cross.</note> on the cross by dying; a Lion by rising from the dead; and an Eagle by ascending to the heavens. Folio 26, column 2.

This revelation is not to be known by the wicked and the impious, but by the good and the servants of God: because the good and the elect hear the word of God for salvation, while the impious hear it to their greater damnation, so that they cannot excuse themselves. Folio 27, column 1.

In this book, the name of an "angel" is not introduced simply; but by the name of an angel, something holy or an order is always understood mystically, or something pertaining to the matter is designated. Folio 27, column 1.

It is the custom of the Holy Scriptures that men sent by God are called "angels" <note>The Greek word "angelos" literally means "messenger."</note>, as is said of John the Baptist: "Behold, I send my messenger [angel]," etc. Folio 27, column 1.

The ministers of the altar are called Angels. Folio 27, column 1.

This book is not only called a "prophecy" in a specific sense like other books, but also in a general sense: because the Holy Spirit has condensed into the sum of this book of prophecy what the extensive volumes of the prophets brought forth in a scattered and confused way. Folio 27, column 2.

While we encounter many false people whom we think are truthful, it happens that we hold both the good and the bad in suspicion indifferently, and we often believe those who closely adhere to God to be liars. Folio 27, column 2.

Regarding when a leader ought to cease from the correction of the wicked: when iniquity overabounds, and it is no longer safe for him to live among those wicked ones, and when he can no longer make any progress. Folio 75, column 2.

Concerning the year of the Lord 630: The Emperor Heraclius, who had gloriously defeated the King of the Persians occupying Jerusalem, returned the wood of the Holy Cross (which had been taken by the defeated king) to its original place with the immense joy of the Christian peoples. Folio 76, column 1.

Folio 77, column 2. <note>The "shattering of the statue" refers to the prophecy in the Book of Daniel regarding the destruction of worldly empires.</note>

That to the five general churches (which belong to Peter) pertain five works of Christ, or five virtues established through them; but to the seven churches which belong to John—namely, those to which he himself writes—pertain the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit. Folio 78, column 1.

That by the church of Sardis is understood the fifth order, which is the order of Western monks, whose father was Saint Benedict. Folio 78, column 1.

Regarding monks or religious persons who love themselves and seek only their own interests, and who think little of the common salvation which is useful to many: such are not to be called monks, but rather pseudo-monks. Folio 78, column 2.

That the first four orders, which are designated by the four living creatures, lasted until the common time pertaining to the throne of God arrived: that is, the time of the herald-angel and the fifth period of the Church. Folio 79, column 1. <note>The "four living creatures" are the winged beings from the visions of Ezekiel and Revelation.</note>

That the hypocrite has only the name of being alive, but he is dead; just as the Pharisees were hypocrites, from whose teaching the Lord commands the apostles to beware; for nothing is more detestable to God than hypocrisy. Folio 79, column 1.

How dangerous or difficult it is to not know how to discern between hypocrites and the just man, and how many evils follow from that. Folio 79, column 1.

How the vigilance of pastors benefits their subjects and negligence harms them, notwithstanding God's predestination of the elect and his foreknowledge of the reprobate: note. Folio 79, column 1.

That one order does not fail unless another has first begun.

In whose state <note>Joachim’s "Third State" or Third Age of the world.</note> the *Psaltery of Ten Strings* <note>original: "psalterium dece cordaru"; one of Joachim’s major theological works.</note> is composed; and the book of psalms of David: which properly pertains to the Holy Spirit speaking spiritual words: and for the one singing psalms in it: a beautiful note. Regarding that which belongs to no one: it passes into the right of the occupant <note>A legal principle meaning the first person to claim unclaimed property owns it.</note>, all the more so when it is given to someone by Him who possesses it by a just right. Folio 98, column 2.

Regarding how the Lord's knocking at the door is either to rouse our hearts by hidden inspirations or to invite us to the palm of victory by open revelations and promises. With what small dishes God is delighted, and with what gifts and sacrifices He is appeased. Folio 98, column 2.

What kind of difference there is between the supper and the dinner <note>original: "cenam & prandium." These represent different stages of spiritual nourishment or historical eras.</note> of the bridegroom. Folio 98, column 2.

# Index to the Exposition on the Apocalypse

That the New Babylon <note>original: "noua babylon"; Joachim often used Babylon to represent the corrupt institutional Church or a worldly society that persecutes the true spirit.</note> must set aside its golden finery and take up lamentation and mourning, because its greatest tribulation and destruction is approaching. Folio 117, column 2.

That it is necessary for Babylon itself to receive in the sixth period—at the opening of the sixth seal—the same evil it inflicted on others in the fifth period, and twice as much besides. Folio 117.

That according to the opinions of the Blessed Augustine and Jerome, whoever attacks the Church of Peter <note>The Roman Catholic Church.</note> with their conduct or by force should know and tremble that they are children of Babylon. Folio 117, column 2.

That the kings who are destined to strike the prostitute <note>The "Whore of Babylon" from the Book of Revelation, interpreted here as a corrupt religious system.</note>—to cleanse the surface of the earth because of those false Christians—will also kill the true and faithful worshippers, so that they may be crowned with martyrdom. Folio 117, column 2.

That the "Day of Judgment" is understood broadly as the time near the end, and strictly as the final day of judgment, as Augustine notes. Folio 118, column 1.

That in the coming tribulation (which will arrive suddenly and unexpectedly), many who are thought to be vigorous and excellent teachers will be cast down. Folio 118, column 1.

That the return <note>original: "plapsis," likely a corruption of "parousia" or "adventus."</note> of Elijah the prophet is uncertain. Folio 118.

That it is necessary for the priests of the Church in this world to often fear, following the example of sailors against whom a storm-spirit rises up unsuitably. Folio 118, column 2.

That peace is a friend to the lifestyle of those in contemplation, and a desired tranquility, because devotion cannot be stirred by sorrow. Folio 118, end.

That just as the stars in heaven illuminate these lower regions, so do the elect in the Church and the prelates <note>High-ranking church officials like bishops.</note> illuminate those under their authority. Folio 119, column 1.

That in the sixth period, because of the great tribulation of the faithful, once the communities of monks or religious orders and the clergy have been driven from their places, they will either be destroyed entirely so they no longer exist, or they will not be permitted to follow their own laws, except for those designated in Noah’s Ark. Folio 119, column 2.

### Here begins the Table for the fourth book.

That what the seven priests with their seven trumpets signified around the walls of Jericho in the Book of Joshua: these same things are signified by the seven Angels with seven trumpets in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>. Folio 123, column 2.

That in the first part of this book, it treats specifically of the leaders of the people (namely, the prelates of the churches); in the second, the army of holy martyrs; in the third, the angels sounding trumpets (namely, the doctors and preachers); in the fourth, the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord (which designates the church of hermits and virgins); and in the fifth, the temple of the tabernacle (which designates the multitude of the elect among the people following the figured Ark of the Lord). Note that these things mentioned are of great weight, and the prudent reader ought to consider them diligently. Folio 123, column 2.

<column-break/>

That just like the city of Jericho, for six days (that is, through six periods) until the opening of the seventh seal, preachers and holy men foretold the ruin of the world; but in the final time (that is, the opening of the seventh seal), they did not go around once or twice, but seven times, repeating their circuit; wherefore at the last, the walls of Jericho collapsed <note>Joachim uses the fall of Jericho as a "type" or historical parallel for the end of the worldly age.</note>. Folio 123, column 2.

That under the seventh angel sounding the trumpet, the destruction of the worldly kingdom is at hand; the Doctors of the holy Church will preach this with one voice, and they will do so with constant urgency—just as a rooster placed in the dawn cries out more frequently and insistently than usual. Folio 123, column 2.

That although the Gospel of Christ has been laboriously announced to the world in the six periods, nevertheless, regarding its fullness and spiritual understanding, it will not be manifested until the seventh, when the enemies of the Cross of Christ will be converted to Him. Folio 123, column 2.

That the seven often-mentioned periods are contained under the sixth age of the world (namely, under the New Testament); when that age is finished, the world will fall along with its inhabitants. Folio 124, column 1.

That in holy scripture, regarding the historical sense (which overshadows the spiritual intelligence), when the seventh opening of the seal arrives, there will be silence; but regarding the spiritual understanding, it will then be opened much more fully. Folio 124, column 1.

That the clarity of the understanding of holy scripture will begin to appear to some in the sixth period—which until now has remained hidden as if under a cloud—but in the seventh (that is, when the seventh angel begins to sound the trumpet), then men will see many things concerning God; and recognizing the truth of God, they will henceforth rest from this kind of labor, because there will no longer be a need for it. Folio 124, column 1.

That ignorance of holy scripture is and has been the mother of error, because of which many heresies have existed and will exist until the seventh period.

# Index of Abbot Joachim

->cc<-

The **crown of twelve stars** refers to the **twelve virtues**. These are born within us: five are directed against the five senses (which are considered the minor virtues) and seven are called the major virtues. These are: first, **penitence**; second, **mercy**; third, **patience**; fourth, **humility**; fifth, **faith**; sixth, **hope**; and seventh, **charity**. See a beautiful explanation of how these are acquired through the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit. <note>Joachim of Fiore often structured history and spirituality around sets of seven, matching the seven seals of the Apocalypse.</note> Folio 155, Column 1.

That without the first six virtues mentioned above, no one reaches **charity**, which is the root and mother of all others. Folio 155, Column 2.

How a **Catholic man** ought to depict in his heart such a perfect and spiritual man, adorned with the aforementioned virtues; if any of these are missing, he can be neither perfect nor saved. Note how this is derived. Folio 155, Column 2.

How a crown is fashioned upon the head of the spiritual and perfect man from the said virtues; note how they are placed. Folio 155, Column 2.

That in the **moon** is designated the chaste humility of the **simple brothers** <note>original: "simplicium fratrum" — likely referring to the rank-and-file monks or the Cistercian 'lay brothers'.</note>; in the **sun**, the justice of the **perfect ones**, which is set ablaze by the fire of charity; and in the **ordered line of a camp**, the virtue of brotherly charity. Folio 156, Column 1.

That **Elisha** <note>original: "Helyseus"</note> bears the type <note>A "type" is a biblical person or event that foreshadows a future person or event.</note> of the **monastic life**, he who once presided over the multitude of brothers in Jericho. Folio 156, Column 1.

That **Elisha**, through a fair agreement, reflects **Saint Benedict**; for although the institution of the holy monastic life is ascribed to Benedict in his own time, its perfection shone forth in the fourth period. Folio 156, Column 1.

That the **first person of the Church of the fourth period**—namely, that of the virgins and hermits—was the **Blessed Virgin Mary**. Folio 156, Column 1.

That the **body of the devil**—that is, his "mystical body"—is the multitude of the reprobate <note>The "reprobate" are those destined for or deserving of condemnation, the opposite of the "elect".</note>. Folio 156, Column 1.

That the **seven heads of the dragon** are seven named tyrants who succeeded one another through the ages in persecuting the Church; but the **ten horns** are ten kings who will reign together, and they themselves will be against the Church. Folio 156, Column 2.

That by the **tail of the dragon**, **Gog** is understood, about whom it is written in Ezekiel 38; he is the final tyrant who is to come at the end of the world. Folio 156, Column 2.

That although the **devil** had known those things which were written concerning **Christ**, he did not know them fully; 

<column-break/>

and for that reason, he tempted him. Folio 156, Column 2.

[How far] the east is from the west: [it is the distance between true love of God] and that love which exists for temporal things. Folio 159, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> Those who love God for temporal things do not worship God truly, but deceitfully; for when temporal things fail, those people whom the devil well knows fail as well. This is the basis of the devil's reasoning when he says: *Does Job fear God for nothing?* etc. Folio 159, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> When we wish to rebuke the faces of those who despise justice, we place before them the lives of obedient brothers as a contrast; so that those who cannot be overcome by words or warnings may be put to shame when convicted by the comparison. Thus, they may either be corrected or, if they are incorrigible, they may fall silent. Folio 159, column 2.

<margin>¶</margin> In a contrary manner, it happens to both the good and the wicked from the correction and admonition given to them: for while the life of the good advances from it, the wickedness of the wicked grows beyond measure. Folio 159.

<margin>¶</margin> God commends the justice of the holy man, namely <note>original: "s. Job"</note> Job, before the father of lies <note>A traditional title for the Devil, based on John 8:44.</note> so that by reproaching his pride He might confound him; for having abandoned the grace of simplicity, the devil wished to be the author of all depravity, and in every way fell by deserting the truth. Folio 159, column 2.

<margin>¶</margin> The devil tries to ascribe his sin to a corrupt nature rather than to his own judgment <note>original: "arbitrio suo"</note>; which he did not use well, but willfully abused. Folio 160, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> The property of truth is to recognize that there is no good except from God alone; and with Him, who is the highest truth, there is no iniquity. Folio 160, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> In the time of Constantine, the number <note>original: "plūū" (plenum/fullness)</note> of martyrs was completed; for then the Church began to be ordered for the salvation and virtue of many, and the Vicar of Jesus Christ <note>The Pope.</note> began to have free power to exact vengeance upon the nations and rebukes upon the peoples. Folio 160, column 2.

<margin>¶</margin> The devil, seeing himself overcome by the second group <note>The martyrs of the early Church.</note>, attacks the faithful and the Church through a third group directed against the simple and unlearned; and this is done through heresies. Folio 160, column 2.

<margin>¶</margin> Two primary virtues are necessary above all others for those desiring to know the truth: namely, Wisdom—which is from above—and the Charity of God. Folio 161.

<column-break/>

<margin>¶</margin> Wisdom is attributed to Christ, and Charity to the Holy Spirit. Folio 161, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> Without these two virtues and gifts, there can be no perfection of contemplation <note>The highest form of prayer and spiritual insight.</note> which is necessary for contemplatives. Folio 161, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> To remain in the desert is, properly speaking, to rest and be free from worldly works. Folio 161, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> In the time of the heresies of Arius <note>Arius (d. 336) taught that Christ was not co-eternal with God the Father, a major early Christian conflict.</note> and others, many faithful chose the eremitic <note>Hermit-like.</note> life, deciding it was better to live with beasts in the woods than to participate with the Arians in the marketplace; just as Elijah, in the time of the kings, when he saw the people of Israel given over to error, withdrew himself from their sight for three and a half years, receiving meat as food first from ravens and then from a widow woman. Folio 161.

<margin>¶</margin> The mystery is the same (by means of concordance <note>Joachim's method of "concordance" matches Old Testament figures with New Testament or Church history counterparts.</note>) between Elijah—who was a pre-figurer of the virginal and eremitic life in the number of years, his flight, his stay in the wilderness, and his food—and the Woman spoken of here who fled into the solitude. Folio 161, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> The place where the Woman flees in the solitude is spiritual; it is the contemplative religious life, which exists even in the cities. Folio 161, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> Frequently, by recognizing the fault of others, we avoid it; we could by no means guard against it in ourselves unless we first blamed it by judging it in others. Folio 161, column 2.

<margin>¶</margin> The order of monks, designated in John the Evangelist, inhabit or inhabited the southern part and region. Folio 162, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> The first war was that of the one whom the Woman bore; the second was Michael's and his angels'; the third was the Woman's in the time of the heretics; and the fourth is truly of those to whom it is given to be free for prayers and psalms—namely, the hermits and the virgins. Folio 162, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> This book is of the greatest subtlety, in which nothing specific can be assigned without general principles. Folio 162, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> The meaning of the beast ascending from the sea: Daniel saw it divided into four beasts. Folio 162, column 1.

<margin>¶</margin> Heaven signifies the Church or Holy Scripture. Folio 162, column 1.

# Index to the Explanation of the Apocalypse

That he shall learn of the rising from the west: from that which happens for the sake of temporal things. Folio 159, column 1.
<margin>¶</margin> That they love God for temporal things: they do not worship God truly, but deceitfully; because when temporal things fail, they themselves also fail. The devil, knowing this well and founding his reasoning upon it, says: "Does Job fear God for nothing?" <note>A reference to Job 1:9, where Satan suggests Job only serves God because of his wealth.</note> etc. Folio 159, column 1.
<margin>¶</margin> When we wish to rebuke the faces of those who despise justice: we set before them the lives of others in contrast, such as the obedience of the brothers; so that those who cannot be overcome by words or warnings may be put to shame when convicted by these comparisons: so that they might either be corrected, or, if they are incorrigible, they may fall silent. Folio 159, column 2.
<margin>¶</margin> In a contrary manner, it happens to both the good and the wicked from the same correction and holy admonition: for while the life of the good is perfected by it, the depravity of the wicked increases beyond measure. Folio 159.
<margin>¶</margin> God commends the righteousness of the holy man, namely Job, before the father of lies <note>The devil.</note>: so that by reproaching his pride, He might confound him; who, having abandoned the grace of simplicity, wished to be the author of all depravity, and who fell by deserting the truth in every way. Folio 159, column 2.

<margin>¶</margin> The property of truth is to recognize that there is no good except from God alone: and with Him, who is the supreme Truth, there is no iniquity. Folio 160, column 1.
<margin>¶</margin> In the time of Constantine <note>The first Roman Emperor to convert to Christianity, ending the era of state persecution.</note>, the battle of the martyrs was completed: because then the Church began to be ordered for the salvation and virtue of many, and the vicar of Jesus Christ began to have free power to enact vengeance among the nations and rebukes among the peoples. Folio 160, column 2.

# Index to the Exposition on the Apocalypse

Regarding the one hundred and forty-four thousand <note>original: "ta quattuor miliū," an abbreviation for "centum quadraginta quattuor milium"</note> martyrs and as many virgins, so that they may be as princes and prelates of that multitude which cannot be numbered. Folio 172, column 2.

That by the angel flying through the midst of heaven having the eternal gospel, he understands the same as him who cried out above with a great voice, "Woe, woe, woe to the inhabitants of the earth," who was the blessed Pope Gregory. <note>Joachim often identifies historical figures like Pope Gregory the Great as the fulfillment of specific apocalyptic messengers.</note> Folio 173, column 1.

That in this place, by the "hour of judgment," the final Day of Judgment is not understood, but rather the time of the Babylonian desolation. Folio 173, column 1.

That the messengers of Almighty God are sometimes sent long before the time and sometimes near it; yet whether they are sent long before or near the time, they uniformly say that the judgment of God is "near," because with God all things are near and present. Folio 173, column 1.

That he thinks this angel is the blessed Gregory for this reason: because among all things he wrote, it is evident that nothing was so familiar to him as persuading men of the fear of Almighty God and the Day of Final Judgment. Folio 173, column 1.

That in the days of the blessed Gregory, Mohammed had already begun to weave his web, through which the opportunity was given for that fourth beast to come forth from the abyss and to do all those things which God foreknew would be done through him. <note>Joachim views the rise of Islam ("the fourth beast") as beginning in the time of Gregory the Great.</note> Folio 173, column 1.

That three angels are soon to be revealed—namely, at the end of the second state <note>original: "secundi status," referring to Joachim's Age of the Son</note> and the fifth period of the Church—all crying out with a great voice. The first has the task of preaching the eternal gospel to all nations; the second announces the destruction of Babylon, saying, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great"; the third has the task of forbidding communion with the beast, lest anyone should worship the beast or its image. Folio 173, column 1.

That the first of the aforementioned angels must precede the others under the opening of the fifth seal; but the remaining ones follow together under the opening of the sixth, who will perhaps be—as was said above—those two witnesses; note concerning Elijah. <note>The "two witnesses" of Revelation 11 are often identified with the return of Elijah and Enoch.</note> Folio 173, column 1.

That after the fall of Babylon, false Christs and false prophets will arise, along with the beast that ascends from the earth to deceive (if possible) even the elect. Folio 173, column 2.

<column-break/>

That the harlot Babylon herself and the Empire of the Romans are to be handed over to the beast—namely, to the infidels. Folio 173, column 2.

That the infidels and false Christs will say that the Roman Empire was handed over to them because the religion of the Christian name is false; and immediately a preacher of Christ will rise up against them. Folio 273 <note>Likely a printer's error for 173</note>, column 2.

That he who has an iniquitous heart always thinks evil, and when placed under the scourge, he does not give off the scent of spices, but the smoke of stinking sulfur. Folio 174, column 2.

That when the good are afflicted, they bless the Lord, and that blessing is an aromatic smoke. Folio 174, column 2.

That when the wicked are afflicted, they murmur and blaspheme; and their blasphemy rises up like the smoke of sulfur or the stench of rotting flesh. Folio 174, column 2.

That Christ, through his passion, rested from all suffering, and together with his companion—namely, the thief—he entered paradise with the palm of victory. Folio 174, column 2.

That although the thief was crucified for his crimes, nevertheless, after his confession, the punishment due for his sins was turned into virtue and made voluntary through the love of Christ. Folio 174, column 2.

That just as Christ suffered on the sixth day and rested from his labors on the Sabbath, so in the sixth period of the Church, the passion of the body of Christ—namely, the mystical body <note>term: "corpus christi misticum" — the Church as the collective spiritual body of believers</note>—will be completed. After this, there will be a glorious Sabbath, whether in those who already reign with Christ, or in those who remain upon the earth after the fall of the Antichrist, continuing in life according to the will of God until that time is completed which is called the Last Day. Folio 175, column 1.

That the author <note>Joachim of Fiore</note> says he does not wish to be seen as inventing anything of his own accord, for he is a man who has been a farmer from his youth; nor should anyone think that anything ought to be demanded of him which was not permitted to be demanded of the prophets themselves before their time. Folio 175, column 1.

That just as the prophets saw in part and prophesied in part, so we also see now; for it is one thing to see many things, and another to see everything. Folio 175, column 1.

# Abbot Joachim
## cc 4
->Catchword: Concerning and<-

A city appears one way when it is still far off according to reports: it appears another way when one arrives at the gate, and another when one goes inside. Therefore, we who are at the gate can speak of many things that were hidden from others either entirely or in part; but those who will be inside will see "eye to eye." <note>A reference to Isaiah 52:8. Joachim suggests that his own prophetic understanding is like standing at the gate, while future generations will have direct, clear vision of these mysteries.</note> Folio 175, column 1.

Concerning the two angels having sickles and the two others calling to them, the interpretation is not entirely certain. Folio 175, column 1.

The state of that Church which is to be in the final time after the ruin of the beast cannot be fully described as it is destined to be. Folio 175, column 1.

The first angel who sits upon the white cloud having a sharp sickle signifies a certain order of the just to whom it is given to perfectly imitate the life of the Son of Man—that is, of Christ—and of John the Evangelist. Folio 175, column 2.

The said angel and the men of the said order will have a learned tongue to preach the gospel of the kingdom of God and to gather in the Lord's threshing floor the final harvest. Folio 175, column 2.

The second angel who came out from the temple and cried out to the first to reap, because the hour has come and the harvest is ripe: this signifies the Son of Man, without any of his greater messengers. Folio 175, column 2.

The aforesaid order, or the men of that order, will have from the manifest gift of God the power to announce the coming judgment to the world no longer through riddles <note>original: "per enigmata," a reference to 1 Corinthians 13:12, suggesting that their knowledge will be direct rather than obscure.</note> but in truth; they will struggle against all vices and overcome them, and because of the preceding victory against the beast and the false prophets, they will be considered worthy to preach the gospel to the elect and gather the wheat into the kingdom of heaven. Folio 175, column 2.

The aforesaid order will be entirely spiritual and contemplative, and it will not be subject to active labor <note>original: "actioni," referring to the "active life" of manual or administrative work, as opposed to the "contemplative life" of prayer.</note> as we are forced to be, even if many are unwilling; but that order, through the abundance of grace, will be more intent on contemplation. Folio 175, column 2.

Just as there is a distance between the black earth and a white cloud, so there also seems to be this distance between physical exercise and the contemplation of heavenly things; for in the former, physical things are acquired, while in the latter, spiritual things are attained. Folio 175, column 2.

<column-break/>

The third angel who came out of the temple which is in heaven, also having a sharp sickle, signifies another order. Folio 175, column 2.

The first order, which is designated on the cloud, is humbler; the second is designated in heaven. Folio 175.

In each of those who have sickles, certain orders are designated; however, in those who cry out to them, the Son and the Holy Spirit are to be understood, whose cry is manifest inspiration; or certainly some spiritual men through whom the Son and the Holy Spirit themselves will speak more specially. Note how [this is so]. Folio 175, column 2.

The New Testament is contained within two states of the world. <note>Joachim of Fiore is famous for his theory of three "status" or ages: the Age of the Father (Old Testament), the Age of the Son (New Testament/Church), and the coming Age of the Holy Spirit.</note> Folio 175, column 2.

Although the first of these two orders, designated by the angel ascending upon the white cloud, may persist in contemplation compared to those who are entangled in earthly business, nevertheless, that one which comes out of the temple which is in heaven is of a higher life. Folio 175, column 2.

There is to be a future order of perfect men keeping the life of Christ and the apostles, designated in the first angel who is like the Son of Man. Folio 175, column 2.

There is another future order contemplative of divine love, designated in the angel who came out of the temple which is in heaven; this will be the order of hermits emulating the life of the angels. Folio 175, column 2.

The men or religious of the first order who serve as soldiers for God in a humbler perfection are given for the benefit of those who observe them in the sight of the chosen people, so that they may receive from them warnings of salvation and an example of pious conversation and perfection. Folio 176, column 1.

The order of hermits, in order that it may live more perfectly, seeks more remote places; and if ever, by the suggestion of the Spirit, they go out to men, they are thought to have arrived as if from the vaults of heaven. Folio 176, column 1.

When the said hermits, if ever at the suggestion of the Spirit, go out to men, it often tends to shake the hearts of those looking on and wondering with fear—whether because of the perfection of their life or the novelty of their presence. Folio 176, column 1.

Also, the said hermits, at the suggestion of the Spirit, will more harshly rebuke the sins of those who fail.

In 그 time after the ruin of the beast, the life of the monks shall be like rain to water the surface of the earth in all perfection and the justice of brotherly charity; but the life of the hermits shall be like a burning fire in the love and zeal of God to burn up the briars and thorns, so that grace for salvation is not lacking to the good, nor do the impious abuse the patience of God any longer. Folio 176, column 1.

The order of monks shall be, as it were, milder and sweeter for gathering the harvests of the elect of God, as if in the spirit of Moses. Folio 176, column 1.

The order of hermits shall be fiercer and more ardent than the order of monks, for gathering the <term>vintage</term><note>The "vintage" refers to the gathering of grapes for the winepress of God's wrath (Revelation 14:19), representing the judgment of the wicked, as opposed to the "harvest" of grain which represents the gathering of the righteous.</note> of the <term>reprobate</term><note>Those rejected by God or destined for damnation.</note>; as if in the spirit of Elijah. According to a saying of the Blessed Jerome: a certain person said that Elijah and his companion would not be killed by the beast, but certain others would be; and that they themselves would come without delay after the ruin of the Antichrist to bring all these things to a consummation. Folio 176, column 1.

In whatever way these things may happen, it is certain that two men are to be sent together: one in the spirit of gentleness who commands the harvest to be gathered; the other in the spirit of zeal who commands the vintage to be concluded; because even up to that point in time, some will be predestined to life and some foreknown to death. Note how. Folio 176, column 2.

In the time of Christ, when forty generations from Abraham were completed, the harvest of the circumcised people came; so also now, after forty generations, will be the harvest of those who have been called and will yet be called into the faith. Folio 176, column 2.

The final preaching of this age is designated by sickles and not by swords: because the sickle holds whatever it takes all at once and encompasses many things together into one; but in other times, the axe placed at the root of the tree threatened judgment with many blows and delayed it in that time, but it is not so here. Note this. Folio 176, column 2.

The said harvest, both of the reprobate and the elect, is to be consummated under the sixth angel, and when there will no longer be time for penance. Folio 176, column 2.

There are two things that exceed measure, so that they ought not to be tolerated: namely, the immensity and the long duration of guilt. Folio 177, column 1.

The final harvest and these evils which have been spoken of will occur at the end of the <term>six ages of the world</term><note>A traditional Christian division of history into six periods, corresponding to the six days of creation, with the seventh age being the eternal Sabbath.</note>. Folio 177, column 1.

The impious would always wish to continue doing the evil they have begun, even to persist forever, invincible in their crimes. Folio 177, column 1.
