### Part of the Exposition
## E 2

...we nevertheless understand Him to be one: and supremely one. For it is not one person who says, "I am Alpha," <note>original: "Ego sum A." Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet.</note> and another who says, "I am Omega." <note>original: "Ego sum O." Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.</note> Rather, He who is one God says, "I am Alpha." He who is Triune says, "I am Omega." Indeed, the Triune and one God says both at the same time. He also says: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." He says: "I am <margin>Exodus 3</margin> who I am," and, "This you shall say to the children of Israel: 'He Who Is' <note>The divine name revealed to Moses, signifying absolute existence.</note> has sent me to you." For it is not different to say, "I am Alpha," than to say, "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." Nor is it different to say, "I am Omega," than to say, "I am Who I Am," and <margin>Exodus 3</margin> "This you shall say to the children of Israel: 'He Who Is' has sent me to you." 

Nevertheless, many say what we say and confess what we confess, and yet, holding only the words in which the truth of the words resides, they are ignorant of the understanding. Nor is this a wonder; for God himself, of whom we speak, says that He appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty <note>original: "in deo omnipotente"</note>; but He says, "My name Adonai <note>original: "Adonay." A Hebrew name for God meaning "My Lord," used here to refer to the deeper revelation of the name YHWH to Moses.</note> <margin>Exodus 6</margin> I did not reveal to them." Why is this? Because the secret mystery of the Trinity and Unity is great, and it cannot be opened in any way to unspiritual men <note>original: "animalibus hominibus." This refers to those who live by natural instinct rather than spiritual grace.</note>. Indeed, Almighty God, as God Almighty, appeared to the three patriarchs; and by showing the riches of His glory in three ways to the three orders of that people, He revealed Himself through open signs to be the Almighty God. 

He showed Himself to be Almighty in the order of the patriarchs when He bestowed upon one of them, whom He chose, the son He had promised in his old age; and when He consecrated and increased that blessed offspring born of a sterile parent, so that within a few years He led them forward into an immense multitude. He showed Himself Almighty in another way among the children of Israel when He rescued those who were subject to Pharaoh from the servitude of the Egyptians with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and He placed them powerfully in a land not their own, giving them judges and defenders who would rescue them from the power of their enemies. Again, He showed Himself Almighty in a third way among the children’s children when, according to what He had promised to Abraham, He produced kings from his loins, subjecting the kingdoms of foreign nations to them, just as it is said through the Psalmist:

<column-break/>

"Into Edom I will extend my shoe; <margin>Psalm 59</margin> the foreigners are subject to me." <note>A reference to Psalm 60:8 (Vulgate 59:10), symbolizing God’s dominion over neighboring nations.</note> The time of the patriarchs was completed within approximately four hundred and eighty years. Similarly also was the time of the judges. Likewise, the time of the kings lasted until Nebuchadnezzar, who prostrated the kingdom of Judah by humbling it. 

Now, in the patriarchs, there was a likeness of the Father, from whom all fatherhood in heaven and on earth is named. <margin>Ephesians 3</margin> There was a likeness of the Son in the judges, to whom the Father gave all judgment; <margin>John 5</margin> who also came into this world for this purpose: to fight and to conquer, and who must (according to the Apostle) reign until He puts all His enemies under His feet. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> The likeness of this victory was completed at the end of the time of the judges—that is, in the days of Samuel and David—from whose time kings began to exist among that people. 

The likeness of the Holy Spirit was also shown in the kings because of the mystery of anointing, which pertains to the same Spirit, just as it is said to that true King, of whom these kings were a type, <note>In theology, a "type" is a historical person or event that foreshadows a future one, usually Christ.</note> through the Psalmist: "God, your God, has anointed you <margin>Psalm 44</margin> with the oil of gladness above your companions." <note>Psalm 45:7.</note> For even the man Christ Jesus has the likeness of the Holy Spirit, just as John the Baptist has the likeness of the Son, and Zechariah the likeness of the Father. As I recall writing elsewhere: just as the likeness of the Trinity is recognized in Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, so it is in Zechariah, John the Baptist, and the man Christ Jesus. The first of these [Zechariah] begat according to the flesh; the second [John] was begotten; the third [Jesus], according to the flesh, had neither father nor son, being likened to the Holy Spirit, who is neither begotten nor begets. 

Why, then, did Almighty God appear to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty, since He showed Himself Almighty in the aforementioned three orders of that people, fulfilling all that He had promised and showing in them His own image and likeness? But if in that first state of the world, as a type of the supreme Trinity, three times and three types of men were noted, what shall we say the second and third states mean (about which we have spoken in this work), except that which...

# John's First Part on the Apocalypse
## E 3

...belongs to the Father; it belongs also to the Son; it belongs also to the Holy Spirit. And that which belongs to the Son, belongs also to the Father and the Holy Spirit; and that which belongs to the Holy Spirit, belongs also to the Father and the Son. This is because the Son is in the Father, and the Father is in the Son; and the Holy Spirit is in both, and both are in Him. Therefore, that the mystery of the Trinity is found in the first state of the world <note>Refers to the era of the Patriarchs before the Law was given.</note> is a matter of a specific mystery, not a general one—and of the fact that specific things are also common to all. 

However, regarding what was said there: "I am Alpha and Omega," <note>original: "Ego sum A. & .O." Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet.</note> where mention of the final coming of the Lord had preceded it, this clearly hints to us what we hold by faith: namely, that every truth is to be opened to us, and that this is the end of the Lord’s works, when the Lord himself shall come for the final judgment. Then it will truly appear, that which has already shone upon us in some way—specifically, from that time when Christ began to open the seven seals. 

To the people of the Jews, He appeared in God Almighty in those three ways written above, teaching that He is a triune and one God. Nevertheless, He did not disclose His name **YHWH** <note>original: "IEVE." A Latinization of the four-letter Hebrew name for God, Yahweh.</note>—which the Hebrews read as *Adonai* <note>meaning "My Lord."</note>—to them, because He did not reveal through a specific understanding that He was a triune and one God until that true Moses, the mediator between God and men, Christ Jesus, appeared. When the hour of His passion was pressing, so that He might pass from this world to the Father, after many things which He spoke to His disciples, He added and said: "I will no longer call you servants, for a servant does not know what his master does; but I have called you friends, because all things whatsoever I have heard from my Father I have made known to you." <margin>Exodus 6; John 15</margin> 

But when did He speak this word, if not when He made known to them that ineffable name which is **YHWH**? He spoke to them clearly about the Holy Spirit and about the Father, and about the glory of His majesty, saying: "I am in the Father, and the Father is in me." <margin>John 14</margin> And: "If you ask anything in my name, this I will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate <note>original: "paraclitum." From the Greek 'Parakletos,' meaning a helper, comforter, or legal advocate.</note> to remain with you forever, the Spirit of Truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him." And because He taught so clearly that there are three 

<column-break/>

persons co-eternal and co-equal to Himself—namely, one and triune God, which is to say **YHWH**—it was nonetheless necessary for Him to teach which of these persons was unbegotten, which was begotten, and which was proceeding. This He manifests clearer than daylight in the following passages, when He says: "When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of Truth, who proceeds from the Father, He will bear witness of me." <margin>John 15</margin> 

And after a few more words: "I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. However, when He, the Spirit of Truth, comes, He will teach you all truth. For He will not speak on His own, but whatever He hears He will speak, and He will announce to you the things that are to come. He will glorify me, because He will receive from what is mine and announce it to you." <margin>John 16</margin> For in this the Holy Spirit glorifies the Son: in that He teaches through specific sacred mysteries <term>sacramentis: here meaning 'mysteries' or 'sacred signs' of divine truth</term> that He proceeds from the Son just as He does from the Father. The exception is this: the Father has this from no one; the Son has it not from Himself, but from the Father. This the Son Himself openly manifests when He says: "When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father." And again: "All things that the Father has are mine; therefore I said that He will receive from what is mine and announce it to you."

In this way, the only-begotten Son of God, Christ Jesus, taught His friends whom He chose out of the world everything He heard from His Father—specifically the mystery <note>original: "sacramentum"</note> of the Trinity, which was not recognized by other generations as it has been since the time He came into the world. For even if there were holy men <note>Referencing the Old Testament prophets and patriarchs.</note> to whom this venerable mystery was revealed, it should not be said that it was "revealed" in a general sense, because private and hidden favors do not override public and solemn ones. 

For the people designated by the order of the Patriarchs were earthly and "animal," <note>original: "aialis" (animalis). In a theological sense, this refers to the 'natural' or 'soulish' man who lacks spiritual discernment.</note> as the entire face of the Scriptures proclaims. Thus, they could not ascend the mountain with Moses because of their own perspective—just as there are some Christians today whose understanding is "animal," like those to whom the Apostle spoke: "I could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as fleshly, as if to infants in Christ. So I gave you milk..." <margin>Exodus 19; 1 Corinthians 3</margin>

# Part of the Abbot’s Exposition
## E 3

...I gave [milk], not solid food. <note>original: "non escam." A reference to 1 Corinthians 3:2, where Paul speaks of giving spiritual milk to those not yet ready for solid food.</note> It is enough for those of this sort simply to believe what is heard. Regarding the name of God, which is *Adonai*, <note>original: "Adonay." The Hebrew word for "Lord," used by Jews as a substitute for the sacred four-letter name.</note> it is better for them to remain silent than to speak. For we do not read that Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob drove their sheep into the inner parts of the desert as Moses did; <margin>Exodus 3</margin> and therefore, what was denied to them was quickly granted to him. For unless someone strives to be far from the tumults of the world—even if they are otherwise just and good—they cannot understand the invisible things of God. 

However, because at the end of this book, where there is a repetition of this word saying, "I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end," <note>original: "Ego sum A et Ω primus et novissimus principium et finis." From Revelation 22:13.</note> it was stated shortly before: "He has sealed the words of the prophecy of this book. For the time is near." I believe this was given to us who are wise—those who are to be called, as if quickly, out of darkness into the marvelous light of Christ—so that we might be able to penetrate the profound mysteries of that sacred name. This name is said to be ineffable <note>Incapable of being expressed in words.</note> and has been known to lie hidden in the "secret of secrets" until now. We may come to know what is contained within it, if not according to our own will, then according to the measure given by the Giver. 

It should be known, therefore, that this venerable name—which is quite appropriately called "ineffable" by both the Hebrews and the Latins—is pronounced *Adonai*. However, in Hebrew, it is not pronounced with the same characters as it is written, but with others. For it is written with four letters, which is why it is noted among the Greeks as the *Tetragrammaton*. <term>Tetragrammaton: A Greek term meaning "four letters," referring to the divine name YHWH.</term> Its inscription is this: **IEVE**. <note>The author uses the Latin letters I-E-V-E to represent the Hebrew letters Yod-He-Waw-He.</note> This name, as the most skilled of the Hebrews pass down, is of such great power that if it is divided into three utterances so that it may be brought forth piece by piece—**IE** individually, **EV** individually, **VE** individually—each distinct part holds the integrity of its own name; and if they are uttered together as **IEVE**, it demonstrates unity. For if these distinctions are written in a triangular figure—which is to say, "I am"—each of the three has its own perfection, and each demonstrates a property of a [divine] Person. And what is greater than this: the second name is propagated from the first, and the third from the second, in such a way that one cannot be pronounced without the other. This is true even if it is permissible to speak of a "first" and "second," since they are not three

<column-break/>

names, but one name. 

Regarding this, I ask that indulgence be granted to me, so that I may speak however I can, since I cannot speak of the matter exactly as it is. For the Fathers themselves wished for no other [allowance] than to be permitted to speak "improperly" when they called them "three substances" or "persons." <note>The author is navigating the difficulty of using human language—terms like "substance" or "person"—to describe the transcendent nature of the Trinity.</note> Therefore, let me be allowed to use the term "Person" out of necessity, even though it is far from the simple truth [of God's nature], so that I am not forced to remain silent on such a great matter. Thus, the second name is propagated from the first, and the third from the second, so that one cannot be pronounced without the other: just as the letter **E**, which is written after **I**, is common to the first name and the second; and the letter **V** is common to the second and the third. By this, because the second name depends on the first, the only-begotten Son of God is shown to be *consubstantial* <term>consubstantial: Of the same essence or substance; a key term used to describe the relationship between Father and Son.</term> with Him by whom He was begotten. And because the third name depends on the second, the Holy Spirit is shown to be consubstantial with the Son, who is consubstantial with the Father. 

However, observe carefully in this matter that the letters themselves are not to be multiplied in reality in the same way they are multiplied in the voice when we pronounce those three [parts] individually. Rather, while those same four letters remain in their place, we ought to pronounce those three one after another in such a way that the second name seems to depend on the first, and the third on the second. We are better able to show this through the figures themselves than to unlock it with fitting words. For as I have already said, the same letters are not to be multiplied so that we write **IE**, **EV**, **VE**. Instead, since there are [four] vowel letters <note>Medieval writers often categorized the Hebrew letters of the Name as vowels or semi-vowels to explain their spiritual resonance.</note> that are free for all outcomes, the first two are to be pronounced first, the middle two second, and the last two third. In this wondrous way, the sacred letters themselves cohere to each other. If someone asks you what the first two are, you can freely answer: **I** and **E**. If someone asks you what the middle two are, you may freely answer: **E** and **V**. If someone asks you what the last two are, you may freely answer: **V** and **E**. If, therefore, we wish to give these three pronunciations—which seem unable to be formed except by six letters—without multiplying the letters, we find it possible in such a wondrous way that we cannot sever what we can distinguish. For it must be written simply.

The author argues that just as the letters overlap and depend on one another, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct yet consubstantial and inseparable.</summary>

# First Exposition on the Apocalypse by Joachim
## E 4

...with these four letters, IEVE. <note>original: "IEVE." A Latin transliteration of the Hebrew Tetragrammaton, YHWH, the four-letter name of God. In medieval theology, these letters were often used to symbolize the Trinity.</note> And yet it is to be read first as **IE**, **EV**, **VE**, and then as **IEVE**. To show this carefully, the name itself must be written with the formed letters. However, its pronunciations should be marked with very small clauses: for example:

<image-desc>A diagram showing the letters of the Tetragrammaton arranged with connecting lines. The letters 'ie', 'ue', 'eu' are placed above 'IE', 'VE', 'eu' with lines connecting them to a central 'ieue'.</image-desc>

And what is closer to the truth than this mystery? Surely you see the ineffable name written with four letters; surely you see—rather, you see the knot of the whole matter: what a great depth of the sacrament is covered within it. Hence, not without reason, it is written by the Hebrews but not spoken; for if you try to speak with your tongue what is distinguished in the mind, it ceases to be a <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>From the Greek meaning "four letters."</note>; therefore, it is better perceived by the mind than sounded by the service of the tongue. And what is closer to the truth than this mystery? That great teacher, Augustine, contemplated this concerning the Trinity—that God is [great]—when he said:

<margin>Augustine, *On the Trinity*, Book 7, Chapter 4.</margin>

When human poverty was constrained to bring forth in speech to the human senses what it holds in the secret place of the mind concerning the Lord God Almighty, its creator—whether through pious faith or whatever intelligence it might have—he feared to say "three essences," <note>original: "tres essentias"</note> lest any diversity be understood in that supreme equality. On the other hand, he could not say there were not "three somethings," because what Sabellius said—having fallen into heresy—led him to seek what he should call these three. <note>Sabellius was a 3rd-century priest who taught "Modalism," the idea that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are merely three different "masks" or roles of a single person, rather than three distinct Persons.</note> He said "three persons," <note>original: "tres personas"</note> or "three substances" <note>original: "tres substantias"</note> according to the Greeks—not so that it might be [fully] said, but so that he would not remain silent. Surely you have heard what Augustine said. But if it delights you to contemplate that same thing—namely, what is granted to be possible in this ineffable name—in which if you try to utter with your mouth those three things you perceive in the mind, you are proved to fail. For if you say "IE" is one name, you speak the truth. If you say "EV" is one name, you speak the truth. If you say "VE" is one name, you speak the truth. But if you say "IEVE" are three names, you say what God does not say; for He did not say "my names," but "my name." <note>original: "non ait nomina mea: sed nomen meum."</note> It is just as if we were to say in other words: If I say, "God the Father from heaven," or "God the Son, Redeemer of the world," or "God the Holy Spirit," it is a true and pious confession. 

<column-break/>

However, it is not permitted to sum them up so that you say "three gods." Instead, the Holy Trinity is one God. For just as it is permitted to say "IE" is one name, "EV" is one name, and "VE" is one name, yet "IEVE" is not three names but one name; so also our faith does not accept three gods, but one God. Because the true God is the Trinity, and the true God is each of the persons individually. Therefore, although the letters themselves are four in number—and not seven, nor only three, but with one being doubled <note>The letter 'E' appears twice in the four-letter name IEVE.</note>—nevertheless, three distinct pronunciations are contained within that one name. These pronunciations are joined to each other with such unity that they can truly be three, and yet they cannot be separated from one another. 

If, however, we carefully note these pronunciations—not as they are ineffably contained in the written name, but as they can come to human ears—by adding at least two letters in a triangular form, writing in this way: We find in a wondrous manner in the letter **A** what is designated in this name. But if we join the three together in one round form, writing in this way, we find the whole name itself in a wondrous manner in the letter **O**, representing what is contained in this name. Not because we intend to show different things here and there, but because there [in the triangle] we have placed the eye of the mind to understand what pertains to the three persons—that is, so each person is believed to be the true God—and here [in the circle] to recognize that together they are not three gods, but one God. And so, when we say:

<image-desc>A circular diagram containing the letters IEVE in the center, surrounded by the syllables 'ie', 'ue', 'eu' and 'IE', 'VE', 'u' arranged in a triangular or circular pattern with connecting lines.</image-desc>

...we do not make a split in the name; and when we say IE, VE, we do not exclude the Trinity, but there we only distinguish what pertains to the persons; here we hold together what pertains to the unity of the essence. Clearly, this unity could not exist in the persons if the persons themselves were separable from one another and yet indivisible, such that they could be pulled apart. But because one name hangs from the other in such a way that what is in the middle of two is common to both of the two names...

### Part of the Exposition

...that he may have union: it is clear that the Father is in the Son, and the Son is in the Father, and the Holy Spirit is in the Father and the Son. Thus, while each is believed to be the individual, true, and perfect God, the three together are truly believed to be not three gods, but one God. Therefore, the Name itself is one; it is not written once for the Trinity and once for the Unity, as we might do for the sake of understanding. Instead, you who read must understand that both **A** and **O** <note>original: "A. ⁊ .O." Referring to Alpha and Omega, the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet.</note> are contained within it: that is, the Trinity and the Unity. 

It is just as if one were to say this fire, from which a flame arises and heat proceeds, is something other than the flame; or the flame which is born is something other [than the fire]; or the heat which proceeds from them is something else—yet these three together are one fire. Each one, individually and truly and without doubt, is fire. However, when we say these three are one fire, we are not predicated on some "fourth thing" that is the fire, just as when we say the root, the trunk, and the bark are one tree, we do not mean a fourth thing. There are only three parts and nothing else. But because those three are themselves the one, or the one tree and the one wood, we say the three are one and the one is three. 

If this can be shown in any way in physical things which can be separated from one another—so that it is not absurd to call the three "one" and the one "three"—why do you think it is foreign to faith or entirely a stranger to reason when the unity of the Trinity is preached to you? Indeed, the demonstrations found in the images of things are more dissimilar the closer they are to "cruder" elements, and conversely, they are more similar the closer they are to more subtle and eminent things. But because tangible and coarser things are more easily grasped by weak intellects, we speak of them to suggest the power of the word, not to show the absolute truth of the likeness. The Apostle demonstrates that this is necessary when he says:

<margin>1 Corinthians 3</margin>
> As if to infants in Christ, I gave you milk to drink, not solid food.

Therefore, just as one tree is one, so too is that Name: it is not three names, but one Name. And just as in one tree those three parts are bound by unity, so those three pronunciations are in one Name, so much so that the ineffable Name itself can be called both One and Triune. Yet it is not three names, but one Name; just as those three are not three trees or three pieces of wood, but one wood. And just as one tree is not entirely the root, or the trunk, or the bark, but the three are one, so also that venerable Name is one. Nor yet is

<column-break/>

the whole contained in **IE**, or the whole in **EV**, or the whole in **VE**, but the three together are the one Name which is **IEVE**. <note>The author is breaking down the Tetragrammaton into syllables to represent the three persons of the Trinity: Father (IE), Son (EV), and Holy Spirit (VE).</note> Thus the Name itself can be called a "one-three," and it is itself one, written uniformly in its own place. 

These sacred mysteries of the Trinity, which are contained within the "secret of secrets" among the Jews, were revealed by a certain Hebrew named Peter <note>original: "petrus noīe." This refers to Petrus Alphonsi (c. 1062–1110), a Jewish physician and scholar who converted to Christianity and wrote the *Dialogi contra Iudaeos*, which influenced medieval Trinitarian thought.</note>, who was illuminated by the grace of Christ and converted to Him. He acted as a pathfinder and precursor for his people, who are soon to be cured of blindness by the Lord. We, too, wishing to investigate this through the unbelieving Jews, questioned a certain very pious Hebrew concerning the power of this Name. Since we occasionally came to dispute concerning our faith and his, he became familiar to us through constant conversation. Especially because he found in us a clear understanding—something he thought confessors of the indivisible Trinity were ignorant of—he did not deny that the matter was as that converted Hebrew [Peter] had said. This was true even though he himself, as one foreign to the light and still bound by the chains of his old faith, did not know the power of the Name.

Therefore, what the Lord says—"I am **A** and **O**"—is to be understood as if He were saying: "I am Three and One." And what He immediately adds—"The Beginning and the End"—is as if He were following with other words, saying: "I am He who teaches from the beginning that I am Three; I am He who demonstrates in the end that I am One." Indeed, the "Three" is demonstrated in the **A**, and the "One" in the **O**. For just as the three corners <note>original: "cornua." Literally 'horns' or 'points,' referring to the shape of the capital letter A.</note> of that figure proclaim the Trinity, so the roundness of the other proclaims the Unity. This is so that no one, when they hear "Three," thinks it is a composite thing, but rather the highest "One"—or if it may be said, the "Most-One."

Furthermore, because that ineffable Name sounds like a plural name—*Adonay*, which is interpreted as "Lords" <note>original: "domini." While 'Adonai' is often translated as 'Lord,' its Hebrew suffix is grammatically plural, which medieval Christians interpreted as a hint of the Trinity.</note>—what do we say? Why does He not say "our name," but "my name," except because the Name of God is such that it demonstrates both plurality and unity? By the fact that He does not say "names" but "name," and not "ours" but "mine," He shows Himself to be one God. And by the fact that He does not say "my name which is Lord (singular)," but "which is Lords (plural)," He manifesty demonstrates Himself to be three in persons. Therefore, from the teaching of this sacred Name, it clearly appears...

<margin>Note concerning the secret sayings.</margin>

...is the only-begotten Son of God, consubstantial <term>consubstantial: having the same substance or essence</term> with the Father; the Holy Spirit is consubstantial with that same Son, who is consubstantial with the Father. Although within the name itself <note>original: "in nomine ipso" - referring to the Divine Name IEVE mentioned on the previous page</note> there lies hidden a depth of mystery beyond even this, it is clearly given to be understood that the Holy Spirit is consubstantial with the Father and the Son, inasmuch as he proceeds not from the Father alone, nor from the Son alone, but from both.

<margin>1 Corinthians 3</margin>
¶ It is evident that there are three letters with which the sacred name itself is written, but one of them is doubled. For **I** is written there once, and **V** is written once. But **E** is inscribed twice: that is, it is written after the **I** and after the **V**. I say that **E** is written after **I** and after **V** according to the fact that one Elijah was sent after Moses (with whom he was seen on the mountain) and is to be sent after John—who is described as having once come in Elijah's spirit. Indeed, the one Elijah seems to be joined in the mysteries of both Moses and John; for this reason, he had to be sent on two occasions: first under the Old Testament, and then under the New, as if to perform a work under both and to cooperate with both Moses and John. This is a great mystery, and closely resembles that venerable name. For there is one God the Father, whom Moses designates in this mystery; there is one Son of God, whom John designates; and there is one Holy Spirit, whom Elijah designates. Therefore, because there is one Spirit of God who proceeds from the Father and the Son, and who cooperates with both Father and Son, it was necessary for Elijah to be sent twice to cooperate with each of the two individually. For the same Spirit is the power of the Father and the Son, the gift of both, and the love of both. Hence the letter itself which is called **O** <note>The Greek letter Omega, the last letter of the alphabet</note> is written in two ways among the Greeks, to demonstrate a double significance here. In the form where it is written simply, just as it is among us <note>the round O</note>, it has the meaning we wrote above; but in the form where it is written in this manner:

<margin>Malachi [the last chapter]</margin>

<image-desc>A small rectangular diagram containing the Greek letter Omega (ω) inside a box.</image-desc>

...it is recognized to be written according to what we hold in our faith to designate something else: namely, that there are two persons, of whom one is the Father and the other is the Son, and one power belongs to both, which is neither the "begetter" nor the "begotten," but only the one Spirit proceeding from both. For so there are two Testaments <note>The Old and New Testaments of the Bible</note> which are designated in this character **ω**, cohering to one another through all things, so that one seems to be born from the other, and the begotten is like the one who begets him, and one spiritual understanding proceeds from both. This is why the character itself is open at the upper part: so that the one "breathing" <term>spiratio: the theological term for the 'breathing out' of the Holy Spirit from the Father and Son</term> of both may be shown to have a connection to each. And because this is shown to be signified in the **A** <note>Alpha</note> as in the **IE. VE.** <note>The Divine Name</note>, it is so that these three persons may be believed to be co-eternal and co-equal with one another. It could not be shown through a single letter alone what must be believed about them: namely, that there are two of whom one is the Begetter and the other the Begotten, and one who is neither Begetter nor Begotten, but only proceeding from both. Saying, "I am the **A**," he immediately added: "I am the **O**." And since many things were written in the first age which demonstrate the Trinity—such as "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob," or "May God, our God, bless us; may God bless us," or "Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God Almighty"—it could not be understood or known through those same oracles whether one of them was the Begetter, one the Begotten, and one proceeding from both, according to how it has been explained to us by the Son at the end of the ages. Rightly, where he says "I am the **A** and **O**," he immediately added "the Beginning and the End"; because he who spoke obscurely for us in the first age (so that we might have in him the beginning of our salvation) has deigned to speak plainly to us in this final age, so that our labor may reach its end and we may recognize him in truth. As Truth itself says: "In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you." And again: "I have spoken these things to you in proverbs; the hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in proverbs, but will tell you plainly about the Father." In this matter there is something else to be considered watchfully: that when we assign the Trinity simply to the letter **A**, and Unity to the round **O**, then those two elements must be gathered together into one, so that the triangular figure <note>the shape of the capital Alpha</note> may teach that there are three persons, each of whom is God—which is to say:

<column-break/>

<margin>John 14</margin>

<meta>This page continues the symbolic and theological analysis of the Divine Name "IEVE." Having previously discussed the letters as representative of historical figures like Moses and Elijah, the author now shifts to the geometric and trinitarian implications of these letters, specifically how they map onto the "Three Statuses" or ages of sacred history—a hallmark of Joachite theology.</meta>

### Exposition Part

IE.EV.VE. And let the round figure indicate that the three persons are one God; which is to say: IE.VE. For there are three angles within it, as well as the roundness itself: these are, if I may put it this way, symbolic tokens <note>original: "voces males" - likely meaning 'signifying marks' or 'vocal tokens'</note> by which the omnipotent God, who is "He who is," is demonstrated to be both three and one. Therefore, just as the unity of the Trinity is noted in that triangular figure, so the pure simplicity of unity is noted in the round figure. Furthermore, if we are dealing with that **.ω.** <note>The Greek letter Omega, often used in the Middle Ages to symbolize the end of time or the Holy Spirit</note> which is found written in the Book of Revelation, we must firmly hold to what we said earlier: namely, that in the letter **.A.** [Alpha] it signifies that there are two proceeding from one; but in **.ω.** [Omega] there is one who proceeds from two. One might say there are not three testaments, but two: namely, the "letter" of the Law of <term>Moysi: Moses, representing the Old Testament</term> and the "letter" of the Gospel of <term>Christi: Christ, representing the New Testament</term>. From these two, one spiritual understanding emerges in a symbolic form: this is undoubtedly the one Spirit who proceeds from the Father and the Son. According to this, two times and two peoples are recognized: the time of the Father and the time of the Son; the Jewish people and the Gentile people. From these two, there emerges the one Church of spiritual men. Because the Spirit himself is God—equal and co-eternal with the Father and the Son, from whom he proceeds from eternity—lest anyone think he is not God, but merely one of the seven virtues (such as the spirit of wisdom or the spirit of knowledge and the like), he could not deny himself, since he is the Truth just as the Son is. However, he reserved for himself his own proper time in which he himself would work: not merely as one of the virtues of God (which are called the gifts of the Holy Spirit), but as true God and true Lord, just as the Father and the Son are. For that reason, because God the Father was clearly seen to work in the first five ages of the world, and the Son in the sixth, it is necessary that the Spirit himself work in the seventh. Thus, just as God is a Trinity, the works of the three periods appear distinct by certain boundaries and properties, corresponding to the specific persons of the Godhead through the nature of the mystery. These are those three periods which, because of the truth of their specific gifts, we believe should be called the "three states of the world" <note>This refers to the "Three Statuses," a famous theory by Joachim of Fiore where history is divided into the Age of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit</note>; for indeed, between these three, there is no small difference. In the first of these three, the church of the laypeople flourished; in the second, the church of the clergy; in the third, the church of the monks will flourish. For it is necessary for the elect of God, when the storm of persecution is imminent, to flee from city to city: that is, from the first to the second, and from the second to the third. For the Lord commanded this, saying:

<column-break/>

<margin>Matthew 10</margin>
"If they persecute you in one city, flee to another; and if they persecute you in that one, flee to a third." <note>A creative allegorical reading of Matthew 10:23</note> This is to say: If, because of overflowing malice, it is no longer safe for you to take wives and remain among the laypeople (when the time comes for those who are pregnant or nursing), flee to the church of the clergy; and if it is not safe there because iniquity prevails, flee to the church of the monks. And again: if they persecute you in the "letter" of the Old Testament, run back to the "letter" of the New Testament; and if they persecute you in that, you must run back to the spiritual understanding. Just as the sum of all generations of the world is to be distinguished into two or three periods in the two ways mentioned above, so in that sacred Name [IEVE], there are two principal definitions to be noted. One seems to regard the works of the "three states" according to the properties of the Persons: which is expressed as IE.EV.VE. The other signifies the mystery of the two Testaments to show that there are two—of which one is the Begetter and the other the Begotten—and one who is neither Father nor Son, but the single communion of both, shown to cooperate with both: which is expressed as IE.VE. Indeed, the letter **I** is seen to belong to the Father, **E** to the Holy Spirit, **V** to the Son, and **E** again to the Holy Spirit. This is not because there are two Spirits, but because he is given twice, to show that he proceeds from both the Father and the Son, just as he proceeds from the Father and the Son together. Hence it is that in the three states, three similar works are to be carried out in the three orders of those to be saved, so that through this the three Persons themselves may be understood to be equal. From the two Testaments (one of which arose from the other) one spiritual understanding proceeds: that is, one meaning signified by two signifiers. By this, one Person is understood to be unbegotten [the Father], another from the unbegotten [the Son], and another proceeding from both. I do not see fit to skip over the following (now that the opportunity is given), which I wished to discuss regarding the three states up to this point: that which cannot be fully grasped by itself as it truly is, may be more easily discussed and understood when considered by comparison with other things. And regarding what we have said in certain places in our small works concerning these matters: whatever was to be contemplated more deeply and subtly, we have left for its own proper time, lest perhaps the untrained capacity of some might be offended or shrink back from a burden they were not yet able to carry.

### First Book of Joachim on the Apocalypse

<margin>1 Corinthians 3</margin> For we have said that the beginning of the first age <note>Joachim uses the term "status" to describe three great overlapping epochs of world history: the Age of the Father (Old Testament), the Age of the Son (New Testament), and the coming Age of the Holy Spirit.</note> is from **Abraham**; the beginning of the second from the **advent of the Lord**; and the beginning of the third from the **conversion of Israel**. Let the reader understand that in saying this, we have imitated him <note>St. Paul</note> who spoke to the "little ones" in Christ, saying: *As if to little ones in Christ, I gave you milk to drink, not solid food* <note>original: "Tanq̄ paruulis in xp̄o lac potū dedi vobis nō escā," quoting 1 Corinthians 3:1-2.</note>. But now, having found the opportunity with those whose intellects are trained by habit, let us be carried toward perfection. Let us place, if you please, two circles before the eyes of the mind joined at their summits, and another in the middle between the two, so that there are only three circles. But why is it that this name of the Lord <term>Tetragrammaton: The four-letter name of God, YHWH, often rendered as IEVE in medieval Latin</term> of which we treat is said to have only three letters, yet four distinctions? It is because one letter is doubled; for this reason the name of the Lord itself is called the *Tetragrammaton*. Indeed, if we do this, we find "three in one" and "one in three" in such a way that, when the unity is considered from every side, every mouth of those speaking iniquity may be stopped. For there is no lack of those who think evil in their hearts, imagining that we divide the Unity because we preach the Trinity in the mysteries. But the Truth is able to heal their hearts, provided they can believe that God made the human race in His own image and likeness. However, so that every occasion for making excuses might be removed—which often arises from the differing opinions of various men—we shall show that very thing which we say must be contemplated with the eyes of the mind through visible figures on the page below; especially since the name of God, the *Tetragrammaton*, demands this, as it can be shown through figures better than it can be expressed by the tongue.

<column-break/>

->Example of the aforementioned matter.<-

<margin>Sabellius and Arius</margin> Look at the present figure: it has three properties, which no one can deny. And yet, if one is able, let him try to divide one of these circles from the others, which so wonderfully fit the ineffable Name. If he finds he cannot do it at all, let him learn to carefully avoid **Sabellius** <note>A 3rd-century heretic who taught that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit were not distinct persons but just different "modes" of one person.</note> without falling into the wickedness of **Arius** <note>A 4th-century heretic who taught that the Son was a created being, lesser than and separate from the Father.</note>. The first of these seemed to hold to the image of only one circle; the other indeed held to three, but three that were unequal and divided by a variety of nature. Therefore, although the boundary of the first age was truly at the advent of the Lord, the boundary of the second is in these present times, and the boundary of the third is at the end of the world, they cannot be divided from one another. This is because the beginnings are not where the ends are, as is clearly gathered from the present figure. And even if, due to the unusual weight of the discourse, we say the beginning of the first age was in **Abraham**, the beginning of the second in **John the Baptist**, and the beginning of the third in a predefined time—not that in those same moments they were equally...

### Part of the Exposition by the Abbot

->IE. EV. VE.<- <note>These letters represent a medieval Latin phonetic spelling of the Hebrew Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God.</note> And let the round figure indicate that the three persons are one God; which is to say: IE. VE. For there are three angles themselves and a roundness: which, if I may put it this way, are like masculine voices by which the Almighty God, who is what He is, is shown to be both three and one. Therefore, just as in that triangular figure, the unity of the Trinity is noted in God; so in the round figure, the pure simplicity of the unity is noted in that same God. Furthermore, if we discuss that **$\omega$** <note>The Greek letter Omega, the "End"</note> which is found written in that place in the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, that which we said above must be held without hesitation: namely, that in the **A.** <note>The Greek letter Alpha, the "Beginning"</note> it signifies that there are two who proceed from one; in the **$\omega$**, it signifies that there is one who proceeds from two. Wherefore the Testaments are said to be not three, but two. Namely, the letter of the Law and of **Moses**; and the letter of the **Gospel of Christ**. From these, one spiritual understanding emerges in a symbolic form: or, without doubt, the one Spirit who proceeds from the Father and the Son. And according to this, two times and two peoples are known: namely, the time of the fathers and the time of the sons, the Jewish people and the Gentile people; from which one Church of spiritual men proceeds. For the Spirit himself is God: equal and co-eternal with the Father and the Son, from whom he proceeds from eternity; lest anyone think he is not God, but as if he were one of the seven virtues, such as the Spirit of Wisdom or the Spirit of Knowledge; and as their daughter, he could not deny himself, since he himself—just like the Son—is the Truth; but he reserved for himself his own proper time, in which he also works, not as one of the virtues of God, which are called the "gifts of the Holy Spirit," but as true God and true Lord, just like the Father and the Son. For this reason, because in the first five ages, God the Father was clearly seen to work; in the sixth, the Son; it is necessary that he himself <note>the Holy Spirit</note> work in the seventh: so that just as God is a Trinity, so the works of the three times may be seen to be distinct by their certain boundaries and properties, according to the persons of the Godhead, fitting the property of the mystery. These are those three times which, on account of the truth of their own gifts, we believe should be named the **Three Statuses** of the world: for truly, between these three, there is no small difference. For in the first of these three, the **Church of the Laity** flourished; in the second, the **Church of the Clergy**; in the third, the **Church of the Monks** will flourish. For it is necessary for the elect of God, when the storm of persecution is pressing, to flee from city to city: namely, from the first into the second; from the second into the third. For so the Lord commanded, saying:

<column-break/>

<margin>Matthew 10</margin>
"If they persecute you in one city, flee into another; and if they persecute you in that one, flee into the third." <note>original: "Si vos psequuti fuerint in vnā ciuitatē: fugite in aliā: & si in illa psequuti vos fuerint fugite in tertiā." A variation of Matthew 10:23.</note> Which is to say: If, because of overflowing malice, it will not be safe for you to take wives and remain among the laity—"woe to those who are pregnant and nursing!"—flee to the **Church of the Clergy**; and if it will not be safe there, because iniquity prevails, flee to the **Church of the Monks**. And again: If they persecute you in the letter of the **Old Testament**, run back to the letter of the **New Testament**; and if they persecute you in that, you must run back to **Spiritual Understanding**. Just as the totality of the generations of the world is to be distinguished into two or three times by the two aforementioned ways: so in that holy Name, there are two principal definitions to be noted: one which may be seen to look toward the works of the **Three Statuses** through the properties of the Persons; which is to say: IE. EV. VE. The other which may signify the mystery of the two Testaments to show that they are two: of which one is the Begetter, the other the Begotten; and of the one who is not Father or Son, but the one communion of both, so that he is shown to cooperate with both; which is to say: IE. VE. For **I.** is seen to pertain to the Father; **E.** to the Holy Spirit; **V.** to the Son; **E.** again to the Holy Spirit: not that there are two Spirits, but because he is given twice, so that he may be shown to proceed from the Father and from the Son, just as he proceeds from the Father and the Son. Hence it is that in the three statuses, three similar works must be brought forth in the three orders of those to be saved: so that through this, those three Persons themselves may be understood to be equal; whence, because there are two Testaments, of which one has its origin from the other, one spiritual understanding proceeds: that is, from two things signifying, one thing signified; so that through this, one Person may be understood to be unbegotten, another from the unbegotten, and another proceeding from the begotten <note>i.e., the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Son</note>. Furthermore (since the opportunity has been given), I do not see that it should be passed over, that I have wished to discuss the **Three Statuses** up to the present point, so that that which cannot be fully comprehended through itself—as it is—might be more easily discussed and understood by comparing it with other things. And indeed, when we were dealing with these things in certain places of our small works, we spoke according to whatever understanding was possible: that which was to be contemplated more deeply and subtly in its own time; lest, perhaps, the untrained capacity of someone might be offended and shrink back before it could bear it.

# John’s First Part on the Apocalypse

<margin>1 Corinthians 3</margin> We have said that the beginning of the <term>first status<note>Joachim’s theory of history is divided into three "statuses" or ages: the Age of the Father (Old Testament), the Age of the Son (New Testament/Church), and the coming Age of the Holy Spirit.</note></term> is from **Abraham**; the beginning of the second is from the advent of the Lord; and the beginning of the third is from the conversion of **Israel**. And let the reader understand that in saying this, we are imitating him who spoke to the little ones in Christ, saying: <note>original: "Tanq̃ paruulis in xpō lac potū dedi vobis nō escā"</note> *“As if to infants in Christ, I gave you milk to drink, not solid food.”* Now, however, having found an opportunity with those who have their intellects trained by habit, let us be carried toward perfection. Let us place, if you please, two circles before the eyes of the mind, joined at their summits, and another in the middle between the two, so that there are only three circles. This is just like that name of the Lord which we are discussing: we said it has only three letters but four distinctions, because one letter is doubled, which is why the name of the Lord is called the <term>Tetragrammaton<note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH. Joachim interprets the Latin spelling IEUE as having three distinct letters (I, E, U) with the 'E' repeated.</note></term>. For if we do this, we shall find three in one and one in three in such a way that, once the truth is considered from every side, every mouth of those speaking iniquity may be shut. For there are those who might think evil in their hearts, judging that we are "splitting the unity" because we preach the Trinity in the mysteries. But the truth is able to heal their hearts, provided they can believe that God made the human race in his own image and likeness. However, so that all occasion for contention—which often arises from a diversity of opinions—may be removed, that which we say must be contemplated with the eyes of the mind, we shall also show in visible figures on the page below; especially since the name of God, the Tetragrammaton, demands this, as it can be shown through figures better than it can be expressed by the tongue.

Thus it happens that a "beginning" can be said to exist in both, and both can be commonly understood under one heading. 

Now, when we take the beginning of the <term>first status<note>Joachim's "Three Statuses" or Ages: the Age of the Father (Old Testament), the Age of the Son (New Testament/Church), and the coming Age of the Holy Spirit.</note></term> from **Abraham**—who was first called "exalted father" <note>original: "pater excelsus"</note> and then "father of many nations"—then the first letter, which is **A**, regards that time which passed under those great Patriarchs: namely, **Abraham**, **Isaac**, and **Jacob**, up until **Malachi** the Prophet. Therefore, let no one think it is not permitted to speak this way concerning the three "statuses" pertaining individually to the three Persons <note>The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit</note>, though not as strictly as demonstrated in the figure written above. But we must not overlook what was said earlier regarding **Moses** and **Elijah**, since the arrival of both men clearly demonstrates the truth. For it is clear that in the first of these times, under which the Law was given, **Moses** was sent; to him, the letter **A** is rightfully ascribed in the mysteries. In the time of the prophets, which began (according to another reckoning) with **Samuel**, **Elijah** was sent, to whom **E** is ascribed. In the third time, **John [the Baptist]** was sent, to whom **U** is ascribed <margin>Exodus 3. 4 Kings 17</margin>. In the fourth time, **Elijah** will be sent again, to whom (as we have already said) **E** is ascribed. 

And these are indeed the two Testaments in which the **Father** and **Son** work, and the one **Holy Spirit** cooperates with both. For the Son is not born from the Father first, with the Holy Spirit proceeding from him only later; rather, both are always together. But neither is the Son to be called the "beginning" of the Spirit according to the fact that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father, but only according to the fact that He proceeds from the Son. Therefore, to show that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, He willed there to be only two Testaments—symbolized by the two wives of **Abraham** and the two **Cherubim**. 

And to show that He is the true and full God, just like the Father and the Son, it was nonetheless necessary for there to be three works designated in **Abraham**, **Isaac**, and **Jacob**, declared potentially in the three "statuses" of the world, so that what is less understood from one mystery may be grasped from another. Concerning these things, enough has been said for this place. For we must say less about some things in certain places, especially where it is not the main topic, lest by keeping silent about everything we fail to say what absolutely must be said. For we have not yet entered into those things which we seem to have begun to approach. Thus far has been the greeting and the introduction. # First [Part] on John in the Apocalypse

...and of monks: that is, those who carry the care of the Lord’s flocks, and those who depart from the world so they can be free for God alone. They rest in solitary places—sometimes alone, and sometimes in communities. For the former <note>The "active" clergy</note>, it is their duty to take up their cross and walk after Christ; for the latter <note>The "contemplative" monks</note>, in chastity and purity, to taste how sweet the Lord is—though at certain times and for certain causes, both [paths] are required of both groups. And indeed the holy martyrs, fighting vigorously alongside the blessed Peter, have earned the merit of receiving the crown of unfading glory. But by the great gift of His love, Christ grants the sons of the contemplative life [the vision of] hidden and profound mysteries. 

Therefore, so that those who hide themselves from human sight—as if in the vastness of some island—to adhere more closely to their King, might not be thought inferior to the holy martyrs or less useful to God, John testifies that he is a brother to those who suffer for the Lord, and a sharer in their tribulation and kingdom. For he is a companion in tribulations, the kingdom, and patience in our Lord Jesus Christ, who bore the passion for us all. Whoever, for love of Him, flees the allurements of the world, desiring the harshness of the mountains and the squalor of the desert—like those who left Egypt and entered the desert land, in a place of horror and vast solitude.
<margin>Deuteronomy 32</margin>
For he who is a partner in the fight will (of necessity) also be a partner in the crown. And he who is a companion in war must also be a companion in the feast. "I was," he says, "on the island called Patmos, because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus." Not only the holy martyrs, who desert the transitory and deceptive life of the world for the sake of Christ, bear testimony; but also those who live so that they no longer live for themselves, but for Christ, bearing the cross of Christ in their own bodies. They too, I say, bear testimony to Christ; for because of the word of Christ, they die in such a manner to the body. For who would be so foolish and insane as to want to forgo the pleasures of this life and willingly condemn themselves to so many miseries, unless they were certain of their faith and that the reward for those who confess the Lord is exceedingly great? Whence, not inappropriately,
<margin>John</margin>

Patmos is said to be interpreted as a "strait" <note>original: "fretum"; Joachim uses the etymology of the word to suggest a narrow, difficult passage of water</note>, because those who are about to fight navigate as if in a certain strait of temptations—those who commit themselves to a religious and very narrow life against the vices of the flesh and spirit, as if they were to die on that very day. It follows:
<margin>Text 13</margin>
**I was in the spirit on the Lord’s day.**

This passage is of great weight and contains deep <term>sacraments<note>In this context, "sacraments" refers to sacred mysteries or hidden meanings within the text.</note></term>; the speech is simple, but the mystery is not; the bark <note>Joachim uses "cortex" (bark/shell) to describe the literal surface of the scripture</note> is evident, but the marrow is hidden. Perhaps for some it was already light and easy to understand; but when I first stumbled upon this place, as if falling into a <unclear>pit</unclear> <note>original: "bytalapsum"; likely a corruption of a term for an abyss or pitfall</note>, I was stuck. For God is accustomed to making clear to one person what seems obscure to another, so that each may learn not to be proud but to agree with the humble. 

Indeed, when I reached this place after going through the preceding chapters of this book, I confess I suffered such difficulty and a narrowing of the intellect—more than usual—that I felt as if a stone had been placed against me at the mouth of the tomb. Dazed, I stopped; and giving honor to God, who closes and opens according to His will, I left the place untouched and passed on to the following sections, reserving that same difficulty for the Universal Teacher <note>Referring to the Holy Spirit or Christ</note>, so that He who opened the book and loosened its seven seals might open it to me or to others when it pleased Him. And while I was occupied with many things and this very matter was being led far away by forgetfulness, it happened as the cycle of the year turned that Easter day arrived. Having been woken from sleep around the morning hour, a certain meditation on this book occurred to me, for which, trusting in God's gift, I became bolder in writing—or rather, more fearful of being silent and not writing, lest at any time the Judge should say to me: "You wicked and lazy servant, you knew
<margin>Matthew 25</margin>
that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter. Therefore, you ought to have committed my money to the money-changers, and upon my return, I would have received it..."

### Abbot: Part of the Exposition

...what is mine, with interest <note>original: "cum usura"</note>. For while I already understood some things, and yet was ignorant of even greater mysteries [sacramenta], a kind of battle was waged in my mind: some things seemed to urge me toward a daring attempt, while others threatened me with the difficulty of the task. Therefore, when something similar had occurred on the night mentioned above: around the middle of the night (as I recall), in the silence and at the hour when our Lion from the tribe of Judah <note>A title for Jesus Christ, referring to His victory over death</note> is believed to have risen from the dead; suddenly, as I was meditating on something, a clarity of understanding was perceived by the eyes of my mind regarding the fullness of this book and the total harmony <note>original: "concordia"</note> of the Old and New Testaments. A revelation was made to me, and yet even then I did not immediately remember the verse written above. Why did he say everyone was "one in the spirit on the Lord’s day"? And did it matter to the subject that this very revelation of this book is narrated as having been made on the Lord’s day? This thought did not occur to my mind: nor did I realize that Christ, emerging from the tomb, signified that the Spirit would proceed from the Letter <note>The "Letter" refers to the literal text of the Bible, while the "Spirit" refers to its deeper, hidden meaning</note>. Nor did I see how the seven days of the Easter week, along with the eighth day following it, coincided in their mysteries with the parts of this book; nor that on that same day He opened the senses of the disciples so that they might understand the Scriptures. When, therefore, after a little time had passed and an opportunity was taken, I had re-read the small portion I had noted down, I came to this place in which it is said: <margin>Luke 24</margin> "I was in the spirit on the Lord’s day." And then, for the first time, I understood what it meant in the mystery, to which John says: "I was in the spirit on the Lord’s day," comparing with myself either those very things which had happened, or those things which are known to be written concerning that day; and how from that point the Spirit, awakened from the Letter, began to act, and many things similar to this, which would be too long to touch upon in this place. <margin>Psalm 117</margin> This is therefore the day which the Lord has made; let us exult and be glad in it. <margin>John 20</margin> This is the day in which Christ rose from the dead, after that great stone was removed <margin>Luke 24</margin> from the mouth of the tomb. This is the day in which He opened the senses of His disciples so they might understand the Scriptures. Truly, the eight days in which the Easter festival is so solemnly celebrated by the entire Church of Christians coincide in significance with the eight parts of this book; no less do the eight weeks which lead up to the Sabbath following

<column-break/>

Pentecost <note>A feast 50 days after Easter celebrating the descent of the Holy Spirit</note>, which are assigned to joy and gladness out of reverence for such great solemnities. Nevertheless, as we have written elsewhere, this book has two typical understandings: one which pertains to the second state <note>The Age of the Son/The New Testament Church</note>, and another which pertains to the third state <note>The Age of the Holy Spirit, which Joachim predicted would be a time of monastic peace and spiritual perfection</note>. In this matter, it is pleasing to look more diligently: for we who are positioned at the beginning of the third state have more need of that revelation which uncovers things to come, than of that revelation which was made to spiritual men from the time of the Apostles—even if that earlier revelation now comes more fully into the light, as it begins to be opened according to the course of time. It is for this reason that on the sixth day <note>Friday, the day of the Crucifixion</note> which precedes the Easter day itself, the rocks were split and the tombs were opened; likewise the veil of the temple was torn from the top to the bottom. <margin>Matthew 27</margin> For because that day which precedes the Lord’s Day (with the Sabbath coming between them) is seen to refer to old things by the very fact that it is the sixth day, so the following day, the Lord's Day, pertains to new things by the very fact that it is the Lord's. What does it mean that on the sixth day the rocks were split and the tombs opened, or that the veil of the temple was torn from top to bottom? <margin>Matthew 27</margin> And what does it mean that on the first day, which is called the Lord’s Day, that greatest tomb was opened, except that the time in which all these things were done was both an end as far as old things are concerned, and a beginning of subsequent ages as far as new things are concerned? Thus, these three days should be accepted as one, as it is said of them in the Easter Preface: "It is truly right to praise You at all times, but on this day most gloriously, when Christ our Passover was sacrificed." <note>A standard prayer from the Catholic Mass</note> Nevertheless, that which was done on the sixth day precedes in significance. That which was done on the day of Easter follows; and although some think the tombs were opened on the very day of Easter after Christ rose from the dead—who for this reason want Him to be called by the Apostle the "firstborn of the dead" <margin>Colossians 1</margin>—if this is so, why did the Evangelist not say this where the resurrection itself is discussed, but rather where it is said: "But Jesus, crying out again with a loud voice, gave up His spirit"? Or perhaps it must be confessed that they were indeed opened then and, as it were, prepared for the third day, so that by their very opening they might designate something? What if...

### Joachim on the Apocalypse
->Page 40<-

...the bodies were raised, according to that passage of Ezekiel: "and they were brought into one place: and after the Lord’s resurrection, were they awakened from the dead?" <note>Referring to the bodies of the saints rising in Matthew 27:52 and the vision of dry bones in Ezekiel 37</note> For God could have done this if He wished, He who does all things whatever He wills in heaven and on earth. And this "opening" seems to pertain to the scriptures of the Old Testament; but the opening of the Lord’s tomb, which was new and cut from rock, pertains to the scripture of the New Testament, which was established at that time and soon opened. This is especially true since it is written in this place that the veil of the temple was torn from top to bottom. Where these two things are placed together—namely the temple and the Lord’s tomb—the temple designates the Old Testament, while the tomb designates the New. In another sense, however, one can be taken for the other. Therefore, on that day when the temple veil was torn from top to bottom and the tombs were opened, the righteous closed Christ—whom the wicked had killed—within the tomb. Although the wicked also wanted this very thing, they did so with a different, depraved intention. This signifies surely those things which are carried out in the Spirit. For even the holy evangelists buried the truth which is in the Spirit under the Letter <note>The "Letter" refers to the literal, historical surface of the biblical text</note>, hiding it from the gaze of the wicked; and the Jews until now have hidden and still hide the same truth under that same Letter, lest their eyes ever be opened and they see the true light which illuminates every man coming into this world, and lest the spiritual understanding—which they hate—be awakened from the burial mound of history. Therefore, at that time, the New Testament was established when the ancient scriptures began to be opened. Yet even this [the New Testament] began to be opened not long after, and its inner contents were made clear to believers; for a mystical understanding has been within it from the very same time the events took place. First, it was perceived by the holy apostles, to whom the first fruits of the Spirit were given, and after them by many others taught by the same Spirit. But what if the New Testament was opened quickly? Did Christ, who lay hidden within it, appear manifest as soon as He ascended from the tomb? Was not His manifest appearance delayed until the evening? What is "until the evening" if not until the "sixth time"? <note>Joachim often divides history into six or seven periods; "evening" represents the transition between these eras</note> Therefore, if these two openings are

<margin>John 1</margin>
<margin>John 20</margin>

treated together, it is clear that the sixth Friday <note>Good Friday</note>—according to what the Church observes annually during the forty days of Lent—is the end; but the day of Easter is the beginning of the paschal feasts. Now, in the first understanding, this signifies that the opening of the Old Testament was delayed until the time of Christ. But the opening of the New Testament was not so; rather, it was made known to spiritual men from that very same time. Nevertheless, even if the opening occurred, the revelation of the Risen One remained hidden for a long time, delayed as if until the evening, by which the end of a certain period is designated. And this is according to that understanding which pertains to the Second State <note>The "Second State" is the age of the New Testament and the Church</note>. Furthermore, if we are dealing with that understanding which pertains to the Third State <note>The "Third State" is Joachim's predicted future age of the Holy Spirit and monastic contemplation</note>, we ought to search and weigh it carefully: just as in the aforementioned understanding the day of the Lord’s resurrection signifies the beginning of the Second State, so in the understanding pertaining to the Third State, it signifies the beginning of the third, which will be after the end, or rather at the end, of the second. However, the fact that Christ was revealed not in the morning of that day, but in the evening, signifies that at the end of the Second State, that understanding which pertains to the same Second State must be revealed; but at the end of the third, the understanding that pertains to the third. Therefore, according to this reasoning: the understanding pertaining to the First State was revealed when Christ came into the world; the understanding pertaining to the second is revealed around the end of the Second State; and the understanding pertaining to the third around the end of that state. Furthermore, the opening of the tomb was made for the teachers of the Second State from the very beginning of that state; and it must be done for the teachers of the Third State from the beginning of the third. Nor should it be thought that the opening of the tomb and the revelation of the Lord are to be taken as the same thing; for the opening of the tomb occurred in the morning and was shown to the disciples, but the manifest revelation of Christ was delayed until the evening. Finally, the tomb is opened or the veil is torn, yet the Lord who rises is not yet shown; this occurs when a disciple of truth understands that the surface of the Letter is empty and that a spiritual and life-giving understanding proceeds from it, yet he has not yet reached the point of perceiving the Truth itself as it is in spiritual understanding. For He is revealed to someone by Himself...

### Abbot: Part of the Exposition

...Christ Jesus: when not only what is understood as the emptiness of the Letter <note>The "Letter" refers to the literal or historical meaning of the Bible, which Joachim often contrasts with the "Spirit" or deeper meaning.</note> is seen, but even the spiritual understanding itself—viewed not as it superficially appears, but beheld with the lights of the heart. And because the same Lord appeared on the morning of that day to Mary Magdalene and to the others whom he wished, whether this refers to the beginning of the Second State <note>The Second State is the age of the New Testament/the Son; the Third State is the coming age of the Holy Spirit.</note> or the beginning of the Third, what John says—"I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day"—can be understood clearly and uniformly. It means that then there were some "in the Spirit" who understood the scripture of the Old Testament spiritually, and now in a similar way there will be some in the Spirit who understand the Letter of the New Testament according to this deeper understanding. It follows:

<margin>Chapter 1:14</margin>
**And I heard behind me a loud voice, like a trumpet, saying: What you see, write in a book, and send it to the seven churches which are in Asia.**

One might ask why Saint John claimed to have heard the voice behind him, were the reason not clear and evident. For while we read those things in the sacred page that were performed in times past, and through them something spiritual begins to shine within our intellect, we hear a spiritual voice as if "behind our backs." Moreover, there is one voice that is small, and another that is loud. The small voice is that which deals with earthly things; the loud voice is that which speaks of heavenly things. Therefore, this voice which John heard is loud, like a trumpet, because it does not deal with earthly and transitory things, but rather with heavenly and enduring ones.

<margin>Mystery of the trumpet</margin>
<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a long, straight trumpet (tuba) with a flared bell, showing decorative bands and a mouthpiece.</image-desc>

For the shape of this instrument, which is so celebrated and frequent in the divine page, represents the mystery of the whole holy church of God. It is a hammered instrument, long and resonant, beginning indeed from a narrow point, but drawn out into a wide flare. And indeed its length is thin, its opening wide; the whole thing is hollow and shaped for sounding together.

<column-break/>

It bears the type <note>A "type" is a person or object in the Bible that foreshadows a future reality.</note> of the preachers of the church—not only of those who are reborn in Christ, but also of those who have been His prophets from the beginning of the world. This preaching was indeed narrow in number and hidden in voice at the start, until the times of the prophets. From then on it began to be broader and more manifest: that is, from the days of Hosea and Isaiah until John the Baptist. There, finally, it was widened and fulfilled in the apostolic choir, where their sound was made in the manner of a great trumpet. Because the fullness of time had arrived, the hidden voice came "upon the roof," and that which was narrowed within a small people was poured out into the breadth of the nations, fulfilling in them that verse which the Psalmist had predicted long before concerning the teachers of truth: *Their sound went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.* <note>original: "In omnem terram exiuit sonus eorum & in fines orbis terre verba eorum." - Psalm 19:4 (18:5 in the Vulgate)</note> Truly, that distinction which we noted from the days of the prophets is designated by that "node" <note>A decorative or structural joint on a medieval trumpet.</note> of the trumpet, from which the trumpet begins to widen and grow large. For just as the trumpet is made larger from the node, so from the days of Uzziah <note>King Ozias/Uzziah, whose reign saw the start of the written prophetic books like Isaiah.</note>—where a certain "node" of insertion was made for the initiation of a New Testament—Christ’s heralds began to multiply and their voice reached the ears of the people more fully. Such, then, was the voice John heard: not a small one that should be hidden among a few, but a loud, public, and manifest one, which—having gone out from the borders of the Jews—would reach the fullness of the Gentiles. This can also be understood regarding the final preaching which will occur in the first [state], a matter in which it was said to the order that John himself designates, through the person of John and the angel inserted among those sounding the trumpets: *You must prophesy again to many peoples and nations and tongues and kings.* <note>original: "Oportet te iterum prophetare: populis & gentibus & linguis & regibus multis." - Revelation 10:11</note> And these things, as they are said, can be accepted without incongruity, although there is something else more proper that can be designated by the name of the trumpet. We know that two things work together for the sound of a trumpet: the instrument itself and the breath. And what is meant by the trumpet, which is visible, if not the surface of the Letter <note>The physical text of the Bible</note>, which in some way is seen when it is read in a book? Or what is meant by the breath, which is invisible and yet, when sent through the trumpet, sounds terribly, if not the spiritual...
