# Concerning the fifth angel sounding the trumpet

<margin>Chapter 9. Lesson 1.</margin>
And the fifth angel sounded his trumpet. And I saw a star had fallen from heaven to the earth. And to him was given the key to the bottomless pit: and he opened the bottomless pit: and there arose smoke from the pit, like the smoke of a great furnace: and the air was darkened by the smoke of the pit: and locusts went out upon the earth.

Who this wretched man was, or from where he arose, who opened that once-closed bottomless pit, I do not know; God knows. However, it appears from the text of this reading that he was a cleric <note>a member of the clergy</note> and imbued with the knowledge of letters. Moreover, whoever he was, he received the key to the knowledge of depraved dogma—undoubtedly from the father of lies—namely, the power to investigate the depths of wisdom: not of God, but of this world, which God has destroyed and will destroy by the hands of his little ones to clear away the stumbling block of the cross, which is set as a sign and salvation for those who believe. Therefore, he opened the bottomless pit: and there arose smoke from the pit, like the smoke of a great furnace. Just as luminaries surely descend from heaven, so does dark smoke ascend from the bottomless pit. For if (as I recall I have already said) the volume of the whole of Holy Scripture—from which true wisdom proceeds, which is the light of human minds and the brilliance of spiritual eyes—is designated by "heaven," what is meant by the "bottomless pit" <note>original: "puteo abyssi"</note> but a certain depth of human wisdom? If indeed it should be called wisdom and not ignorance, since from it proceeds the smoke of error, as the Lord says: <margin>Matthew 22</margin> "You err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God." For we know that certain philosophers attempted to comprehend all things by reason, and handed down to memory for posterity some of the things they felt. Although they seemed to have disputed many things reasonably, they were nevertheless ignorant of the kindness and gentleness, as well as the omnipotence of the Creator,

<column-break/>

who was able to make all things from nothing, and by the wish of his own will, to change some things into a better and happier state. One of them proceeded so far in disputing about the body and the spirit that he said every body <note>meaning the physical, material flesh</note> is to be shunned. After this most wicked error was once cleared away in Christ, we see a certain new kind of heretics—taught by I know not whom—who have clung to it, saying that all bodies were created by the Devil. Through this, they profess that Christ did not come in the flesh, so that they clearly indicate they belong to the one who is to come, the Antichrist, as John says: <margin>2 John 1:7</margin> "Whoever denies that Christ has come in the flesh, this is the deceiver and the Antichrist." These are those heretics who are commonly called Patarenes <note>original: "pathareni"; a medieval dualist sect, similar to the Cathars, who believed the material world was evil and created by a lesser or evil deity</note>, and among others, they are named by various different names. To demonstrate that they are what they are—namely, children of darkness—they meet (as it is reported) at night, and this on appointed days, throughout the provinces in their synagogues, so that having gathered as one and showing their faces to one another, they may finally do the works of their father. Therefore, men of this sort—if indeed they are men and not reptiles—are the locusts that have gone out from the smoke of the pit. Just as Paul says to those who had believed through his word: <margin>1 Corinthians 4</margin> "In Christ Jesus through the gospel I have begotten you," so also did that one who was seen in the likeness of a star falling from heaven beget these through his error. But because all these evils happen to the human race after the sins of the sons of men, what and of what kind is the power given to them to persecute the impious, and those who do not carry the Cross of Christ to follow him, is revealed in what follows.

# And power was given to them just as <margin>Lesson 2.</margin> the scorpions of the earth have power.

Some of the reprobate have the will to harm, but they cannot, because without the permission of the just God, not even the Devil himself dared to tempt Job <margin>Job 1</margin>. Even after receiving power, he was not permitted to scourge him as much as he himself wanted, but only as much as he who gave the power willed. Hence it is added here.

This error gives rise to the Patarene heretics, whom the author equates to the biblical locusts because they deny the goodness of the physical body and the reality of Christ's incarnation.</summary>

Having previously established that the smoke represents false doctrine, the author now defines who the "grass," "trees," and "locusts" represent in the context of medieval heresies—specifically targeting the Patarenes.</meta>

->John’s Third [Part] on the Apocalypse<-
R 3

<margin>E. 3.</margin>
**And it was commanded them that they should not hurt the grass of the earth, nor any tree; but only those men who do not have the seal of God in their foreheads.**

By the **grass of the earth**, the simple folk are designated: those who do not know their right hand from their left, except for Jesus Christ and him crucified. When questioned by heretics, they turn their ears away, saying it is not their place but that of the clergy to dispute concerning the faith. In the **trees**, however, perfect men <note>In this context, "perfect" refers to those mature or fully instructed in the faith</note> are designated, who bring forth fruit in their seasons. Regarding these two kinds of men, as we said above, heretical depravity cannot find a place within them. This is because the simple are such that, once they have received the faith, they cannot be moved from it by any argument; and the others are so wise according to God that they know, through the grace given to them, how to avoid the arrows of the enemy. But those who are called "men" because of their carnality, and who do not have the seal of the living God written on their foreheads, are—by the just judgment of Almighty God—handed over to the **Locusts**, to be tormented vehemently by them for their iniquities until the time of their power is fulfilled. Truly, I believe the **seal of the living God** is the Lord’s cross, which those people truly carry on their foreheads who are not ashamed of the Crucified One, and who say continually with the Apostle:

<margin>Galatians 6.</margin>
> **But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.**

And who are they? They are those who do not wish to be wealthy in this present wicked age. For those who wish (according to the Apostle) to become rich fall into temptation and the snare of the Devil. But let us come to the essence of the matter. We know that the **Locust** is an unclean animal, and by the wings it has above it, it is raised to higher places. But the **Scorpion** lurks in hidden places and suddenly strikes the unwary—not with its mouth, but with its tail. According to this, the <term>Patarene heretics</term> <note>The Patarenes were a medieval religious movement, often associated with the Cathars, who criticized church corruption but were condemned as heretics for their dualist beliefs</note> pretend to be clean before the people and endowed with justice; yet from a hidden place, near the end of their speech, they bring forth the stings of their error. With these, however, they are not permitted to strike the servants of God, but only those men (as we have said) who lust after worldly delights. It is well known to everyone that some of them are considered "perfect," while others are called "believers." For they call those "perfect" who keep their doctrine in all things; the "believers" are those who do not keep it, but nevertheless believe those who do. Therefore, those among them who are "perfect" are those designated by the Locusts; those called "believers" are the men whom the Locusts strike with their tails. But why are those who believe them tormented? Because their stung conscience accuses them, knowing they have clung to them for the sake of temporal support—as we have learned from the reports of those who were once among them and have since repented. Finally, meeting together, they make collections of their goods; and if they see any poor people longing for the riches of the world, they first show them an affection of mercy and pity. Then they blame wealthy Christians, and especially the Priests and Clergy, who (they say) ought to maintain the apostolic life and relieve the miseries of the poor and needy, so that no one would be in want in the Christian religion—just as there was no one in want in the <term>primitive church</term> <note>The earliest Christian community in Jerusalem, described in the Acts of the Apostles as holding all property in common</note>. Then they say that the clergy have fallen from the faith and have become persecutors of the just, like the priests of the Jews who persecuted the Apostles. At last, they claim to know men who keep the apostolic faith in its integrity, so that there is no one destitute among them; and whoever comes to them poor (they say) is immediately made rich. Crafting these and similar things as if they were reasonable, they pretend to be clean animals until they strike men unexpectedly, saying: "And you too, if you wish to be among the believers in this faith, and to cling to those who observe it—or at least provide protection and oppose those resisting this sect—you will be able to be rich in this world, flowing with delights, and in the future world [have] eternal life..."

<meta>This page continues the allegorical interpretation of the locusts from Revelation 9. The previous page established that the "grass" and "trees" represent the simple faithful and the perfect, whom heretics cannot harm, while those without the "seal of God" are vulnerable to their sting.</meta>

->The Abbot’s Part of the Exposition<-

...to possess eternal life. Furthermore, a greedy man who hears these things—blinded in the eyes of his mind—is drawn by the love of riches and is made like the **horse and the mule**, 
<margin>Psalm 31 <note>Original: "Ps. 31." In modern Bibles, this is Psalm 32:9.</note></margin>
which have no understanding. And so, corrupted by words and money, he begins to exist for those riches, or as one of them; yet he is trembling and accusing himself in his own thoughts, knowing that whatever is obtained in such a way by money cannot be from good. In this manner, therefore, they torment many whom they do not kill; for while they corrupt them with money, they cannot totally uproot them from the faith of Christ. And indeed, those who do not have the seal of the living God—unless they strive to have it—are destined to die; yet they are tormented by the locusts but not killed. This is because, even if the heretics can have them as defenders corrupted by money, and though they may deny the faith of Christ, the heretics cannot draw them all the way into total perfidy <note>Here, "perfidy" refers to a complete betrayal or loss of religious faith.</note>. But a limit has been set for them which cannot be passed. For it follows:

<margin>Revelation 9:4</margin>
**And it was commanded them that they should not kill them: but that they should torment them for five months.**

This "dying" is not spoken of as eternal death, but as the extinction of faith, by which the reprobate mostly live for a time among those who truly live. However, because they neglect to carry the seal of God on their foreheads—that is, the fear of God in their hearts—they live in such a way that some die, unless they pass over to the way of life of those who truly live. Concerning such people, the 
<margin>Titus 1</margin>
Apostle Paul says: *They profess that they know God, but in their works they deny him.* But why for **five months**? Perhaps because five months contain one hundred and fifty days, and a day is sometimes used to designate a year. Thirty days represent one generation of years. Perhaps, then, five months signify five generations of years: namely, one hundred and fifty years. For it has been a long time since this sect became known, though we do not know by whom it was started or increased. As for what follows:

<margin>Revelation 9:5</margin>
**And their torment was as the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a man.**

This is a repetition of the speech so that the work may be understood. Here, something even more terrible is added, which further expresses the cause.

<column-break/>

<margin>Revelation 9:6</margin>
**And in those days (he says), men shall seek death and shall not find it: and they shall desire to die, and death shall flee from them.**

Which men shall seek death? Is it all men? No. But those whom the locusts strike. It is a heavy thing, a diabolical temptation, and difficult to bear. Wherefore the Apostle also says: 
<margin>1 Corinthians 10</margin>
*Let no temptation take hold of you but such as is human.* Finally, even **Samson**, when he was tempted by the **Philistines** through the harlots he loved so dearly, was afflicted even unto death. Because he knew it was unlawful to reveal his secret, yet overcome by her persistence as well as by pleasure, he was unable to do otherwise. So it is with these men: as we have learned through those who, coming to us in the same calamity, have confessed that they stood in it for some time. Seeing how hard it is to be separated in mind and faith from the community of the Church, and listening to the words of the heretics—which seem entirely plausible—they fall into various temptations and insoluble, harmful questions; so much so that they think it better for themselves to die than to live. This is why those who are of this sort are sad at all times, and their faces are weighed down with a perpetual paleness. And this is true of those who, for some temporal advantage, pass over in spirit to their sects, yet think it hard to relinquish the faith once received and to withdraw from **Christian piety**, which the multitude of believers preserves under all of heaven. But those who are totally subverted do not consider these things. Instead, having abandoned human reason, they have become like **Locusts** and **Scorpions** alike, seeking whom they may strike and infect with their poison, seeking those with whom they may engage in common or singular combat, so that they might either prevail by overthrowing the enemy or, if killed (as they assert), be crowned with **martyrdom**. But if this is the case, it is not concerning those evil men...

# Third Part of John in the Apocalypse
-> R 4 <-
<meta>catchword: running</meta>

But it is said more concerning the faithful; or this speech may be taken not inappropriately as referring to the end of the fifth period: since the Locusts <note>In this commentary, "Locusts" represent heretical teachers or movements.</note> will begin to prevail more harshly than usual, besides other innumerable evils that are to come upon the earth; which we ourselves who speak of these things clearly gather both from the end of the age and from the change of affairs. Indeed, in certain parts of the world, it is reported that such pestilential men have become so strong that, like **horses prepared for battle**, they fear no adversity, utterly despising temporal life as if they were to attain the eternal through punishments. For which reason it is immediately added:

<margin>Verse 7 <note>Original: "C. 7." Throughout this text, "C" is used to mark verses within Revelation 9.</note></margin>
### And the shapes of the locusts were like unto horses prepared for battle; and on their heads were as it were crowns like gold.

<margin>2 Timothy 2</margin>
They exhort one another in turn to be strong in war, as if they were about to fight for the faith, promising themselves that word of the Apostle: *No one shall be crowned except he who has striven lawfully.* <note>Reference to 2 Timothy 2:5.</note> For this reason, the crowns themselves are said to be **like gold**, because they cloak their error with plausible words, claiming to be Catholics and defenders of the orthodox faith. For they even call their own people "martyrs of God"—those who perhaps were burned with fire by Catholics—regarding them as the princes of their sect, crowned with glory and honor in the heavens. And this indeed is said of those whom they venerate as if they were God’s martyrs. But what follows is general to them all. For it is added:

<margin>Verse 8</margin>
### And their faces were as the faces of men; and they had hair as the hair of women, and their teeth were as the teeth of lions.

In the face of any living creature, either its gentleness or its ferocity appears. Therefore, the knowledge of what kind of man one is is designated in the face. Yet in these Heretics, it is not so; rather, they show one thing in their face while hiding another in their mouth, so that those whom they deceive with a human face, they may bite with the teeth of lions. They show themselves to be humane and seemingly simple, so they may crush with their molars those whom they suspect of resisting them. Therefore, in the human face, a feigned humanity is designated; in the lion-like teeth, a true monstrosity. Truly, in the **hair of women**, which is longer than the hair of men, is designated an assiduity in labor; for they boast that they are religious and modest, as if living by their own labor, abusing that authority of the Apostle which says:

<margin>Philippians 4</margin>
> *Rather let him labor, doing that which is good, that he may have something to give to those suffering need;* <note>While the margin says Philippians 4, this quote is closer to Ephesians 4:28.</note> not heeding that Gospel passage:

<margin>John 6</margin>
> *Labor not for the meat which perisheth, but for that which endureth unto everlasting life.* Nor that which

<margin>Luke 14</margin>
is said of him who said: *I have bought five yoke of oxen, I pray thee have me excused.* Finally, even the priests of the Lord are forbidden in Ezekiel to shave their hair, yet they are not permitted to grow a mane; rather, they are commanded by the same prophet to poll <note>i.e., to clip or shear. Refers to Ezekiel 44:20.</note> their hair. This is because the religious are not permitted to be idle from the works of their hands, yet they are not allowed to insist upon work beyond measure; so that there may be that which is given to Martha’s part <note>The active life of service.</note>, and yet not be lacking that which Maria <note>The contemplative life of prayer/listening.</note> receives in her part. It follows:

Just men have a breastplate against the temptations of the Devil; because, fortified and armed with constancy of mind, they do not fear the darts of the enemy. # Part of the Exposition
-> Abb. <-

By such holy animals are understood men of contemplation: whose nature it is to contemplate heavenly things and, from now on, to impart many sublime matters to you in a few words. However, those who are designated among the others as "Locusts" <note>In this context, locusts represent heretical teachers who mimic the appearance of true contemplatives.</note> are those held among them as the "perfect among the perfect" <note>A likely reference to the "Perfecti," the elite ascetic class of the Cathar heresy common in the 12th and 13th centuries.</note>. Whenever they come to a conflict, they do not act simply, but screeching and roaring they scatter their words so that they might seem to overcome with words those whom they cannot conquer with reason. Whence, in the fourth part of this book, regarding the likeness of a certain Beast ascending from the earth, it is said of these same people: *It had two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a Dragon.* <note>Reference to Revelation 13:11, illustrating hypocrisy: looking innocent (lamb) but speaking with evil intent (dragon).</note> Yet in whatever way they speak, they nevertheless use the authorities of the Scriptures—or rather, they do not "use" them but **abuse** them. Because they cannot demonstrate what they say by reason, they fortify their position with those words of the Holy Scriptures which are, according to the voice of Peter, *difficult to understand.* <margin>2 Peter 3</margin> By corrupting these through a wicked understanding of the literal text, they are able to drag them into their own treachery. However, the end result must always be observed in their words, which John shows we ought to do when he repeats the word again and again, recalling the memory of the Scorpion. For it follows:

### And they had tails like unto scorpions: And there were stings in their tails. <margin>Chapter 9, Verse 11 <note>The text cites C. 11, referring to the verse in Revelation 9.</note></margin>

For this is what the Apostle says: *And their word spreads like a cancer.* <margin>2 Timothy 2</margin> But since such horrifying creeping things are present today upon the earth, it is necessary for the faithful to cautiously redeem these evil days and to be wise in discerning between the true and the false—between the signs of Moses <margin>Exodus 7</margin> and Aaron, and the signs of Jannes and Mambres. <note>Jannes and Mambres were the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses by mimicking his miracles through sorcery.</note> Let those look to it who refuse to discern between one time and another—between a calm sea and one tossed by the storms of a mighty tempest—so that they might still be permitted to devote themselves to feasting and to spend their days in <margin>Job 21</margin> good things, as in the years of an age and days of old. For if all worldly times were equal for salvation, and the last times were not worse than the first, the Apostle would not have said: *In the last days perilous times shall come.* <margin>2 Timothy 3</margin> Nor, having passed over so many kinds of heretics whose infestations the Church has sustained until now, would he have bothered to show those of whom we speak in the spirit of prophecy; he would either have spoken of everyone at once or remained silent about all of them. 

But he spoke of these specifically, as if of those heretics who are the extreme of all heretics, and nothing other than what we see and hear. They certainly condemn lawful marriages and the foods which God created for the faithful to receive with thanksgiving. <margin>1 Timothy 4</margin> And because it was going to be so, it was predicted (as we have already said) by the Apostle Paul, writing in this manner in the letter to Timothy: *The Spirit clearly says that in the last times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to spirits of error and doctrines of demons in hypocrisy, speaking lies and having their conscience seared with a hot iron, forbidding to marry and commanding to abstain from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by the faithful.* These most serene words of Paul—or rather of the Holy Spirit—have been read in the Church of God for nearly one thousand, one hundred and fifty years. <note>This specific number suggests the commentary was written around 1210-1220 AD, calculating from the time of Paul's letters.</note> And always this is said in them when they are read by anyone: that which was in them at the time they were written. It is not because a "future time" is always announced in them that the thing said will be in the future without end; rather, it was necessary for it to be in the future only until the time arrived in which what was said should happen. But if it was written by the Holy Spirit so that it might be known when it happened, it is perfectly clear that He spoke of this time, in which we see heretics in the world who do those evil things which the Apostle prescribed—or rather, which the Spirit of the Almighty God predicted would come. But that too is known which John (the author of this book) predicted in his letter concerning the Antichrist; just as that which these men say is not unknown. So much so that while we read those things to be predicted, which we see for the most part fulfilled in these men, one would rather weep than say anything. For indeed...

# Third Book of Joachim on the Apocalypse
-> Third Part <-

...is given to be understood, because what is fostered within them is nearly ready to burst forth into a basilisk <note>original: "regulum," literally "little king," often used to describe the basilisk serpent. Joachim uses this to describe the hidden venom of heresy finally manifesting in the Antichrist.</note>. For they deny that the Son of God has come in the flesh, saying that all flesh was created by the Devil; thus it is aptly understood that the blessed John foresaw them in the spirit <margin>1 John 4</margin> when he says in his epistle: *Every spirit that denies that Jesus has come in the flesh is not of God; and this is the Antichrist, who is to come.* Indeed, they even claim to possess an apostolic rule which all obey, concerning which it is subsequently added in this present passage:

<margin>Chapter 12</margin>
### And they had over them a king, the Angel of the Abyss; whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon, in Greek Apollyon, and in Latin he has the name the Destroyer. <note>original: "exterminans"</note>

¶ I think that these kinds of pseudo-prophets similarly hold the place of the Antichrist, just as David and the other kings of Jerusalem held the place of Christ. Hence the kings of Judah themselves were called the "Anointed of the Lord" <note>original: "Christi domini"</note>. Indeed, just as all those were called the Anointed of the Lord, so in this sect many have perhaps already preceded who, by the authority of their treachery, should be called "Antichrists"—especially since John says, using the present or past tense for the future: <margin>1 John 2</margin> *As you have heard that Antichrist comes, even now many Antichrists have arisen.* And because he immediately adds: *By this we know it is the last hour.* He demonstrates that the Great Antichrist himself follows not long after. Considering the various faces of the Scriptures and the harmony of their beginnings and endings, I believe he is present in the world, even if the hour of his revelation has not yet come. For according to Jerome <margin>Jerome</margin>, the Roman Empire—which resists him—must be desolated before he is revealed; and then (he says) the wicked one will be revealed <margin>2 Thessalonians 2</margin>, whose coming is according to the working of Satan, with all lying signs and wonders. He will be revealed openly when the sixth Angel sounds his trumpet, even if he begins to work secretly before then. We truly believe the time of the sixth Angel 

<column-break/>

will be brief, because of what the Lord says: *For the sake of the elect, those days shall be shortened.* <margin>Matthew 24</margin> For (unless I am mistaken) that same tribulation and the time of the sixth Angel's trumpet-blast must be concluded within three years. Although the sixth period is twofold, something must precede that belongs to the time of the sixth Angel while the fifth Angel is still in battle; especially since that which belongs to the subsequent things usually begins before the preceding works reach their completion. If this is so, the Antichrist must precede the time of the sixth Angel, either in person or (as is more commonly believed) through his messengers, so that having long ago conceived his poison, he may then pour it out, already prepared for war and fortified by many diabolical arguments. 

He is rightly called the King of the Abyss because he reigns in the hearts of the unfaithful from the beginning. He is called Abaddon in Hebrew and Apollyon in Greek, and in Latin he has the name the Destroyer <note>original: "exterminans"</note>, because in his days what is written in the Book of Psalms must be fulfilled: *You have brought a vine out of Egypt; you have cast out the nations and planted it,* etc. And further: *Why have you broken down its hedge, so that all who pass by the way pluck its fruit? The boar from the forest has destroyed it, and the singular wild beast has devoured it.* <margin>Psalm 79</margin> <note>This is Psalm 80 in modern Bibles. Joachim interprets the "Boar" as the Antichrist.</note> This is as if to say: Many heretics, passing by and stepping off the path, have brought many damages and reproaches upon the Church, which could be tolerated for a time; for even if the fruit was lost, the vine itself remained whole in its status. But he who is called the "Boar from the forest" will destroy it so intolerably that it will no longer look like a vine, but like a desert wilderness. While the Devil works much destruction through his members under the fifth Angel, a greater and heavier destruction will follow under the sixth; and how hard and narrow will be that which follows under the seventh! Whence it is added immediately after:

### The first woe is past; and behold, two more woes are coming after these.

# Part of the Abbot's Exposition

By such holy animals <note>original: "sanctorum animalium," referring to the four living creatures of the Apocalypse, often interpreted as types of contemplative men or the four Gospels.</note> are understood contemplative men: whose proper role is to contemplate heavenly things and, henceforth, to intimate many and sublime truths to us few. However, those who are designated among the other kind of Locusts are the "perfect of the perfect" <note>original: "perfectorum perfecti." This likely refers to the "Perfecti," the elite rank of the Cathar heretics who practiced extreme asceticism.</note> among them: if they ever come into conflict, they do not do so calmly; rather, hissing and roaring, they scatter their words so that they might appear to overcome with words those whom they cannot conquer with reason. Hence, in the fourth part of this book, regarding the appearance of a certain Beast ascending from the earth, it is said of these same ones: *He had two horns like a lamb, and he spoke like a dragon.* <note>Revelation 13:11</note> Yet, in whatever way they speak, they nevertheless use the authorities of the scriptures—or rather, they do not use them, but abuse them. Because they cannot demonstrate what they say through reason, they fortify their position with those words of the holy scriptures which, according to the voice of Peter, are *difficult to understand.* <margin>2 Peter 3</margin> By adulterating these through a depraved understanding of the letter, they are able to drag them into their own treachery. Nevertheless, the end goal must always be observed in their words, which John demonstrates we ought to do when he repeats the word again and again, recalling the memory of the Scorpion. For it follows:

### And they had tails like scorpions: and there were stings in their tails.

<margin>2 Timothy 2</margin> For this is what the Apostle said: *And their talk will spread like a cancer.* <note>original: "ut cancer serpit," traditionally translated as spreading like gangrene or a canker.</note> But since such horrific creeping things are present today upon the earth, it is necessary for the faithful to cautiously redeem these evil days and be wise in discerning between the true and the false—between the signs of Moses <margin>Exodus 7</margin> and Aaron, and the signs of Jannes and Mambres <note>The legendary names of the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses.</note>. Either he would have spoken of all together, or he would have remained silent about all. ### Third Part of the Exposition on the Apocalypse
<meta>The header "Joa. Tertia In Apo." refers to the third part of the commentary on the Apocalypse by Joachim of Fiore.</meta>

...it is given to be understood) what has been nurtured within them: it is altogether ready to burst forth into a basilisk <term>regulum</term> <note>original: "regulum." In medieval bestiaries, the *regulus* or "little king" is the basilisk, a deadly serpent born from a cock's egg, often used as a symbol for the Antichrist or heresy.</note>. For they deny that the Son of God has come in the flesh, saying that all flesh was created by the Devil: so that it may be aptly understood that the blessed John foresaw them in the spirit <margin>1 John 4</margin> when he said in his epistle: *He who denies that Christ has come in the flesh is not of God; and this is the Antichrist who is to come.* <note>The text cites 1 John 1, but this refers to 1 John 4:3 or 2 John 1:7.</note> Indeed, they even claim to have an "apostolic man" whom they all obey; regarding whom it is added in the present passage:

<margin>Revelation 9:11</margin> **And they had over them a king, the Angel of the Abyss: whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon; in Greek, however, Apollyon: and in Latin he has the name Exterminator <note>original: "exterminans." This is usually translated in English bibles as "The Destroyer."</note>.**

¶ I think that pseudo-prophets of this kind likewise hold the place of the Antichrist, just as David and the other kings of Jerusalem held the place of Christ. Hence, even the kings of Judah themselves were called the "Christs of the Lord" <note>original: "Christi domini," meaning "the Lord's anointed."</note>. Just as all of those were called the Lord's anointed, so too in this sect, many perhaps have already come before who, by the authority of their treachery, should be called Antichrists; especially since John speaks using the present or past tense for the future: <margin>1 John 2</margin> *As you have heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many Antichrists have arisen.* And because he immediately adds: *By this we know it is the last hour.* This demonstrates that the great Antichrist himself follows not long after. Considering all the aspects of the scriptures and the harmony of their beginnings and ends, I believe him to be present in the world, even if the hour of his revelation has not yet come. <margin>Jerome</margin> For according to Jerome, it is necessary for the Roman Empire—which currently resists him—to be desolated before he is revealed; and then (he says) that wicked one will be revealed, <margin>2 Thessalonians 2</margin> whose coming is according to the working of Satan, with all lying signs and wonders. He will be revealed openly under the sixth angel sounding the trumpet, even if he begins to work secretly before then. The time of the sixth angel is believed

<column-break/>

to be very brief, because of what the Lord said: *For the sake of the elect, those days will be shortened.* <margin>Matthew 24</margin> For in three years (unless I am mistaken) that same tribulation and the time of the sixth angel sounding the trumpet must be concluded; although that sixth period is twofold: something must precede which belongs to the time of the sixth angel while the fifth angel is still in the fray; especially since that which belongs to the following things usually begins before the preceding works reach their completion. If this is so, the Antichrist must precede the time of the sixth angel, either by himself or (as is more widely believed) through his messengers; so that having conceived his poison long before, he may then pour it out, already prepared for war and forewarned by many diabolical arguments. He is rightly called the King of the Abyss, because he reigns in the hearts of the unfaithful from the beginning. He is called *Abaddon* in Hebrew, *Apollyon* in Greek, and in Latin he has the name *Exterminator*: because in his days that which is written in the book of Psalms must be fulfilled: *You have brought a vine out of Egypt; you have cast out the nations and planted it,* etc. And further down: *Why have you broken down its wall, so that all who pass by the way pluck its fruit?* <margin>Psalm 80</margin> *The Boar from the forest has exterminated it <note>original: "Exterminauit eam Aper de silua." Although the Devil works many destructions through his members under the fifth angel, a greater and more grievous extermination will follow under the sixth, and what is harsh and narrow will follow under the seventh. Hence it is immediately added:

¶ **One woe has passed; and behold, two more woes are coming after these.**

# Joachim’s Third Part on the Apocalypse

...it is understood) because what is nurtured in them is near to bursting forth entirely into a basilisk <note>original: "regulum." In medieval bestiaries, the basilisk was known as the "little king" of serpents, often used as a symbol for the Antichrist or deadly heresy.</note>. For they deny that the Son of God came in the flesh, saying: "all flesh was created by the Devil." Thus it is aptly understood that the <margin>1 John 4</margin> blessed John foresaw them in spirit when he said in his epistle: "He who denies that Christ has come in the flesh is not from God; and he is the Antichrist who is to come." <note>Joachim is likely referring to the Cathars or dualist heretics of his time, who believed the physical world was evil and thus denied the Incarnation.</note> Indeed, they even claim to have an "apostolic man" <note>A leader claiming apostolic authority, perhaps a reference to the Cathar "Pope" or regional bishops.</note> whom all obey, about whom it is subsequently added in this present passage:

<margin>T. 12</margin>
### And they had over them a king, the Angel of the Abyss; whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon, but in Greek, Apollyon; and in Latin he has the name Exterminans <note>The Destroyer or Exterminator</note>.

I think that he himself <note>The Antichrist</note> comes to hold the place of the Antichrist among these kinds of false prophets in the same way that David and the other kings of Jerusalem held the place of Christ. Hence, even the kings of Judah themselves were called the "Christs of the Lord" <note>In the sense of being "Anointed ones."</note>. Since all of those were called "Christs of the Lord," so also in this sect, many have perhaps already preceded him who, by the authority of their treachery, should be called "Antichrists." This is especially so since John says, using the present or past tense for the future: <margin>1 John 2</margin> "As you have heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many Antichrists have arisen." And because he immediately adds: "Whereby we know that it is the last hour," it demonstrates that the great Antichrist himself follows not long after. Considering all the aspects of the Scriptures and the harmony of their beginnings and endings, I believe he is present in the world, even if the hour of his revelation has not yet come. <margin>Jerome</margin> For according to Jerome, the Roman Empire—which resists him—must be laid waste before he is revealed; and then (he says) that <margin>2 Thess. 2</margin> lawless one will be revealed, whose coming is according to the working of Satan, with all signs and lying wonders.

He will be revealed openly under the sounding of the trumpet of the sixth Angel, although he may begin to work secretly beforehand. Indeed, we believe the time of the sixth Angel to be very brief, because of what the Lord said: <margin>Matt. 24</margin> "For the sake of the elect, those days shall be shortened." For in three years (unless I am mistaken) that same tribulation and the time of the sixth Angel's trumpet must be ended; although the sixth period is twofold: something must go before which pertains to the time of the sixth Angel, while the fifth Angel still remains in the battle; especially since that which pertains to the following things usually begins before the preceding works receive their completion. If this is so, it is necessary for the Antichrist to anticipate the time of the sixth Angel, either by himself or (as is more believed) through his messengers, so that he may pour out the poison conceived long before, being then already prepared for war and fortified by many diabolical arguments. He is also rightly called the King of the Abyss, because from the beginning he reigns in the heart of the unfaithful people. He is called Abaddon in Hebrew, Apollyon in Greek, and in Latin he has the name Exterminans <note>The Exterminator</note>, because in his days that which is written in the book of Psalms must be fulfilled: "You have brought a vine out of Egypt; you have cast out the nations and planted it," etc. And further down: <margin>Psalm 80 (79)</margin> "Why have you broken down its hedge, so that all who pass by the way pluck its fruit? The Boar from the forest has laid it waste <note>original: "Exterminauit eam"</note>, and the singular wild beast has devoured it." This is as if to say: Many heretics, passing by and stepping out of the way, have brought many losses and reproaches upon the Church, which could be tolerated for a time; for even if the fruit was lost, the Church herself remained whole in her state. But he who is called the "Boar from the forest" will destroy her so intolerably that she will not seem to be a vine, but a desert solitude. Although the Devil works many destructions through his members under the fifth Angel, yet a greater and more grievous destruction will follow under the sixth, and a hard and narrow one will follow under the seventh. Hence it is immediately added:

### Woe, one has passed; and behold, two more woes are coming after these.

### Concerning the sixth angel sounding the trumpet.

<margin>A. 13</margin>
**And the sixth Angel sounded his trumpet. And I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar, which is before the eyes of God, saying to the sixth Angel who had the trumpet: "Release the four angels who are bound in the great river Euphrates." And the four Angels were released, who were prepared for the hour, and the day, and the month, and the year, so that they might kill a third part of men; and the number of the equestrian army was twenty thousand times ten thousand; and thus I saw the horses in the vision; and those who sat upon them had breastplates of fire, and of sulfur, and of hyacinth <note>original: "iacyntinas." In this context, it refers to a deep smoky blue or violet color, often associated with the sky or gemstones.</note>.**

The time of the sixth Angel sounding the trumpet—of which we speak in the present chapter—is such that we feel it is a future event in its full sense, yet it seems to have already taken its beginning in some measure. For just as John the Baptist was made a preacher of grace before the Law of Moses had entirely fallen away, so any sixth Angel begins to sound his trumpet before his predecessor has ceased to ring out. Subsequent battles commence before the preceding wars reach the consummation of the age. Therefore, as far as I am able to grasp, the time of the sixth Angel has indeed been initiated, but the time of the fifth has not yet reached its completion up to the present. The time of the sixth Angel, then, has already begun in some respect, and it is necessary that what is written about him in this book be fulfilled with all speed and urgency. **And I heard** (he said) **a single voice from the horns of the golden altar**

One of these is the Blessed John (whose solemn voice this especially is) which has often rung in our ears. For if we are capable of contemplating the course of the four gospels, we hear in those four a single common voice announcing to us that the Lord Jesus would be handed over into the hands of sinners at the end of the fifth day which precedes the Day of Preparation <note>original: "parasceue." The Friday before the Sabbath; here referring to the day of the Crucifixion.</note>; and on the day itself which is called the sixth, he was crucified, died, and was buried. If we understand this voice spiritually, it surely hints to us in the spirit what was to come: namely, that the sons of night and darkness are to be released in the time of the sixth Angel sounding the trumpet, to fulfill what the Lord said when asked about the end of the world in <margin>Luke 21</margin>: **"When you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that its destruction is near."** Now, the sixth Angel is told to release the four angels when, because of the infinite crimes of men, the Saints of God are commanded not to pray for a wicked and adulterous People—according to what is said by the voice of the Lord to <margin>Exodus 32</margin> Moses: **"Let me alone, so that my wrath may blaze up."** It was as if God were "bound" by the prayer of the righteous man so that He could not do what He willed. If God Himself is thus bound, how much more (though in a different way) are wicked men bound by the prayer of the righteous, lest they do the evil they are prepared to do, until the sins of Babylon reach even unto heaven and the Lord remembers her iniquities. Or certainly, it is said to the sixth Angel sounding the trumpet that he should release the Angels—not because it is his role to release them, but because it is his role to show them as released—according to what is said to the Prophet Isaiah <margin>Isaiah 6</margin>: **"Blind the heart of this people,"** and the other things that follow. For the Prophet did not blind the heart of the Jewish people himself, but the prophe-

<margin>Job 40</margin>

One is said to be prepared for the "month" or the "year" who believes he can persevere in his cause for as long as he is either permitted or commanded to remain in it. These four evil angels are therefore said to be prepared for the hour or the day because they are always anxious and vigilant for evil, waiting for the hour and day when the power might be given to them to interrogate Christians with tortures and to drag some of them into their own filth. They are said to be prepared for the month or the year because they do not believe themselves to be so transient that they would do what they can for just a moment and then stop; rather, they are prepared to fight for their error (even if it were necessary) until death, as the Lord says: **"They will think they offer service to

### John’s Third Book on the Apocalypse

...the land of Jerusalem is called spiritually "the rising of the sun," because there Christ our God, the **sun of justice**, <note>A reference to Malachi 4:2, often applied to Christ in medieval exegesis.</note> arose. This was symbolized by the feet of the statue which King Nebuchadnezzar saw in his vision: it arose from a planting of pure iron. This refers to that kingdom of the Saracens which was initiated by **Muhammad**. I believed this should be noted especially, so that no one may accuse me of bringing the afflicted nation of the Saracens into the narrative twice—that is, in two different times, namely the fourth and the sixth. This is neither contradictory nor absurd, because one head of the beast, which seemed as if dead, lived again from the dead; and it was seen to have done worse evils than those it did from the beginning. It is not foreign to the faith that in that vision of Nebuchadnezzar, <note>In Daniel 2, Nebuchadnezzar sees a statue made of different metals representing successive world empires.</note> gold was placed once, silver once, and bronze likewise once; but iron was placed not once, but twice. I say these things for this reason: because these two final kingdoms have their place among the conflicts of the seven angels of whom we are treating—namely, in the fourth and sixth periods—while the other three kingdoms are excluded from this specific grouping. 

Therefore, the cavalry army which Saint John saw signifies both the pseudo-prophets and the Saracens together. **Anger**: because they do not wish to act rationally like men, but without reason or justice, they rage against those who do not hold the same views as them. 

**Lust**: because while we praise a chaste life, they consider a life of luxury to be happy.

# Explanation of the Apocalypse: Part Two

...finished: because the numbers ten and one thousand are perfect numbers. But he says: "Twenty thousand times ten thousand." <note>original: "Vicies millies dena millia." This refers to Revelation 9:16, describing the massive size of the demonic or enemy army.</note> This is just as if one were to say: ten thousand times ten thousand, and then again ten thousand times ten thousand. We have heard about the riders—what they are like and with what weapons they are armed to resist the truth. Now let us also hear about the horses, who are perhaps even more cruel in the evils they inflict. For it follows:

<margin>Chapter 14</margin>
**And the heads of the horses were like the heads of lions; and out of their mouths issued fire, smoke, and sulfur. By these three plagues, a third of mankind was killed: by the fire, smoke, and sulfur that came out of their mouths. For the power of the horses was in their mouths and in their tails. For their tails were like serpents, having heads; and with these they do harm.** <note>Quoting Revelation 9:17–19.</note>

When any nation begins to prevail and subject tribes and languages to itself, it is customary for the one who is their leader to divide cities and castles among his soldiers. We have learned that this has happened not only among the pagans, but even among the people called Christians. Those who rule over peoples also usually study wisdom and doctrine so that they may appear distinguished among other men and act, as it were, with human reason. However, it often happens—and happens frequently—that those who dominate peoples are seen to possess a human form among men due to their reason and knowledge, while those who are unrefined <term>rustici</term> <note>Literally "country-dwellers," used here to denote uneducated, coarse, or "brutish" common soldiers.</note> and brutish have no humanity or reason in themselves. Instead, they are like the **horse and the mule**
<margin>Psalm 31</margin>
**who have no understanding.** <note>Psalm 32:9 in modern Bibles, though cited as Psalm 31 in the Latin Vulgate used by the author.</note> Very often, when...

<column-break/>

...judging others, those who judge them pronounce the sentence with a certain pity, so that they do not appear to act of their own will, but compelled by necessity. However, those who are unrefined and brutish, when they receive the power to punish, gnash their teeth at the victim like roaring lions, showing themselves to have no feeling of mercy. Just as the Governor Pilate tried to rescue Christ and took pity on him, but the ministers <note>The soldiers and temple guards who carried out the physical abuse of Jesus.</note> not only killed Him, but also—to show themselves cruel in His passion—inflicted heavier torments upon Him with spit and blows, among the other indignities of His death. Thus, the riders of the horses are shown to be terrible enough, yet they are far different from the horses themselves. These horses are defiled by lion-like heads and made monstrous with serpent-like tails, presenting a horrible spectacle to those who observe them. For what is more ferocious than a lion? What is more furious than a serpent? **Their fury** (he says) **is according to the likeness of a serpent.** <note>Psalm 58:4.</note> Furthermore, the lion rages openly;

In secret, they speak charmingly and promise a happy life to those who renounce their faith, so that they might break with flatteries those whom they cannot overcome with torments. This is why there are lion heads on the horses, and why there are serpent heads on the tails. Nor is it a wonder if **fire, smoke, and sulfur** are said to proceed from their mouths, because **out of the abundance of the heart** (says the Lord) **the mouth speaks.** **The good man, out of the good treasure of his heart, brings forth good; and the evil man, out of the evil treasure of his heart, brings forth evil.** <note>Matthew 12:34–35.</note> For what kind of disciples can they be who have evil teachers? ### John’s Third Part on the Apocalypse

...sulfur. Because they see those riders dressed in **hyacinth-colored** breastplates, they perceive the smoke within their hearts. Because of the intelligence they possess, their consciences are seared; they are less bold in doing the evils they think up because they fear the judgment of the all-seeing God in some way—or at least they fear the temporal punishment that has struck many in past ages. However, those who are deceived by them believe they have good consciences and think that in the things they do, they are offering a service to God. This is why the riders

<margin>John 18 <note>The text quotes John 16:2 ("offering a service to God"), though the margin notes Chapter 18.</note></margin>
of the horses appear to have breastplates of fire, sulfur, and hyacinth <note>original: "iacyntinas," a deep blue or violet color</note> to protect their own error. But the fire, sulfur, and smoke that the horses vomit out are not so much for protecting their own error as for the slaughter of many—specifically those of whom it is said: **By these three plagues a third of mankind was killed: by the fire, smoke, and sulfur that came out of their mouths.** And what follows: **For the power of the horses was in their mouths and in their tails; for their tails were like serpents, having heads; and with these they do harm.** It is as if one were to say: "The strength of other horses is in their backs and their feet; but these horses, contrary to all custom and reason, have their strength in their heads and their tails." For usually, proud men begin to do evil slowly, but after they are stirred up, they burn with rage; then, once their anger is spent, they rest from inflicting harm. But these are not like that; they begin to commit evil with open rage, and just when they are thought to be resting

<margin>1 Thessalonians 5</margin>
from inflicting evils, they suddenly commit even worse ones unexpectedly. For this is what is meant by: **When they say: "peace and security," then sudden destruction will come upon them, like labor pains on a woman with child, and they will not escape.** <note>1 Thessalonians 5:3</note> Therefore, that head of the **Beast** (which refers to these adversaries) is said to have had a sword-wound and yet lived: because when people believe they are failing, they are actually beginning; and when they are thought to be dead, they live on in a worse way. Let those die by these plagues who, having denied the Christian faith, commit themselves to the judgment and command of these enemies. They do this either because they fear their wrath, or because they are enticed by the stench of luxury, or because they see some color of false religion in this fierce sect—but most of all because of the lying signs which (as shown elsewhere) they are going to perform. Just how great this people is, and the great evils they will do, is shown by the prophecy of Joel

### Part of the Exposition

<margin>Lesson 15</margin>
**And the rest of mankind who were not killed by these plagues did not repent of the works of their hands, so that they would not worship demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk; nor did they repent of their murders, nor of their sexual immorality, nor of their thefts.**

¶ Having said these things, he stopped, leaving the discourse unfinished and incomplete. No doubt this was because of what is said in another place by the prophet:
<margin>Isaiah 24</margin>
**"My secret is my own; my secret is my own."** <note>original: "Secretum meum mihi." A common medieval citation of Isaiah 24:16 to indicate divine mysteries that remain hidden.</note> For it seems in these words that the tribulation itself is to be ended for a time, and a little peace given to the Christian people—not because their crimes will have been purged by then, but because that Merciful One begins to strike in such a way that he eventually pulls back his hand. He does this so that, in whatever way possible, those who are dying in their sins might return and live. Yet, those whom he waits for to repent, but who do not, he punishes more harshly. Hence, he threatens men of this kind through the prophet:
<margin>Isaiah 63</margin>
**"The day of vengeance is in my heart."** Why is this? Because **"the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night."** It will come in such a way that it cannot be foreseen.
<margin>Book 5</margin>
But if this is so, how is the prophet Elijah promised to come before the great day of the Lord arrives?
<margin>Malachi 4</margin>
Is it because this matter itself is deeply hidden? For who would have understood at the first coming of the Lord
<margin>Matthew 11</margin>
that Elijah had come, if the Lord had not revealed it by saying
<margin>John 1</margin>
that John himself was Elijah? This is especially striking since John himself had said, "I am not Elijah." For who is capable of tracing the <term>philia dei</term> <note>literally "friendship of God," though contextually referring to the deep designs or mysteries of God's love and wisdom</note>?
<margin>Romans 11</margin>
**"O the depth of the wisdom and knowledge of God!"** says the Apostle. **"How incomprehensible are his judgments, and how unsearchable his ways!"** It seems, therefore, that John wished to hint at something when he said: *And the rest of mankind who were not killed by these plagues and did not repent of the works of their hands...* Yet, because of the severity of the judgment, he was not permitted to finish the thought. Men are accustomed to use this manner of speaking when they know that evil is prepared for wicked people; they wish to make it known, but they do not dare to out of fear or love for their masters. Moved by piety or zeal, they begin to say what they know, but because they know it is a secret, they fail to follow through. It is as if one were to say: "Since it is clear that the Just Judge will render to each according to his works, will those who abuse the mercy of God be immune from his plagues just because he shows mercy for a time for the sake of his elect?" Not at all. Indeed, lest anyone should think this silence should be maintained, other things are added, one after another, which seem far more grave.

But perhaps someone says: "Do I worship demons and idols, that I should fear God’s judgment on this? I do not worship demons, but God. For mute and deaf idols have been crushed in almost the whole world. What, then, do these plagues have to do with me?" But if the rest—and indeed if not all—the words of the book are spiritual, then this very thing can surely be understood and explained spiritually. For there are many who think they adore what they do not adore, and do not adore what they do adore. There are some who think they do not worship demons, and yet they commit themselves with the full devotion of their minds to sorcery, divine incantations, spells, and omens. These people certainly worship demons, and they are no different from those who used to serve demons. The cult of <term>idolatry</term> <note>the worship of physical images as gods</note> has been wiped away from the face of Christ; there is hardly a man in the world (except perhaps in unknown regions) who would fashion and worship a mute statue. And yet, the sentence of Paul is clear:
<margin>Ephesians 5</margin>
**"No fornicator, or unclean person, or covetous man—which is the service of idols—has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God."** And lest anyone should imagine anything else regarding this, flattering himself about the mercy of God, he added: **"Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of unbelief."** Therefore, those who have defiled themselves with such impurities, even if they escape these plagues when the day of peace arrives—

Nevertheless, before that tribulation comes, the Lord will send to men an Angel of Light who—by opening the volume that was once closed—may teach them the hidden secrets <term>mysteries of God; secret truths known only through divine revelation</term>, so that it may serve as a support for the elect and as a weight of damnation for the reprobate (who despise these things). While the former group profits toward salvation from the opening of the book, the latter group incurs a greater blindness of ignorance from the brightness of the light. For as the Prophet says, speaking in the type of the spiritual Church:

<margin>Isaiah 60</margin>
**"Arise, be enlightened, O Jerusalem, for your light has come,"** <note>original: "Surge illuminare Hierusalem: quia venit lumen tuum"</note> and immediately he added and said, **"For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and a thick mist the people."** Therefore, even if the reprobate are not worthy, yet either for their sake—so that they may have no excuse—or for the sake of the elect—so that they may know how to redeem the time because the days are evil—a Preacher of Truth must be sent by the Lord during the "sixth time" <note>The "sixth time" refers to the era of the sixth trumpet or the sixth age of the world in medieval chronology.</note> to teach men to despise earthly things and love heavenly ones. For what follows is:

<margin>Chapter 10, v. 1</margin>
**And I saw another strong Angel descending from heaven, clothed in a cloud, and a rainbow <note>original: "yris," a Latinized form of the Greek "iris."</note> was on his head; and his face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire. And he had in his hand an open book, and he set his right foot upon the sea, but his left upon the earth; and he cried out with a loud voice, just as when a lion roars. And when he had cried out, seven thunders uttered their voices.**

Whoever this Preacher of Truth may be, he is described as "strong" because he will be robust in faith. He will descend "from heaven" because he will come down from the contemplative life to the active life. He will be "clothed in a cloud" because he will be wrapped in the scripture of the Prophets. Furthermore, he wears a "rainbow on his head" because he will have the gift of the Holy Spirit in his mind. For just as the rainbow (that is, the heavenly arch) appears joined to the clouds of heaven, so too, in order to convince adversaries, the mystical understanding must be joined to the scripture of the holy Prophets. But more on this in what follows. For first it must be asked (if indeed it can be found) who this Angel is, so distinguished that we may afterwards investigate what the things written about him signify spiritually. According to the letter <term>literal interpretation</term>, I would believe this Angel to be either Enoch or Elijah, were it not for the fact that in the following sections the prophetic discourse speaks of two prophets—who are thought to be Enoch and Elijah—

<margin>Enoch.</margin>
in terms no less significant than these. However, if this Angel is one of them, it would seem that he should be understood more as Enoch, who was the first to disappear. But I believe God knows this best. One thing I say for certain: the significance of this Angel personally touches upon some great preacher, although spiritually it may appropriately be applied to many spiritual men who will exist at that same time. This is especially true since, just as Christ chose for himself many disciples to preach the letter of the Gospel, so it is necessary for the Holy Spirit to choose for himself whomsoever he wills to lead them, as if from darkness to light, into a spiritual and life-giving understanding—as the Lord says: **"For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you."** Hence, this same Angel is rightly said to have a rainbow on his head, because the rainbow (as we have already said in the second part) signifies either the Holy Spirit himself or spiritual understanding. Truly, the face of the Angel was like the sun, because in this sixth time the contemplation of the wisdom of God must shine forth in the manner of the sun, reaching the knowledge of those who are designated by Peter, James, and John—namely, the people of the Hebrews, the Greeks, and the Latins.

Indeed, first of the Latins, then of the Greeks, and of the Hebrews: the last have been made first, and the first last. <margin>Matthew 20</margin> For to touch upon another mystery <term>mysterium; a sacred secret revealed by God</term> pertaining to this: Peter was the first to enter the Tomb, and after him John; but thirdly, Mary Magdalene bowed down and looked into the Tomb. Furthermore, what these three—who saw the face of Jesus Christ shine on the mountain <margin>Matthew 17</margin>—designate is the same as the Magi who came from the East to the house in which Christ, the Sun of Justice, dwelt, guided by the sign of the Star; for they also, for the same reason of the mystery, are traditionally said to have been three. But because a worthy opportunity has been given to speak of such worthy and holy things, it is necessary for us to treat these three Apostles ascending the mountain a little more broadly: so that we may understand that what was performed there according to the letter must be fulfilled here according to the spirit. For there can be no doubt that it was a matter of a great and hidden mystery that after six days, Christ Jesus deigned to reveal the glory of his majesty to three close disciples. And this occurred between Moses and Elijah, upon whom a great loftiness of authority was conferred among the great prophets. I judge the "sixth day" to signify the "sixth time" of the church, in which—between Moses and Elijah—the face of Christ shines like the Sun in its strength. This is because at the boundary of the second state (which mystically pertains to Moses, who was the shepherd of the people of Israel) and the third state (which in like manner pertains to Elijah, who was truly spiritual, knowing no wife, but leading a solitary and private life), the face of Christ Jesus—that is, the scripture of the New Testament—becomes more clearly known than usual to those designated by those apostles. For just as the Old Testament, which is according to the spirit the "face of Moses," became known to the cultivators of truth at the start of the sixth age of the world when the veil (which was over it) was removed: so now also, at the start of the seventh, for the lovers of

<column-break/>

justice, the Gospel of Christ Jesus will begin to shine more fully. Thus, we who have hitherto known him through faith may be led all the way to the contemplation of the beauty of his very loftiness. Therefore, because the sixth age—which ends in six specific times (as we have often said)—was given to the martyrs for labor, and the seventh to those resting for the contemplation of God, the face of the Savior rightly shone like the light of day between Moses (the shepherd of the people laboring in governance) and Elijah (leading a quiet and contemplative life). For at the boundary (as we have already said) of the second state, which was established for labor, and the third, which is for leisure and rest, this so wonderful clarity is granted to us and our children (if we are not negligent). Thus, as signs and miracles—by which a tender and temporarily weak faith has been nourished until now—become rare, we should now, as elders and provident men, not seek to see a sign from heaven like those who hesitate or tempt God; rather, let us walk tirelessly in the light of our Savior through the path of Justice. Certainly, for this reason, one had to labor longer in the sixth age, and especially in the "sixth time of the sixth age." Just as the children of Israel labored doubly on the sixth day to collect manna for both the sixth day and the Sabbath, so should the faithful labor in the word of God in the sixth age. They must diligently recognize both the afflictions of the present time and the sacred meanings <term>sacramenta; here meaning the hidden divine purposes</term> of those same afflictions, so that they may pass over to contemplate the mysteries of the following world—that is, the seventh age which follows—in the splendor of celestial light. This is clearly stated because of the sixth day and the sixth time, and because of the splendor of the Sun which appeared in the face of this Angel just as it did in Christ Jesus. This is so that it might be aptly understood that what is hinted at there on the sixth day (not without mystery) is to be fulfilled spiritually in the "sixth time." ...harmony of the two testaments? This sense of harmony is rightly held to be like the pillar of fire: <note>original: "columne ignis"</note> which both reveals the firmness of truth in the literal word and illuminates and enflames those who seek Him in truth; and like one about to discern the true light, it returns to higher things. Therefore, this three-fold quality is ascribed to the doctors <term>doctors; here meaning "learned teachers" or "theologians"</term> of truth: because through their mediation and labor, that grace—which was designated in the rainbow <note>The Latin "vri" is likely a contraction for "iri," referring to the rainbow over the Angel's head in Revelation 10:1.</note> to the understanding of the listeners—is brought forth by the Lord’s generous gift. Wherefore the book in the hand of that same Angel is rightly shown to be open, though it was once sealed; for when these three <note>Likely referring to the three languages or the three types of spiritual understanding mentioned previously.</note> come into harmony, that which was previously closed in the Holy Scriptures is opened, its bolts having been unlocked. Moreover, the book remains open in the hand of the Angel because it remains in the power of those to whom it is given to show the faithful what is contained in the book. This is so that no one, trusting in their own strength, should presume anything without the gift of grace, and that one wishing to know high things might unlearn how to think humbly. And what follows from this?

<margin>Luke 14</margin>
"Everyone," he says, "who exalts himself shall be humbled, just as, conversely, he who humbles himself shall be exalted." For the one who provides the gift is powerful enough to increase virtue, so that the greater someone is in the house of God, the more humbly they think of themselves. Otherwise, it is better not to presume anything, lest perhaps one becomes a heretic by asserting falsehood, or becomes incorrigible through pride. But those who have received the gift return the "money" <note>A reference to the Parable of the Talents.</note>—even the unjust ones, fearing that sentence by which it was said to the wicked and lazy servant:

<margin>Matthew 22</margin>
"Bind his hands and feet and cast him into the outer darkness." Now, how those who teach the truth should teach is demonstrated in the action of this Angel when it says: *He placed his right foot upon the sea, but his left upon the earth.* In the Divine Page <term>Divine Page; a traditional way of referring to the Holy Scriptures</term>, "sea" and "earth" have different meanings depending on the places in which they are written. Here, however, the New Testament is understood by the "sea," and the Old Testament by the "earth." The latter was given to earthly men and those who savor earthly things, while the former was given to the wise and those capable of walking through the depths of the Holy Scriptures.

<column-break/>

The Angel placed his feet upon the sea and upon the earth because the spiritual understanding of a teacher—who wishes to bring forth the truth hidden in the Divine Page—leans upon the literal words of the two testaments (as if upon the roots of a certain tree). Thus, it may bear spiritual fruit all the more highly as it is planted in good soil, and being watered frequently, it endures in greenness. For what is the "greenness" of Christ if not faith? And where is faith better sought than where "two or three witnesses" agree on the same point? "By the mouth," says the Lord, "of two or three witnesses every word shall stand." And it is well that he placed his right foot on the sea and his left on the earth; for just as the younger Ephraim, touched by the right hand, was preferred over Manasseh, who was touched by the left, so the New Testament (though it was later in time) was made first in dignity. As the Lord said regarding the elect of both times:

<margin>Joshua 4</margin>
<margin>Matthew 20</margin>
"The last shall be first, and the first last." Therefore, in the "earth," which is the lower element, the letter of the Old Testament is designated; in the "sea," the letter of the New Testament; and in the rainbow <note>original: "vri"</note> which appears in the clouds of heaven, the spiritual understanding <term>spiritualis intellectus; the deeper, allegorical meaning beyond the literal text</term> which proceeds from both. This is why the two feet of the Angel are like pillars of fire, and his face is like the Sun. Namely, because the sense and knowledge of the two testaments occupy the lower positions, as it were, while the contemplation of spiritual Wisdom remains in the higher things. But why is the book shown to be open under the sounding of the Sixth Angel's trumpet, if not so that what preceded in mystery on the day Christ suffered might be fulfilled? On that day, the veil of the Temple was torn from top to bottom, and the tombs (as the Evangelist says) were opened, and many bodies of the Saints who had slept arose, and they came into the Holy City and appeared to many.

Wherefore it was perhaps said "Seal" in the sense of making a mark. Because, clearly, when we make a sign, we speak to our own people, not to foreigners, so that while our people understand, the others, having seen the sign, cannot track it. ### John, Third Part on the Apocalypse
S 4

<margin>Matthew 25</margin>
...to be understood as a specific moment of time: it must be carefully discerned whenever the Divine Page <note>original: "diuina Pagina", a common medieval term for the Bible</note> speaks of the last day: whether it is spoken of as a single period of time, or as the final moment of that same time, in which the Lord, sitting on the throne of his majesty, will bring an end to that same judgment, the elect going into eternal life, but the reprobate into eternal fire. For that passage of Peter (which we mentioned above) is not to be understood regarding that judgment or that moment of time: <margin>1 Peter 4</margin> "it is time for judgment to begin from the house of God"; rather, it is about the beginning of that time which Augustine says is called the "last day." But when we accept "the last day" in this way, we ought to consider the last day itself to be the last—that is, the seventh—age. For just as the seventh day is the end of the week, so the last age, however long its span may be, is the end of the world. And although the <term>sixth age</term><note>In traditional Christian chronology, the sixth age of the world began with the birth of Christ and continues until the end of time.</note> (as we have already set forth above in the preface) is called the end of the world, yet this can be said far more truly of the seventh; which, although it began in some sense from the Passion of the Lord simultaneously with the sixth, its proper character nevertheless begins from the ruin of Antichrist. That time is called the day of judgment because God will avenge his elect upon all their enemies: because the Kingdom will be taken away from the sons of this world, and will be given to the people <margin>Daniel 7</margin> of the Saints of the most high. But that matter remains entirely hidden until now: whether in the beginning of that time (of which Augustine speaks here), or in the middle, or at the end, the Lord will come to judgment; <margin>Luke 12</margin> especially since he himself says: "In the hour that you do not think, the Son of Man will come." That is: whether at evening, or at midnight, or in the morning. For he is coming <margin>Mark 13</margin> (as Scripture testifies) and will settle <margin>Luke 16</margin> accounts with his servants: taking away the talent from the lazy servant, and giving it to him who doubled the money. According to this, however, it can be presumed that he will come either around the beginning of that time, or not far from its beginning: especially since Truth itself says, speaking of the persecution of Anti-

For who understands that which follows in the same place: "And he will send his Angels with a trumpet and a loud voice: and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from the heights of the heavens even to their ends"? Is it really (as the simplicity of the letter seems to suggest) to be understood so simply: that he sends his Angels with <margin>Matthew 24</margin> trumpets for the purpose of collecting the souls of the elect, when on the contrary it is written in the <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> Apostle Paul: "We shall all indeed rise again, but we shall not all be changed: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet"?
