# Abbot’s Part of the Exposition

<margin>Genesis</margin>
...and joined with the nations, they persecute the church together with them. Indeed, in respect to the sea, the church of the elect is designated as being on the land, as it is written: *Let the waters that are under the heaven be gathered together into one place, and let the dry land appear.* <note>original: "Congregentur aque que sub celo sunt in locum vnum: & appareat arrida" — Genesis 1:9.</note> Therefore, just as sometimes in heaven the faithful people are designated, and in the abyss the unfaithful, so sometimes on the land the faithful people are designated, just as the unfaithful are in the sea. This is surely because the sea always fluctuates, and to one passing through it, it promises death rather than life; but the earth, since it is stable, brings forth green grass and fruit-bearing trees according to their kind. 

Nevertheless, just as in Genesis it is openly reported that the floodgates of heaven opened and from them pestilential waters descended upon the earth—acting as a type <term>type: a biblical person or event that foreshadows a future one</term> of the false prophets who fall from the bosom of the church—so also here, after that terrible beast which came out of the sea, another even more wicked beast is said to come out of the land. That is, a beastly crowd of false prophets will go out from the church. Just as in the past waters came from two directions <note>A reference to the Great Flood in Genesis 7:11, where water came from both the "fountains of the great deep" (sea/earth) and the "windows of heaven."</note> to punish the sinners of the earth, so here, to do that same thing, two most immense and exceedingly terrible beasts are reported to come from two directions: namely, from the sea and from the land. For it follows:

<margin>Genesis</margin>
<margin>chapter 7.</margin>
**And I saw another beast ascending from the earth: and it had two horns similar to a lamb.** <note>Revelation 13:11.</note>

<margin>Daniel</margin>
He says "another" because of the one he had previously said ascended from the sea. Just as in Daniel, the male goat signifies a kingdom rather than a single person, so also in this place, the beast that ascends from the land by no means designates any single person, but rather a sect or some kingdom. That the sect of false prophets is to be understood by this beast ascending from the land, the author of the book [John] himself clearly demonstrates, for he calls this very beast the "false prophet" in the following sections. Since this is clear, it seems quite wonderful <note>In this context, "wonderful" (mirabile) means strange or astonishing.</note> who those two wicked ones will be who are to be understood in the two horns similar to the lamb, since it is clear from many places in Scripture that the persons of men are designa-

<column-break/>

-ted in the horns of some beast. 

But there is a great difference between the horns of a lamb and those of other beasts that have horns. For the horns of certain beasts or animals are sharp and rigid and ready for striking; but the horns of a sheep are curved, holding nothing of terror or suspicion in themselves. But our Lamb [Christ], who took away the sins of the world, is said to have seven horns, because seven men were sent through different times, whom we mentioned in the first part of the book. Two of these were especially meant to be sent to prepare His paths: namely, John [the Baptist] and Elijah. But also two were seen together with Christ on the mountain—that is, Moses and Elijah—and now two are expected to come: namely, Enoch and Elijah. <note>Medieval tradition held that Enoch and Elijah never died and would return to earth to preach against the Antichrist.</note> 

Therefore, let him who fears to be deceived or seduced take notice subtly; being circumspect on all sides, let him examine things on the right and on the left. The author of guile [the Devil] is indeed a great imitator, so that he can fashion certain works that are mockery, whether to deceive the unwary by them or to appear similar to the Creator. For because the Lord found for Himself David to reign in Jerusalem, the city which He chose, he [the Devil] found Nebuchadnezzar to reign in Babylon and to be a persecutor of Jerusalem all the days of his life. Because the Lord redeemed the human race through His Christ, that one [the Devil] will act through the Antichrist, whom he will fill with lies. For just as God is the Almighty of truth, so he [Satan] is (as the Lord says) the father of lies; he will devastate everything beyond what can be believed. 

Therefore, let every faithful person watch themselves and be always solicitous and circumspect, lest perhaps the one who knows the faithful are prepared to receive Enoch and Elijah—whom the teachers predicted would come—should himself find and send ahead a false Enoch and a false Elijah. These are the "two horns similar to a lamb," the masters of the beastly crowd, about whom the Lord deigned to forewarn His disciples, saying: *Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.* <note>Matthew 7:15.</note> Furthermore, I say this not because I am certain, but so that we may be circumspect in all things and suffer shipwreck in nothing. What we say seems plausible; and therefore, just as we cannot confirm it with authority...

->The Fourth Part of the [Commentary on the] Apocalypse of John<-

...just as we lack the power to establish it by authority, we likewise lack the power to destroy it. Concerning what is merely "likely," it does not possess certain authority; it remains to be held as suspect and under caution until it is proven by the outcome of the event. There is also another matter in this section that must be guarded against no less diligently than the first: lest perhaps those very true witnesses who are to come—coming as God knows best—might be judged to be liars by men, and that instead assent might be given to those who truly are liars. Therefore, it is by no means easy for anyone to be certain in such a moment of great necessity how to discern between the true and the false: namely, between Moses and <margin>Exodus</margin> Aaron on one side, and Jannes and Mambres <note>Jannes and Mambres are the traditional names given to the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses in Pharaoh's court.</note> on the other, because of the extreme similarity of their wicked works. For the Lord says: *False Christs and false prophets will arise, and they will give signs and wonders to seduce (if it were possible) even the elect.* <note>original: "Surgent pseudo xpi: & pseudo prophete: & dabunt signa & pdigia ad seducendos (si fieri possit) etiam electos" — Matthew 24:24.</note> 

There is, however, another thing that is even more moving. It is certain that many things have already come into the light under the New Testament which formerly lay hidden, cloaked in shadows. Similarly, in the future, many things will be made plain which until now and even until the end are either only partially known or entirely unknown. Who then would boast that he fully knows the hidden counsels of God? Who among the Jewish people would have ever believed they would be disappointed regarding the coming of Elijah <note>original: "Helye"</note>, when it was not that Elijah they expected who came, but another? <note>A reference to John the Baptist coming in the "spirit and power of Elijah" (Luke 1:17) rather than the literal prophet returning from heaven as many Jews expected.</note> If indeed there will not be something similar to this, who do you think knows in what order those messengers are to come? Suppose that tomorrow Enoch were to come to your door and testify that he is indeed Enoch. Why should we believe him? If he shows signs, heretics will also do unheard-of things. If he shows religious devotion, they will do the same. If he uses subtle words, they will do no less. And so, it is added here:

### And he spoke like a dragon.
Indeed, he will speak like a dragon because, being filled beyond measure with the dragon's cunning, he will pour out words that are seemingly <margin>Exodus</margin> spiritual and likely, even more than one might think. For Moses (who signifies the true teachers) turned a rod into a dragon <note>original: "draconem" — usually translated as "serpent" in Exodus 7:10.</note>—that is, he turned the letter [of the Law], which is as if dead, into a living spirit; but the false prophets will do the same. For they too will speak mystical things, which will seem to the unlearned to have nothing less 

<column-break/>

than divine weight, so much so that even the learned <margin>Saint [Paul]</margin> might fall. Nevertheless, the rod of Moses devoured the rods of the magicians because the true wisdom of Christ, which the elect shall speak in His name, will show the wisdom of those men to be false. As the Apostle says: *Just as Jannes and Mambres resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth—men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith; but they shall proceed no further. For their folly shall be manifest to all, as was that of the others.* <note>original: "Quemadmodum Jamnes & Mambres restiterunt Moysi... Inspiētia enim eoz manifesta erit oibus" — 2 Timothy 3:8-9.</note> Therefore, there will be this and many other signs by which they can be distinguished. 

But blessed is he who, while there is still a little light in us, strives by the works of light and purity of soul to please God, so that the darkness does not seize him, fearing greatly that terrifying sentence: *Blind the heart <margin>Isaiah</margin> of this people, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest perhaps they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.* <note>original: "Obceca cor populi huius... & sanem eum" — Isaiah 6:10.</note> If indeed the just and pious God permits these things to happen because of the sins of the people—and it is certain that many are to be deceived—why should a man not fear lest he be deceived by those whom God, in His wrath, will suffer to deceive many? For whom would Jannes and Mambres not deceive, <margin>Exodus</margin> performing signs and wonders with their incantations similar to those of Moses and Aaron? For just as Jannes and Mambres acted in the presence of Pharaoh, and just as Simon Magus <note>A magician mentioned in Acts 8 who, in later tradition, challenged St. Peter in Rome before the Emperor Nero.</note> acted in the sight of Nero and his army, so the false prophets will perform signs in the sight of that eleventh king mentioned in Daniel and his army, before that multitude of which we spoke above. This is clearly revealed when it is added:

### And he exercised all the power of the former beast <margin>Chapter 13</margin> in his sight.
He will surely do these things in the sight of the beast and its king, but there is something here that ought to be noted. For he does not say simply "he exercised power," but adding to the word "power" he says "of the former beast," showing clearly that he will perform signs by the power of the first beast. But what is meant by these ambiguities...

If this is so, what belongs to the power of the beast and the false prophet—or rather, the swarm of false prophets acting in the presence of the beast—is to perform signs. Perhaps it will be their task to preach and perform miracles, perhaps by some other art of sorcery, so that either the beast itself is amazed at what they do, or—which is more likely—because they come out from the heart of the church and know the language and customs of Christians, that pagan ferocity <note>Referring to the Antichrist's secular, non-Christian power.</note> will judge them more fit and useful for deceiving the faithful. # Fourth Part of Joachim on the Apocalypse

<margin>All</margin> [that] has emerged from the sea: this entirely agrees with the sixth vision of Daniel, in which he deals with the four beasts emerging from the great sea. Likewise, this second [beast] which ascends from the earth agrees with his seventh vision, in which he deals with the **male goat**; <note>Joachim is referencing Daniel 7 and 8, where Daniel sees symbolic animals representing world empires.</note> except that there, in the first beast, an eleventh king is shown to be about to reign, who will think he can change times and laws. In the second, there is another of whom it is written: *beyond what can be believed, he shall lay all things waste.* <note>original: "Quod supra q̃z credi poteſt: vniuerſa vaſtabit" — a reference to the "king of bold countenance" in Daniel 8:24.</note> Here, neither in the first nor in the second is mention made of any specific king, except that in this fourth part, solemn mention is made of the **dragon** having seven horns, which signify seven kings. And in the sixth part, it is spoken of the two final kings: *one is, and one has not yet come; and when he comes, it is necessary for him to remain a short time,* <note>original: "unus est & unus nondum venit" — Revelation 17:10.</note> so that it may be aptly understood that these are the two kings written of in the two visions of the prophet Daniel.

But why two kings, when the Dragon himself is one? Is it not because, in the pattern of the one Christ coming for the redemption of the human race and coming for judgment, two persons are accustomed to be anointed in the church of God: one as king, the other as priest? <note>Joachim refers to the medieval concept of "the two swords"—secular and spiritual authority.</note> Indeed, is the priest himself not more truly a king, since he is a king of souls? And can both not be called "the Lord's Anointed," since God is both man and king? 

So here it seems likely that just as that beast which ascends from the sea is to have a certain great king of its sect who is similar to <margin>Antipope</margin> **Nero**, <note>Nero was the Roman Emperor famous for the first major persecution of Christians; here he represents the archetype of the secular tyrant.</note> and is as it were the emperor of the whole world—so the beast which ascends from the earth is to have a certain great prelate, who is similar to **Simon Magus**, <note>Simon Magus (Simon the Sorcerer) was a biblical figure who tried to buy spiritual power; in the Middle Ages, he became the archetype of the false religious leader or heretic.</note> and is as it were a universal priest in the whole world. And he himself is that **Antichrist** of whom Paul says that *he is exalted and opposed above all that is called God or that is worshipped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as if he were God.* <note>original: "extollitur & aduerſatur ſupra oẽ qđ dĩ deus" — 2 Thessalonians 2:4.</note> 

Wherefore, not without reason, where it is said of him in Daniel: *A king of bold countenance shall rise, and shall understand riddles, and his strength shall be strengthened*—it is added—*but not by his own power.* <note>original: "Surget rex impudens facie... ſed non in viribus ſuis" — Daniel 8:23-24.</note> Because, namely: just as Simon Magus did not persecute the apostles by his own power, but by the power of Nero, so also this one [will act] in the power

<column-break/>

of that eleventh King; and beyond what can be believed, he shall devastate the universe. 

And perhaps he will not go to that King by himself from the beginning, but will send to him his two principal prophets, who may perform signs in his presence and say they have a prince by whom they were sent. Nevertheless, some of the teachers call that eleventh king the "Antichrist," just as they do the one who is called **Gog**. <note>Gog is a prophetic figure from Ezekiel and Revelation representing the final enemies of God's people.</note> However, this seems true to me because there is one dragon, but many heads; and the malice which he does not <margin>Many antichrists.</margin> complete in one Antichrist, he will complete in another. And whichever of them is worse, he is the one to be called the "Great Antichrist." 

And so much for that. But as for what is said of this beast that had two horns like a lamb: *it performed great signs, so that it made fire descend from heaven to earth in the sight of men.* I think this is said because fire is a living and shining thing, and "heaven" designates the life of the saints. Thus, they may be <margin>Matthew</margin> thought to be so similar [to the truth] that, if it were possible, even the elect might be led into error. <note>original: "in errorem inducantur: ſi fieri poſſit etiam electi" — a reference to Matthew 24:24.</note> For even the elect will stumble because of them. And if, according to <margin>Daniel</margin> what is written in Daniel, *some of the learned shall fall,* <note>original: "De eruditis ruent" — Daniel 11:35.</note> what must be thought of the weak multitude of the common people, who do not know how to discern between the true and the false? Wherefore it is immediately added:

> <margin>Chapter 13</margin>
> **And he will seduce those dwelling on the earth because of the signs which were given to him to perform in the sight of the beast: saying to those dwelling on the earth, that they should make an image of the beast, which had the wound of the sword and lived.**

The "image of the beast which had the wound of the sword and lived" is to be considered some **special tradition** <note>Joachim suggests the "image" isn't just a statue, but a "tradition" or political system created to honor the Antichrist's power.</note> which the false prophets will compose in memory of the beast itself, saying that this is that kingdom which is to remain forever, seeing that it, coming even to its fall, deserved to reach such a summit of glory.

# Explanation of the Abbot, Part Four

...after the fall. Concerning this—namely the image—what follows is truly terrifying.

<margin>verse 11</margin>
**And it was granted to him to give breath to the image of the beast, and that the image of the beast should speak.**
¶ The image of the beast will receive breath when the evil spirit is present in that same diabolical operation to perform false signs. <note>Joachim interprets the "breath" of the image not as true life, but as the presence of a "malignant spirit" enabling deceptive miracles.</note> It will speak when those signs begin to occur and, once performed, reach the knowledge of many. It is shown that this sect will possess great power—granted by the just but rigorous judgment of God—when it is added:

<margin>verse 12</margin>
**And he will cause whoever does not worship the image of the beast to be killed.**
¶ This is what is spoken of concerning the eleventh horn in the Book of Daniel: *And he shall wear out the saints of the Most High.* <note>original: "Et sanctos altissimi cōteret" — Daniel 7:25. The "eleventh horn" is a traditional figure for the Antichrist.</note> These will be the accusers, and those will be the killers. These will set the traps, and those will take the prey. It follows:

<margin>Daniel</margin>
<margin>verse 13</margin>
**And he will cause all, small and great, rich and poor, free and slave, to have a mark on their right hand or on their foreheads; and that no one may buy or sell except he who has the mark of the beast, or its name, or the number of its name.**
¶ If the beast signifies the multitude of persecutors themselves, the image signifies its most wicked tradition. What is meant by the "mark" <term>mark: Latin 'caracter', referring to a brand or identifying seal of ownership</term> but some writing or edict of his commands? Likewise, by the "name," the glory of the beast itself; and by the "number of the name," the multitude of its crimes? In times of persecution, the small usually fail out of weakness, while the great act manfully and persist strenuously in the struggle. The rich of the world usually spare their pleasures <note>Meaning they compromise to keep their wealth.</note>, but the poor offer themselves willingly for martyrdom. Slaves usually despise their own condition,

<column-break/>

but the free look to their nobility, at least so they do not seem to cloud their famous lineage with infamy. The affliction of this tribulation will be so great—and what is worse, the deception of signs—that nearly the whole of the people may be led into error; on one side, threats of torture threaten punishment, and on the other, miracles persuade them toward the sect. In these words, therefore, I think nothing else is designated than that we should know the multitude of those to be damned is infinite: from every condition, age, and size, so vast that it can by no means be estimated. Truly, whoever refuses to adore this image will be killed, according to what was said above: *He who kills with the sword must be killed with the sword.* <note>Revelation 13:10.</note> The "sellers" are the preachers. The "buyers" are those who hear and receive the word. For the former offer life, while the latter expend good works. The former provide the word of salvation; the latter repay with themselves and whatever they possess. Yet in those days it will not be permitted [to buy or sell], because no one will dare to preach, or hear a preacher, except one destined for punishment and death; unless power in this area is granted to those about whom there is no suspicion—those who are truly servants of the Beast and disciples of the Antichrist. And what will be the sign? To have the mark on the right hand or on the foreheads, or the name of the beast, or the number of its name. Concerning this number, it is immediately added:

**Here is wisdom: let him who has understanding calculate the number of the beast. For it is the number of a man; and its number is six hundred sixty-six.**
¶ The human intellect is eager to grasp what it does not know; yet, for reasons I cannot immediately say, once it has recognized what it desired, it promptly despises it. For if Holy Scripture revealed everything at once, it would become cheap in the eyes of wicked and proud men because of its disclosure. Therefore, whoever desires to be made worthy to reach the knowledge of what he does not know, let him strive to cherish the charity <note>original: "chaz", abbreviation for "charitatem". The author suggests that spiritual love/charity is the prerequisite for understanding deep prophecy.</note> which he already knows; so that he who invited him, seeing his devotion, may say to him: *Friend, move up higher.* <note>original: "Amice: ascēde superius" — Luke 14:10.</note> Certainly

## Johannes, Part Four: On the Apocalypse
*y*

...ly. Certainly, he who has understanding is commanded to calculate the number of the name of the beast. Do you ask this of me? Perhaps I would give you what you seek, if the name itself were present, the power of which you wish to know. But if its name has not been revealed, how can there be understanding in a matter where the literal spelling is unknown? For it is as if understanding were sought in a future vision—which is entirely absurd—as if the narration of the vision should not rather be awaited, so that he who has understanding might interpret it, not before its time, but in its own time. Therefore, the revelation of this name must be awaited until the proper time, and then it will be permitted for him who has understanding to calculate the number. For it must first be known how that number matches the name according to the literal characters, so that the spiritual understanding which follows is not, as it were, empty.

Otherwise, if we are compelled to go ahead and reveal the power of the number in some way, we know that the number six encompasses temporal things, and only those things in which the children of this world rejoice. These are the people whose way of life is on the earth, who call those people fools who despise present things for the sake of the future, and who hope for invisible things instead of visible ones. And its number (it says), which is expressed in its name, is six hundred and sixty-six. Why this? Because this number signifies the totality of secular times <margin>Adam.</margin>—that is, from Adam until the end of this beast, which will be in the times of the Antichrist. 

Indeed, **six hundred** signifies the six ages of the world, in which this beast reigned in its members from the beginning of time. <note>The "six ages of the world" is a traditional Christian historical framework, roughly corresponding to the millennia from Creation to the birth of Christ.</note> **Sixty** signifies the six periods of this sixth age, in which, having received a certain special power from the dragon, it persecuted the church of God more fiercely. **Six** signifies the time of that eleventh horn—that is, forty-two months: specifically, seven-month periods <note>original: "septem menses." The author appears to be dividing the biblical 42 months of the Antichrist's reign into six sub-periods of seven months each to fit the numerology of 666.</note>—under which his fury will blaze forth beyond measure and beyond what can be said. Without a doubt, this fury is kindled by that ancient dragon, who knows very well that he has only a little time. Therefore, in the **six hundred**, it encompasses all that pertains to the six ages of the world; in the **sixty**, it specifies that part which pertains to the sixth age; and in the **six**, the sixth

<column-break/>

period of this sixth age, in which that eleventh horn is to reign—that is, *a time, and times, and half a time.* <note>A reference to Daniel 7:25 and 12:7, traditionally interpreted as three and a half years.</note> 

Now since this is so: what is it that the power of selling or buying does not grant except to him who carries the mark of the beast on his right hand or on his forehead, or the name, or the number of its name, except that those will be judged worthy and faithful who, commending only temporal things, mock and sneer at those who promise eternal ones? For those who despair of themselves, so that they do not see the light of heaven—whom can they love except desperate men? For those who are on its side appear to carry the mark of the beast, or the name, or the number of the name, on their right hand or on their forehead, because it is not enough if they do this with sadness or out of necessity, unless in the very thing they do, they show themselves cheerful and manifest, saying with a clear voice in their assemblies: "If this kingdom were not from God, it could not do anything. Therefore, those who resist it, resist the ordinance of God." 

For to carry the mark of the beast, the name, or the number of its name on the right hand or on the forehead is either to show a joyful face in beastly work according to what is contained in its writings, or to preach this very thing publicly in their meetings, or certainly to magnify the power of the beast, or not to blush at any crime and delight in sin. For these are the only things the dragon demands from his soldiers. 

But these things are said according to the spirit, and according to what some conjecture can exist in a future thing. For he has not yet been revealed <margin>Daniel</margin>—the one who will think that he can change times and laws, to be delivered into his hand for *a time, and times, and half a time.* But when this begins to be fulfilled, then the actual event will make the understanding clear. 

As for what is said—*for it is the number of a man*—in certain codices one finds *of a name.* And since he had already said above, "except he who has the mark, or the number of its name," it forces us to doubt whether, by a scribe's error, it was altered—either "of the name" into "of a man," or "of a man" into "of a name"—which there is no doubt could have happened through the similarity of the words. <margin>The Greeks.</margin> On this point, the Greeks should also be consulted...

## Abbot’s Commentary: Part of the Exposition

...at least from their own books: let certainty stand firm. In the meantime: if the truth belongs to man, it pertains well enough to the matter: because whatever is worldly belongs to man more than to God, and the number six <note>original: "senarius numerus," referring to the number 6 or a grouping of six.</note> pertains more to him, which is the proper number of labor: for on the sixth day man was created, and soon his labor followed—which, however, worldly men take up as if it were rest. For nothing is more laborious to them than leisure, and nothing is more leisurely than labor <note>A paradoxical way of saying that worldly people find spiritual rest "hard work" but find worldly toil easy or fulfilling.</note>. Such is the sense of the flesh, such is the sense of those who rejoice in carnal things. Wherefore it is also said through the prophet: *Egypt is man, and not God; its horses are flesh and not spirit* <note>original: "Egyptus hō: ꝛ non deus: eq eius caro ꝛ nō spiritus," quoting Isaiah 31:3.</note>. Egypt indeed is man, and not God: because the glory of this world is transitory, not eternal; its strength is like the morning dew passing away. Therefore this number—which pertains to the course of the world through a mystery—is the number of man: because in truth, those who choose temporal things for themselves are "men" <note>In this context, "men" implies those who are merely mortal and worldly, as opposed to "divine" or spiritual beings.</note>, not of God, according to that word of the Psalmist:

<margin>Psalms</margin>
*Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail: let the nations be judged in your sight; and let the nations know that they are but men.* <note>Quoting Psalm 9:19-20.</note> This Psalm (as I think) specifically looks to that time in which the "man of sin" <note>The Antichrist.</note> shall reign; whom the Lord Jesus (even if he permits him to prevail for a time), being at last moved by the prayers of the Church, shall arise in wrath against him; and having judged those who are on his side, he shall subject the remnants of the Jews and the Gentiles to his scepter. Therefore, the men who follow the "man" [the Antichrist] say these things, bearing his mark <note>original: "caracterem," referring to the Mark of the Beast.</note> on their foreheads, glorying in transitory things because they do not know eternal honor, preferring the gifts of the world because they do not know the rewards of the heavens. Let the wretched ones hear, therefore—those who are soothed by the gifts of the beast, who are led so far as to follow it and wear its mark written on their foreheads. Let them hear against whom and what kind of people they are judged as opposites: namely, those who, led by the Spirit, despise all temporal things; who, so that they might perfectly please God, have learned to abstain even from those things which are lawful. The former, indeed, stay for a time with the beast by the rivers of Babylon, not weeping, but feasting. The latter stay there upon Mount Zion with the Lamb, singing a new song, from now and forevermore. But why a "new song," unless because just as the former decided to walk and live in the oldness of the first man [Adam], so the latter live in the newness of Him who descended from heaven? Thus, they are contrary to the commands of the beast in all things; and since they are set in opposition, just as the former precede all other sinners to punishment, so the latter surpass and precede many righteous ones to glory. For there are some within the holy church who, even if they do not give up their own property for God, nonetheless do not wish to take the property of others through theft or force against God's command. And this is often a good thing. It is even found among the gentiles. But between the ministers of Christ and the servants <note>original: "domesticos," literally members of the household.</note> of the beast, the matter is conducted in total opposition: as if they were dividing the regions of the North and the South between them <note>In medieval allegory, the North (Aquilo) represents the Devil and coldness, while the South (Auster) represents the Holy Spirit and warmth.</note>, the former desert all their own property, while the latter steal what belongs to others; the former flee marriage <note>A reference to clerical celibacy or monasticism.</note>, while the latter commit adulteries without discretion. And to catch it all in one point: the former choose everything that pertains to a living hope; the latter, on the contrary, pursue whatever is wicked and desperate. Therefore, the former have the name of Christ written on their foreheads, because they strive to preach this by their conduct and life; the others have the name of the beast, because they serve beastly works. I say these [the righteous] chose the inner parts of the South, while the others chose the deepest parts of the North: because just as the former adhere to their King, so the latter adhere with their whole heart to the red dragon—so that just as the former are first on the walls of Babylon, so the latter are on the walls of Jerusalem. And while the former gnash their teeth over all who descend into the pit, the latter sing a "new song" which no one else is permitted to sing. ### John’s Fourth Part on the Apocalypse
#### Z 2

...especially from that place where it is said: *And the wound of his sword was healed* <note>original: "Et plaga gladij eius curata est," referring to Revelation 13:3.</note>: these things are not to be referred to the fourth time, which is presently being discussed, but to the time of the Antichrist. Nor is it strange if, in the fourth part of the book—stretching from the year 185 <note>The text uses "C. lxxxv" likely denoting 185 AD, a common periodization in Joachite chronology.</note> until the time of the Antichrist—the whole time of the Church is comprehended. This is seen in the "woman clothed with the sun" who remained in the wilderness for "a time, and times, and half a time," whose offspring are these holy virgins; or in the red dragon and the beast having seven heads. This is because in the remaining parts of the book, this consideration remains almost uniform. 

I say these things for this reason: lest by the occasion of the words interspersed regarding the beast and the false prophet, it should seem forgotten that this fourth part—and the fourth distinction of this fourth part—is dealing with the **Virgins and Hermits**. This was the primary reason why the terrible beast was discussed in this fourth part of the book: namely, because the **fourth beast**, which signifies the race of the Saracens <note>original: "Agarenoꝝ" (Agarenes), a medieval term for Saracens, referring to their traditional descent from Hagar.</note>, rose up in the fourth time of the Church against the hermits and virgins. 

It is not that this was the only general cause, but just as the holy Apostles bore the battles specifically of the Jews; the holy Martyrs, those of the Pagans; and the holy Doctors, those of the Arians; so the holy hermits and virgins sustained the greater weight of the Saracens. This is both because they destroyed the cities in which they lived, and because they treated them so cruelly, roaming through the deserts like Arabs. Therefore, the cause or occasion for treating the beast in this fourth part was this. 

First, the dragon wanted to devour the son of the virgin; second, he had a battle with Michael and his angels; third, he pursued the woman; fourth, he went away to make war with the rest of her offspring—that is, with the virgins leading a hermetic or monastic life. Having said these things, he began to introduce the order of the battle. For he said that he saw a beast ascending from the sea. Why? Because just as the Church generally begins from Mary, the mother of the Lord, it is not consummated except in the "fullness of the nations." Therefore, the woman was said to remain in the wilderness for one thousand two hundred and sixty days. 

Yet, her special glory shone forth in the fourth time. Likewise, this beast—taking its origin from the first persecutor Herod, or even from Herodias, the adulteress of the other Herod—is directed toward the goal of that same time. In this goal, the time of the aforementioned woman going into the wilderness is completed. For the same number is granted to the beast as to the holy woman: that is, forty-two months. Nevertheless, in the fourth time, both the glory of the woman and the ferocity of the beast were increased, so that the darkness of the prince of shadows might cover the earth even more as the light of justice increased in the bosom of the holy Church. 

As for what is added: *I saw one of his heads as if slain to death* <note>original: "Vidi vnum de capitibus eius quasi occisum ad mortem," quoting Revelation 13:3.</note>, and the rest that follows, this is to be referred to the sixth time of the Church. That is why in certain "sixth chapters" of some parts of this book—and generally in the sixth part—that which could have been omitted concerning the struggle of this beast in this part is repeated, so that it might be grasped more firmly the more the discourse is repeated in similar places. 

Therefore, in the fourth time, the hermetic and virginal order sustained the weight of the struggle, even in the male sex; and for this reason, in the fourth distinction of this fourth part, the discourse is properly about the virgins. Concerning them, it is said: *And I saw, and behold, the Lamb standing upon Mount Zion, and with him one hundred forty-four thousand, having his name and the name of his Father written on their foreheads.*

<margin>A notable rule of the book</margin>
<margin>A general rule.</margin>
<margin>Mount Zion is the Church.</margin>
<margin>Ezekiel.</margin>

That Mount Zion signifies the Church can be doubted by no one. Upon this mountain stands the Son of God, like a king and lord of the kingdom, like an immaculate lamb with an immaculate army. It is written concerning the face of the "fourth living creature" in the prophet Ezekiel that it was above the four of them. He says: *As for the likeness of the faces of the living creatures, the face of a man and the face of a lion were on the right side of the four; and the face of an ox was on the left side of the four; and the face of an eagle was above the four of them.* <note>original: "facies agle desup ipsoꝝ q̃tuor," quoting Ezekiel 1:10.</note> Truly, the ascent of the Lord of higher times signifies the contemplative life, which is higher than the active life...

# Fourth Part of Joachim on the Apocalypse

The crowd of martyrs is innumerable to men; so also is the crowd of virgins believed to be innumerable. Just as in a finite number there is the highest equality, so also in the infinite: should the highest equality be held? But this is more quickly resolved if we weigh the <term>sacraments: sacred mysteries or symbolic meanings</term> and virtues of the two <term>orders: specific groups of the faithful, such as martyrs or monks</term>. For as I recall having already said in the introduction of this book, and as I have just mentioned slightly above: the two aforementioned apostles were chosen by the Lord from the very beginning of the divine preaching: **Peter** and **John**, as a <term>type: a symbolic person who represents a larger group or future reality</term> of those orders of which the present discourse speaks: namely, of the holy martyrs and the virgins. For Peter signifies the order of martyrs, and John the order of virgins; because one was a martyr, and the other was a virgin. Indeed, in the martyrs, **Christ**—who suffered for them—fights and conquers; but in the virgins—who are pure in mind and body—the **Holy Spirit**, who seeks such for his temple, rests more specially. 

If, however, the order of martyrs belongs by the property of its mystery to Christ, and the order of virgins to the Holy Spirit, the reasoning is fitting: why in this *second status* <note>Joachim’s "Second Status" refers to the Age of the Son (the era of the New Testament and the Church), while the "Third Status" is the coming Age of the Holy Spirit.</note> the sum of all martyrs is gathered, which no one can number. Of the virgins, however, it is not the same multitude, but only a part; because the order of martyrs, following Christ, will receive its completion with the second status of the world. But the order of virgins—which was begun in the type of the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father, simultaneously with the order of martyrs—was indeed begun at the commencement of the second status, but it will by no means be finished equally at the end of that same second status. Instead, in the type of the same Spirit proceeding from the Son, it will persevere whole until the end, as the Lord said in a type concerning **John**: *I want him to remain until I come* <note>original: "Sic eum volo manere donec veniam," from John 21:22</note>. Therefore, it was not necessary that under this second status an infinite multitude of virgins should be gathered in sum: because what is less completed regarding it in this second status will be completed in the third. Nevertheless, this itself is not devoid of the mystery of the city. For (as John says), the structure of its wall was of the stone **Jasper**. For Jasper is of a green color, and it signifies the integrity of faith which the holy martyrs had, in which they also conquered. Whence it is said to the same city through the

<column-break/>

prophet: *I will make your battlements of Jasper* <note>original: "Dabo Jaspidem propugnacula tua," referencing Isaiah 54:12</note>. For the saints conquered kingdoms through faith. But why was Jasper given as battlements? We know that battlements are located on the exterior part, so that while they resist the enemies and endure the blunt strikes of the stones thrown against them, whatever remains inside is kept unharmed. For that reason, those **one hundred and forty-four thousand** who are written in the second part to protect the interior of the city were placed like certain squared stones in the exterior part of the structure; but here, as many thousands are in the interior. Between both, however, is that multitude which no one could number for the completion of the structure, so that—excepting the interior face—the entire thickness of the wall appears to be of Jasper; lest those who are ordered in the exterior face alone should be unable to sustain the blows of the fighters. 

But if to these stones which are on the outside, through the legitimate action of the contest, so innumerable a multitude of others is joined to perfect the structure, will they be the only ones who persist in the interior face, so that they do not also have companions of infinite estimation who may advance in the structure? Far from it! They certainly have them too—those who advance in the structure of the city—lest it be thought void of the construction of houses, and rather so that it may be understood to belong to the innumerable multitude of virgins, that which was subsequently added: *The city itself was like pure gold, like clear glass* <note>original: "Ipsa vero similis auro mundo: simile vitro mundo," from Revelation 21:18</note>. For as the greenness of Jasper signifies the perfection of faith through which the holy martyrs conquered kingdoms, so the purity of gold, like clear glass, designates the perfection of **chastity** and **contemplation**. Surely, in a religious man, one is judged less useful without the other. (That is), if he is either not pure so as to be loved by God, or if he neglects to see God—who, unless he is seen and acknowledged, surely cannot be loved as is fitting. But how shall he see Him whom no one has ever seen? Without a doubt: with the eyes of the heart. For it is written: *Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God* <note>original: "Beati mundo corde: quoniam ipsi deum videbunt," from Matthew 5:8</note>. But why does it say "in heart," and not "in cor—" <note>The text cuts off mid-word as the page ends.</note>

He distinguishes between the "Second Status" (Age of the Son), which focuses on martyrs, and the "Third Status" (Age of the Spirit), which will bring the order of virgins to its full perfection.</summary>

# Joachim’s Fourth Part on the Apocalypse
-> Y 3 <-

The multitude of martyrs is innumerable to men; so too, the multitude of virgins is believed to be innumerable. Just as in a finite number there is a total equality, does a total equality also hold in the infinite? This is more quickly resolved if we weigh the <term>mysteries: Joachim uses "sacramenta" to mean hidden spiritual truths or symbols</term> and the virtues of these two <term>orders: specific categories of the faithful, such as the martyrs or the monastic virgins</term>. For, as I recall having already said in the introduction to this book, and as I mentioned a little earlier, two aforementioned apostles were chosen by the Lord from the very beginning of the Lord’s preaching: **Peter** and **John**. They serve as a <term>type: a symbolic figure or prophetic model</term> of these orders of which we are currently speaking: namely, the martyrs and the virgins. 

For **Peter** signifies the order of martyrs, and **John** the order of virgins, because one was a martyr and the other was a virgin. And indeed, in the martyrs, **Christ**—who suffered for them—fights and conquers; while in the virgins—who are pure in mind and body—the **Holy Spirit**, who seeks such people for His temple, rests in a more special way. If, however, the order of martyrs belongs by the property of its mystery to **Christ**, and the order of virgins to the **Holy Spirit**, there is a fitting reason why in this <term>second state: the current age of the Church, or the age of the Son</term> the total sum of all martyrs is gathered, which no one can number. 

But of the virgins, there is not an equal multitude, but only a part; because the order of martyrs, following **Christ**, will reach its consummation along with the end of the second state of the world. However, the order of virgins, which was begun in the type of the **Holy Spirit** proceeding from the **Father** at the same time as the order of martyrs (at the start of the second state), will by no means end at the conclusion of that same second state. Instead, in the type of that same **Spirit** proceeding from the **Son**, it will persevere whole until the end, as the Lord said in his <note>John's</note> type: *So I wish him to remain until I come.* <note>original: "Sic eum volo manere donec veniam" — John 21:22</note> Therefore, it was not necessary that the infinite multitude of virgins be gathered in total under this second state; for what is less completed of it in this second state will be completed in the <term>third [state]: the coming age of the Holy Spirit, characterized by monastic life and contemplation</term>. 

Yet even this does not lack the mystery of the City. For, as **John** says, the structure of its wall was of the stone **Jasper**. For Jasper is of a green color, and it signifies the integrity of faith which the holy martyrs held, and in which they also conquered. Whence also it is said to that same city through the

<column-break/>

prophet: *I will give Jasper for your bulwarks.* <note>original: "Dabo Jaspidem propugnacula tua" — cf. Isaiah 54:12</note> For the saints through faith conquered kingdoms. But why is Jasper given for bulwarks? We know that bulwarks are located on the exterior part, so that while they resist the enemies and endure the blows of the stones sent against them, whatever remains inside may be preserved unharmed. 

For that reason, those **one hundred and forty-four thousand** who are written about in the second part were placed like certain square stones in the exterior part of the structure to guard the interior of the city. Here, however, are just as many thousands in the interior. Between the two, truly, is that multitude which no one could number, for the completion of the structure; so that, except for the interior face, the entire thickness of the wall appears to be made of Jasper, lest those who are arranged on the exterior face alone might not be able to sustain the blows of the combatants. 

But if to these stones which are on the outside—because of the legitimate action of the struggle—such an innumerable multitude of others is joined to perfect the structure, will those alone be the ones who stand at the interior face of the wall, so that they themselves do not also have companions of infinite estimation who contribute to the structure? Far from it! They certainly have them too, those who contribute to the structure of the city, lest the fabric of the houses be thought empty; rather, it should be understood that what is added subsequently pertains to the innumerable multitude of virgins. 

*The city itself was like pure gold, like clear glass.* <note>Revelation 21:18</note> For just as the greenness of Jasper signifies the perfection of faith through which the holy martyrs conquered kingdoms, so the purity of gold like clear glass designates the perfection of chastity and <term>contemplation: the practice of deep spiritual prayer and "seeing" God with the mind</term>. Certainly, in a religious man, the one is judged less useful without the other. That is to say: if he is either not pure so as to be loved by God, or if he neglects to see God—whom, unless one sees and recognizes Him, one surely cannot love as is fitting. But how will he see Him whom no one has ever seen? Without doubt, with the eyes of the heart. For it is written: *Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.* <note>Matthew 5:8</note> But why does He say "in heart," and not "in the hear[t]"... <meta>catchword: non cor/</meta>

# The Abbot's Exposition: Part Four
-> Y 3 <-

...time? Just as purity of heart cannot be possessed without purity of the body, so too without purity of the heart, chastity of the body is nothing. Therefore, chastity of the heart is altogether necessary; and because it cannot be possessed without chastity of the body, the latter must be preserved for the sake of the former no less than the former itself—indeed, even more diligently by all means. 

It must be known that those 144,000 sealed <term>martyrs: those who died for their faith</term>, and these same thousands of virgins of whom we now speak, have the name of Christ and his Father on their foreheads. This is because they were not ashamed of the name of the Lord and the Gospel of Christ, but with free power and a revealed face, they preached it. They bore the name of God, rejoicing in the insults and reproaches they suffered for the name of Christ; what they once received in the <term>sacrament: <note>original: "sacramento"</note> likely referring to the seal of baptism or the sign of the cross</term> (when it was permitted), they fulfilled in their character and their voices. It follows:

<margin>Chapter 2</margin>
**And I heard a voice from heaven, like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of great thunder. And the voice I heard was like that of harpists playing on their harps.** <note>Revelation 14:2</note>

Waters, even if they are many, nevertheless produce a single voice. For rainwater falls from heaven with a sound, and likewise thunder. "Heaven" in this place designates the excellence of the <term>contemplative life: a life dedicated to prayer and meditation, away from worldly affairs</term> in which these saints dwelt; or it may designate the saints themselves, who above all others—having neglected earthly things—yearned only for heavenly ones. 

For when the spiritual words of spiritual men, along with the reputation of their holiness, resounded in the ears of men, does it not seem to you that it was even then fulfilled: *Their sound went out into all the earth*? <margin>Psalm 18</margin> <note>Psalm 19 in modern numbering</note> And for this reason, a voice was heard like the voice of great thunder. Why indeed, from that same voice, were the hearts of many men moved with remorse, so that most of them, having left the world, joined the <term>monastic communities: <note>original: "cenobiorum collegijs"</note> groups of monks living together</term>? Was it not

<column-break/>

as if a voice of waters was raining upon the field of the Church, preaching better through examples than through words? For a voice of exhortation sometimes stirs the worker, and when it rouses him by force, it wrests from him some fruit of good work. But when the life of the saints—and especially those who are present—is brought forward as an example, the heart is opened as if to hear a <term>harp: <note>original: "cytharam"</note> often used as a symbol for the harmony of the soul's virtues</term>, and like a certain sweet ringing, it strikes the soul of the listener with remorse.

Indeed, that new militia of saints was not small; by no means small was the voice that rose from their venerable reputation, but it was like the voice of many waters and of great thunder, and like harpists playing on their harps. The voice of other saints has been heard, great enough and manifold like this one, but it was not like harpists playing on their harps; instead, it was mostly weeping and wailing. For those converted from the vanity of the world perform <term>penance: acts of repentance to atone for sins</term> for their sins; they have a need to expiate their faults with weeping and to make satisfaction for their guilt with a mournful voice. 

But these, because they are virgins in both body and heart, and for this reason are also placed upon the mountain of the Lord—what can they sing, except from the songs of Zion? Therefore, whether this voice comes from them or is about them, it cannot be anything but joy, sweetness, and love; for what they feel within themselves, they pour out unceasingly in both words and examples. 

The angels are also like harpists, who continually praise their God, and that praise—on account of its great sweetness—is their perpetual food; and the very gifts of grace, signified by the harps, are their inheritance. "Like" (he says) "harpists playing on their harps." A harpist is accustomed to play not by compulsion, but willingly and exulting; for he is fed by the sound, and his food is not consumed, because that same sound flows continuously from his art like an unfailing spring—so long as the harpist, through his practiced skill, does not cease to strike the strings with hand and <term>plectrum: a small tool used to pluck or strum the strings</term>. But what are these strings, which are thus struck without intermission by a just man who holds to the purpose of chastity? When he had numbered many gifts of the Holy Spirit...

Joachim emphasizes that true chastity requires both physical and spiritual purity, which allows the soul to sing the "songs of Zion" like the angels.</summary>

[John’s Fourth Part on the Apocalypse]
-> Y 4 <-

...the apostle: and wishing to show an even more excellent way, after many things he had spoken, he added and said: *And now there remain: faith, hope, charity; these three; but the greatest of these is charity.* <note>original: "Manent autem: fides: fpes: charitas: tria hec: maior autem his eft charitas." (1 Corinthians 13:13)</note> Behold, these are the three strings by which the sound of joy is produced. For who truly rejoices without faith? Who is fruitfully glad without hope? Who wisely exults without charity? 

But these three cannot be possessed except in the "new man" <note>The "new man" is a Pauline concept (Ephesians 4:24) referring to a person renewed by Christ.</note> who says: *If anyone does not renounce all that he possesses, he cannot be my disciple.* <note>Luke 14:33</note> The hollowness of the harp, therefore, signifies voluntary poverty. For the string does not resonate well if the musical vessel itself is not concave. Likewise, one cannot perfectly possess those virtues, or their effect, unless the mind is empty of the desire for money. For it is written: *Where your treasure is, there also is your heart.* <note>Matthew 6:21</note> 

Hence, the holy virgins are said to sing as it were a "new song"; because although some holy men sang this same song before the coming of the Lord—such as <term>Elijah and Elisha: <note>Elijah and Elisha were Old Testament prophets often cited by medieval commentators as the first practitioners of celibacy and the monastic life.</note></term>—nevertheless, it was solemnly confirmed in Christ, and from that time those who would sound forth this new song began to be multiplied. And it is rightly added:

<margin>Chapter 3</margin>
### Before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders.

Because they do not sing before earthly kings and princes like the children of this world, but in the sight of all the sainted ones, who are designated either in the throne of God or in the <term>four living creatures: <note>The "animalia" or living creatures of Revelation 4:6-8, traditionally associated with the four Evangelists.</note></term> and in the sight of those who hold the places of the twenty-four elders on earth. Or perhaps it is because it shall be so at the consummation of the age, when all the ranks of the saints shall be gathered into one, and in the eternal blessedness of that heavenly homeland, they shall begin to keep the festival day. 

Nor should it seem absurd that he says "before the four living creatures," for the reason that the virgins themselves are known to belong to the fourth living creature; because spiritually that 

<column-break/>

fourth creature is that which is designated in the woman—that is, in the church of holy virgins—whose seed are these holy men. They, by a special privilege, sing that "new song" which others cannot sing; and because in the fourth living creature <note>The fourth creature, the Eagle, is often associated with St. John the Evangelist and the heights of spiritual contemplation.</note> may be included all who are true contemplatives, even those who, after a fall of the flesh, turn back to the Lord. These, however, have received something special which is attributed to the other multitude of saints. For it follows:

<margin>Chapter 4</margin>
### And no one could learn the song except those hundred and forty-four thousand who were redeemed from the earth.

Why? Because they alone received this as a gift. Other saints also have their own songs, as it is written: <margin>Psalm 83</margin> *Blessed are those who dwell in your house, O Lord; they will praise you forever.* <note>Psalm 84:4 in modern Bibles; Psalm 83 in the Vulgate.</note> Nevertheless, this special song is given to these alone as their own property. Otherwise, even in the female sex, how many virgins have been crowned! And yet this specific kind of song is not given to them, because not all virgins follow the Lamb wherever he goes in the same way as these holy men. For they did not receive this gift for virginity alone, but because in their mouth no lie was found. Indeed, John commends them for both gifts when he says:

<margin>Verse 5</margin>
### These are they who have not been defiled with women, for they are virgins. These follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These were redeemed from all as firstfruits to God and the Lamb, and in their mouth no lie was found: for they are without blemish before the throne of God.

-> Part of the Exposition <-

He who made all things from nothing, and who produces beautiful flowers from a beautiful tree, He himself has done this. Why do you wonder? Each person has his own gift from God: some in one way, and others in another. Therefore, He who bought us with his own blood and redeemed us from the power of the prince of darkness <note>original: "principe tenebrarum," a common medieval title for Satan.</note>, He himself bought these men from the earth, so that they might not think of anything earthly, and that they might be among the <term>firstfruits: <note>original: "primitiis." In biblical tradition, the firstfruits were the first part of the harvest dedicated to God; here it refers to the 144,000 as the elite of the redeemed.</note></term> of the other righteous ones, whose number is infinite. And it is blessed in the end. 

And in their mouth no lie was found: so that humility may be understood to be the <term>fortification: <note>original: "munimentum." A defensive wall or protection.</note></term> of virginity. For whoever attributes this gift of celibacy to himself is a liar, and he is as far removed from the number of the righteous through his pride as he thinks he is righteous because of his virginity. For without humility, he does not deserve the fellowship of the righteous. For how could it easily be said: *They are without blemish before the throne of God* <note>original: "Sine macula sunt ante thronum dei" (Revelation 14:5)</note>, if these follow the Lamb wherever He goes, if only the virginity of the flesh was what made them commendable? 

Some people attempt to apply these words to all the saints, and as if through a spiritual understanding, to attribute them to the whole church—as if there were not different <term>mansions: <note>original: "mansiones," referring to John 14:2, "In my Father’s house are many mansions," interpreted here as different levels of reward in heaven.</note></term> in the kingdom of heaven, and as if there were no difference between the married and the continent, between the continent and the virgins, and indeed between one virgin and another—between the one who is simply a virgin and the one who, along with virginity, has attained the great ornaments of the virtues. 

But lest the "rivalry of virginity" <note>An "emulatio," or holy competition to excel in virtue.</note> be dissolved by such an interpretation, Saint John does not simply say: *And they sang as if it were a new song*, but he adds: *Before the throne and the four living creatures and the elders*. This is so that some may be understood to be those who sing this special kind of song, while others are those before whom it is sung. This is especially so that the former may rejoice because something has been given to them that was not given to others; and the latter may rejoice because the singers are so worthy that they may stand in their very presence. Just as the number of these statements is true, so the number of 144,000 martyrs is true, and the same number of virgins, so that they may be like princes and leaders of that multitude which cannot be numbered. 

Enough has been said about these things for the time being. For it is necessary for us in some places to say less about the immensity of the things to be discussed, lest their too great breadth create narrowness for other things that must be said.

*And I saw another angel flying through the midst of heaven, having the eternal gospel, to preach to those sitting upon the earth, and over every nation, and tribe, and tongue, and people, saying with a loud voice: Fear God, and give him honor: because the hour of his judgment is come, and adore him who made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of water.* <note>Revelation 14:6–7</note>

The explanation of this passage is as follows: To you, nations, tribes, tongues, and peoples—listen and understand. Fear God, and give Him honor, at least out of fear of punishment, because the hour of His judgment has come. And adore Him who made heaven, earth, the sea, and the fountains of water. 

I believe this angel is the same one who, in the second part of this book, was seen in heaven in the form of a flying <term>eagle: <note>original: "agle," a variant of "aquila." This refers to Revelation 8:13.</note></term> announcing the immensity of the evils that were about to come upon the whole world. For it is written in that same place: *I saw and heard the voice of an eagle flying through the midst of heaven, saying with a loud voice: Woe, woe, woe to the inhabitants of the earth* <note>original: "Veh: veh: veh" (Revelation 8:13)</note> because of the remaining voices of the three angels who were about to sound their trumpets. For what else is it to cry "Woe, woe, woe" than to announce the hour of judgment? Nor is it a wonder if he is said to fly through the "midst of heaven" who is sent to announce the hour of judgment, because it is necessary that by contemplating high things and the meanings of the heavenly scriptures...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Revelation 14. Having previously discussed the 144,000 and the necessity of humility, the author now interprets the "angel flying in mid-heaven" and the fall of Babylon, transitioning from the Fifth to the Sixth Distinction of his work.</meta>

...[purely] by flying: let those who wish to recognize the approaching hour of judgment without delay run through [these things]. For just as he who, through a bare understanding of the literal letter, knows only how to deal with earthly things, is earthly and animalistic; but he who, through a contemplative understanding, fixes the eye of the mind upon God Himself, who is the true light, is seen to have flown even above the heavens. So too, those who, through a <term>typical intellect <note>original: "typicum intellectum," a method of biblical interpretation where historical events or people are seen as "types" or symbols of spiritual realities.</note></term>, recognize the judgments that God is about to perform on the earth, and that the time of those same judgments has drawn near, they fly as if through the middle of heaven. This is because they leave some things below them and others above.

What does it mean when it says, *Fear God and give Him honor* <note>original: "Timete deum: & date illi honorem" (Revelation 14:7)</note>, except that he honors Him who fears Him, while he dishonors Him who despises fearing Him? Indeed, when it adds, *Because the hour of His judgment has come*, it is as if he said: "Even if you have hitherto <unclear>disregarded</unclear> the fear of God when it seemed equal in the world and its ruin was still far off, at least now perform penance, since the hour of judgment is near." In this place, he calls the "hour of judgment" not the final day of judgment, but rather—as is gathered from what follows—the very desolation of <term>Babylon <note>original: "Babylonice desolationis." In the Apocalypse, Babylon represents the corrupt worldly power or the "city of man" opposed to the city of God.</note></term>.

And what does it mean when it says, *And adore Him who made heaven and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of water*, except that it openly shows that those who refuse to show reverence to the princes of this world—who are not able to make a single hair white or black—are guilty, and yet they despise the one who made all things?

Now, whether this preacher was sent into the world in the fourth period of time or the fifth cannot be easily explained in these days. This is because the messengers of Almighty God are directed, some long before the time and some near it; and both when they are sent long before and when they are sent near the time, they uniformly say that the judgment of God is near. Truly, what is long for men is short and <margin>A long time</margin> momentary for God. If, therefore, this mission was completed in the fourth period, I believe this angel flying through the middle of heaven, who thus thundered the day of judgment, to be <insert>Saint Pope Gregory</insert> himself. Among all that he wrote, nothing was more familiar to him from God than to persuade men of the fear of Almighty God and the day of the final judgment—especially since in his days, <term>Mahometh <note>original: "Mahometh." A medieval spelling for the Prophet Muhammad, whose rise was often interpreted by Christian commentators as a sign of the end times.</note></term> had already begun to aim his darts. Through this, the opportunity was given for that <term>fourth beast <note>original: "bestia illa quarta." A reference to the fourth kingdom in the vision of Daniel 7, often associated with Rome or a final world empire.</note></term> (which we mentioned above) to go out from its place to execute in many places the judgment that Almighty God foreknew was to be done through it.

But if he is still to come, because the same angel is said to have the <term>eternal gospel <note>original: "evangelium eternum." Some medieval theologians interpreted this as a new spiritual understanding of the scriptures for the final age.</note></term> to preach to those sitting on the earth and to every nation, tribe, people, and tongue, then the words written about him and about the two others who followed him must be compared. Thus, by investigating one thing through another, they may either become entirely clear to our understanding, or whatever remains may be consumed by fire.

# Abbot’s Part: Exposition

it can be otherwise: because He who is great above all Kings can have many attendants and send various ministers. Regarding what the second angel says: *Babylon that great city has fallen, has fallen* <note>original: "Cecidit: cecidit Babylon illa magna" (Revelation 14:8)</note>: because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication: this refers either to the ruin of the current time—which is entirely near—or certainly (as I rather think) it will be said as a reproach after the ruin. Her wine is the wine of wrath: and the incurable poison of asps <note>A biblical metaphor for deadly sin or malice, often referencing Deuteronomy 32:33.</note>. This is her very fornication, through which she treasures up judgment for herself on the day of wrath: fornication not only of the body, but also of the heart. With this wine of wrath she made all nations drink—namely, all her families—because whoever participates in her pleasure must necessarily receive the wine of her passion. And this much concerning the voice of the second angel. What about the voice of the third who followed them?

<margin>Chapter 7</margin>

With a loud voice he says what must be said: the third Angel: because there will be greater pressure there, and a calamity hitherto inexperienced. And what will it be? *False Christs and false prophets shall arise* to seduce (if it were possible) even the elect: and as was said above concerning the Beast that ascends from the earth: he shall cause whoever does not worship the image of the Beast to be killed. When will this be? (Without doubt) after the ruin of <term>Babylon <note>In this context, Babylon is often interpreted as the corrupt worldly city or society that opposes the City of God.</note></term>. For because that harlot herself is to be delivered into the hand of the Beast and his ten Kings—the Beast itself and the false prophets being ignorant of the Lord’s counsel—they are destined to win. And therefore the Roman Empire, which once presided over all Kingdoms, is delivered to their power, because the religion of the Christian name has become false. And therefore, triumphing over Babylon, they will also seek to erase the name of Christ from the earth. While that misery continues, some—seeing their enemies prosper—will fail in faith and bow their heads to do the will of the Beast and the king who is to reign over them once the Christian religion is dissolved and the name of Christ denied. But for the sake of the elect who will be among them, and so that the reprobate themselves have no excuse, that messenger is sent: who does not merely preach this in secret, as if fearing, but cries out with a loud voice, which can be heard further off and by everyone. And what does he cry? It has been stated: *If anyone has worshiped the Beast and its image, and received the mark on his forehead or on his hand, he too shall drink of the wine of God’s wrath, which is mixed with unmixed wine in the cup of His wrath.* It should be noted that the preceding angel had said Babylon made all nations drink the wrath of her fornication; but here it says those who worship the beast and its image will drink of the wine of God's wrath, which is mixed with unmixed wine in the cup of His wrath.

->Joa. Fourth [Book] on the Apocalypse<-

I say it must be noted: why it was said there that all nations were made to drink of the wine of the wrath of Babylon’s fornication, but here it says those who worship the beast and its image must drink of the wine of God’s wrath. We know that in ancient times, every nation obeyed its own prince and kept the traditions of its predecessors, whether they were good or bad. However, when the Roman Emperors began to be raised up high above all other kings, they could not be content with their own borders. They began to perform "wonders"—namely, how they might expel the kings of individual nations and multiply fornicating "wives" <note>In this context, "wives" likely refers to allied cities or subject nations brought into the Roman sphere through political "fornication."</note> for themselves in diverse parts of the world. Those who strove to remain under their own king were certainly made to drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication, because any nation that refused to commit "fornication" with the Romans by abandoning its own princes or laws incurred wrath and hatred. <margin>Danger of the Romans</margin> For this reason, the Jews said to Pilate: *Anyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.* <note>John 19:12</note> But if earthly power is angry with those who refuse to fornicate with them voluntarily, is it any wonder if God is angry? For He destroys <margin>Psalms</margin> all who "fornicate" by turning away from Him, not considering how much difference there is between those who kill the body and Him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna <note>Matthew 10:28</note>. 

Regarding what he says: *And he shall drink of the wine of the wrath <margin>Psalms</margin> of God, which is mixed with unmixed wine,* <note>The Latin "mixtum est mero" is a paradox. In the ancient world, wine was usually "mixed" with water to dilute it. "Unmixed" (merum) wine was pure and intoxicating. God's judgment is "mixed" (prepared/poured) but "unmixed" (full strength/undiluted).</note> it is similar to what is written in the Psalm: *He humbles this one and exalts that one; for in the hand of the Lord there is a cup of unmixed wine, full of mixture. And he has tilted it from this side to that; yet its dregs are not emptied out; all the sinners of the earth shall drink.* <note>Psalm 75:8 (Vulgate 74:9).</note> Three things are mentioned in this one cup: wine, the unmixed (*merum*), and the dregs. The dregs signify sin; the mixture of the wine and the unmixed signifies judgment. The Lord tilts the cup from vessel to vessel, judging now this person, now that one; and yet the dregs of sin are not exhausted by human fire, but persist even after judgment upon judgment until the end. Therefore, He does not cease to judge, humbling one and exalting another. But

<column-break/>

why is the cup that He offers to sinners "full of unmixed wine, mixed"? It is because He often judges those who refuse to be corrected with temporal punishment, and then condemns them with eternal punishment. Thus, in a sense, they are seized from the "wine of wrath" toward the "fury of the unmixed," which cannot be soothed—according to that word of the Apostle: *It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.* <note>Hebrews 10:31</note> Therefore, Saint John rightly added "which is mixed with unmixed wine" after saying "he shall drink of the wine of God's wrath." This is so no one might think that any amount of sin can be purged at the end of time through temporal punishment inflicted on vices. Rather, the punishment of "obduration" <note>A theological term for the "hardening" of a heart, making it incapable of repentance.</note> belongs to that strict judgment signified by the wine; thus, those who are struck cannot feel any sorrow, but being hardened under the lashes, they become worse. Consequently, where the elect find mercy, the wicked find eternal judgment. 

He intended this judgment to be understood when he subsequently added: *And he shall be tortured with fire and sulfur in the sight of the holy Angels and in the sight of the Lamb.* Although the reprobate truly suffer worthy torments in the sight of the holy angels, those "angels" can also be understood as those elect men <note>The word "angel" (angelus) literally means "messenger." The author interprets this as the preachers or saints who warned the world.</note> who, having been sent by the Lord, never ceased to cry out so that the faithful might beware the worship of the Beast and its image. Thus, the wicked are tortured in the future before the eyes of those whom they once mocked and cast out from their sight as fools. For this reason, it is fittingly added: *in the sight of the Lamb.* For the Lamb Himself, when He was sent by the Father for the salvation of the world, was cast out by the impious outside the city, and was condemned to a most shameful death among murderers. It follows.

<margin>Text 8</margin>
### And the smoke of their torments shall ascend forever and ever.

A smoking piece of wood, if it is perfectly set on fire and turned into charcoal, soon dissolves into smoke.
