### The Sixth Vision of John in the Apocalypse

...of her: for he has judged the great prostitute <note>original: "meretrice magna"</note> who corrupted the earth with her fornication: and he has avenged the blood of his servants from her hand: and again they said: Alleluia: and her smoke rises forever and ever.

When that ancient Babylon was struck by the Persians <note>original: "aspersis", likely a contraction or variant for Persians/Medes</note> and the Jews were liberated by King Cyrus, ascending out of Babylon, the book called Ezra <note>original: "Esdre"</note> clearly declares how much joy that people experienced. And not without cause. For if it is not permitted to sing the song of the Lord in a foreign land because of the memory of the holy fatherland from which they were exiled, how could they do anything but sing when called back to that fatherland? For thus it is read concerning this in the Psalm:

<margin>Psalm 136</margin>
By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept when we remembered you, Zion. On the willow trees in its midst, we hung up our instruments. For there, those who led us captive asked us for the words of songs, and those who led us away asked for a hymn, saying to us: "Sing to us from the songs of Zion." These were the words of the adversaries. But what do those answer who recognize themselves to be captives? "How," they say, "shall we sing the song of the Lord in a foreign land?" And they add: "If I forget you, O Jerusalem, let my right hand be given over to oblivion." Therefore, it was not permitted for the Jews to sing the song of the Lord in a foreign land. Nor does this New Babylon <note>Representing the corrupt world or the anti-Christian power</note> allow us to sing "Alleluia"; nor, while placed in this exile, are we permitted to sing with a full heart until we arrive at the Kingdom. Yet, because it is good for us to rejoice and be glad in our Creator, and to praise him day by day for the benefits we have received, let us inquire what that great dance of the Hebrews returning to Jerusalem signifies, and how, by God's favor, it is also fulfilled in time—both because the present passage requires it and because through present joys we are made more certain of future ones. Because our...

<column-break/>

...migration remains, and the dark memory of Babylon still chokes the vine of Christ, how great do you think the joy of God's elect will be when they see the briars and thorns cleared from the earth? Babylon reigns while the Church is enslaved because the former occupies everything, and kills the latter lest she bring forth fruit. The Church is cut down; Babylon multiplies and sprouts. What wonder is it then if the Church rejoices when she sees the briars and thorns cut down—she who is not even allowed to breathe in this day of Babylon? Just as it says: the children of Judah, snatched from the chains of Babylon and returned to their fatherland, sang a song of joy; so also we, in that day when God strikes our rival, shall sing: Alleluia. Not merely because she falls and perishes, but because as she falls, liberty is left to us, and because the temple which was burned by the Chaldeans shall be founded again with living stones. For so it is written in the book of Ezra, which is contained under the sixth seal <note>The author uses "sixth seal" (sexto signaculo) here as a structural division of his commentary or a mystical interpretation of history.</note>:

<margin>Ezra</margin>
When the temple of the Lord was founded by the masons, the priests stood in their finery with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise God by the hands of David, King of Israel. And they sang together in hymns and confessions to the Lord: "For he is good, for his mercy endures forever." All the people also shouted with a great cry in praising the Lord, because the temple of the Lord had been founded. Thus, a great joy was made among the people; and this happened four times: First, when they set up the altar and performed the solemnity of the Tabernacles. Second, when the temple was founded. Third, when the work of the temple itself was finished. Fourth, when the structure of the city was completed. According to this, certain new and prosperous things shall be in the Church of God. For these things, perhaps not incongruously, "Alleluia" shall be sung four times. Indeed, "Alleluia" was pronounced four times. After these things (he says), I heard as it were a great voice of many trumpets <note>The Vulgate usually says "many crowds" (turbarum multarum), but the author here writes "many trumpets" (tubarum multarum).</note> in heaven saying: Alleluia. After the ruin of Babylon, a voice like many trumpets will be heard in heaven, for there will be such exultation of the elect in the Church as has not been since the days of Constantine...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Revelation 19, focusing on the spiritual meaning of the "Alleluia" and the "many trumpets." It transitions from the historical liberation of the Jews from Babylon to the future spiritual liberation of the Church and the conversion of the Jewish people during the "sixth age" of history.</meta>

# Part of the Abbot’s Exposition

...[continuation of the previous thought]... on account of the great consolation and joy which the Lord is about to bring upon the earth. And because the mysteries, now opened, will resonate in harmony in the mouths of many; and even many mouths of the Jews will be opened to the praise of Christ through a manifest spiritual understanding. Because, just as a certain mighty breath proceeds from the trumpets of various histories, it is rightly called the sound "of many trumpets": for the voice of the Jews and the Gentiles shall be heard in harmony. Whence it is also written in the Gospel: "The crowds that went before, and those that followed, and even the children of the Hebrews who came out from Jerusalem to meet Christ, were crying out, saying: Hosanna <note>original: "Osanna"; a Hebrew prayer meaning "Save us, we pray"</note> to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!" For now, it begins to become clear what those praises of the singers—the Alleluia <note>original: "alleluia"; a Hebrew expression meaning "Praise Yahweh"</note>—mean for themselves. Even if we are unable to express these praises exactly as they will be, we can nonetheless firmly and securely promise that they will happen in such a time. This is known not only from the opening of this passage, but also from those things we have mentioned up to this point, all of which converge on the "sixth place," showing that in the sixth age <note>Joachim of Fiore divided history into ages; the "sixth age" was the time leading to the Sabbath of the Spirit</note> this great praise will be in the Church of God, on account of the good things that will come upon the remnants of His elect.

For when the sixth seal <note>original: "Sexto signaculo"</note> was begun, Babylon, the metropolis of the Chaldeans, was struck by the Medes; and the captivity of the Jews was ended (as I have already commemorated above). The temple and the walls of the city were built in a "troubled time" <note>original: "angustia temporum"; a reference to Daniel 9:25</note>; because of this, the children of Judah praised the Lord for all the mercy of the Lord by which He consoled them. Likewise, the Solemnity of Palms <note>Palm Sunday</note>, in which Christ was glorified, is celebrated annually in the Church of Christ at the start of the sixth week of Lent, on the sixth day before the Passion of the Lord. There is no doubt that this is a "type" <note>a symbolic foreshadowing</note> of those things which are to come after the striking of Babylon, when the people of the Jews shall be converted to the Lord. Truly, the crowds that "went before" signify the Greeks; those that "followed" signify the Latins; and those who "met them" at the descent of the Mount of Olives signify the Jews—who until the present are enemies of the faith and of our people, but then shall be designated as friends and fellow citizens. They themselves shall sing together with us,

<column-break/>

saying: "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!" Whence Truth itself <note>Jesus</note> says to that same people, who are until now unfaithful: "I say to you, you shall not see me from now on until you say: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord." Therefore, in that day, the severity [of God] will be completed, and a sufficiently harsh vexation will "give understanding to the hearing." <note>A reference to Isaiah 28:19, suggesting suffering leads to wisdom</note> Their eyes will be opened, and they will see Jesus, and they will say—as I have already said—along with us: "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord."

Therefore, the first "Alleluia" will be sung for the destruction of the adulteress <note>original: "adultere"; referring to the Great Prostitute or corrupt worldly power</note>, which is to preach that the Lord is just; for He is just in all His ways. The second "Alleluia" is for the liberty of the Church, which is to acknowledge Him as merciful. The verse which follows the "Alleluia" is an exposition of that very joy signified by the word "Alleluia." The repetition of "Alleluia" demonstrates that the joy and the solemnity are twofold. And indeed, since it comes from the removal of the [oppressor] from their midst, a twofold joy is exhibited: both because the oppression ends, and because consolation is applied. Therefore, in the single judgment of Babylon, "Alleluia" is said once and then again: because the evil that was there ceases to be, and the good that was absent is found.

Just as that very passage has it (unless we have forgotten): "I heard as it were a great voice of many trumpets in heaven, saying: Alleluia." Then the verse follows in the exposition of that Alleluia, saying thus: "Praise and glory and power to our God, because His judgments are true and just, who has judged the great prostitute <note>original: "meretrice magna"</note> who corrupted the earth with her prostitution; and He has avenged the blood of His servants from her hand." And again they said, "Alleluia."

As for what follows—"And her smoke rises forever and ever"—it is doubted whether this is said of Babylon or of those giving praise, because it could be referred to both in a sound understanding. Indeed, "smoke" rises from the elect when their praise and blessing is directed to the living God. Whence comes that saying: "The smoke of the incense of the prayers of the saints ascended from the hand of the angel before God." But smoke also rises from the reprobate: namely, the murmur and blasphemy of a wicked thought.

# John, Sixth Age in the Apocalypse

...according to what is written in this book: *And the smoke of their torments shall ascend for ever and ever.* <note>Revelation 14:11; original: "in secula seculorum"</note> However, both are "for ever and ever": because both the praise of the righteous will be forever, and the murmuring of the wicked will be eternal. It follows:

<margin>Text 2</margin>
**And** the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits upon the throne, saying: Alleluia. <note>Revelation 19:4; "Alleluia" is a Hebrew expression meaning "Praise the Lord"</note>

There is no doubt that the saints rejoice over the liberation of the Church, and they repay thanks to Him who makes us rejoice and share in this joy; for when prosperous things happen to us according to God’s will, they lead to salvation. Therefore, it is not without merit that "Alleluia" shall be sung in heaven for the liberation of the righteous—and no less for the conversion of the Jews, so that what was once fulfilled in us may also be fulfilled in them. *There is joy before the angels of God over one sinner doing penance.* <note>Luke 15:10</note> If this is so before the angels, how much more is it before holy men, who are of the same condition, race, and nature? Moreover, the saints praise before God when they show Him worthy honor and reverence, returning thanks for so many gifts as to a Father and Lord. This is what that miserable one <note>Satan</note> refused to do, who would not submit his heart to the Most High, and therefore he fell in such a way that he could not rise again after his ruin. For yours was lifted high, but he fell into the depths, just as Truth itself <note>Jesus Christ</note> says: *I saw Satan falling like lightning from heaven.* <note>Luke 10:18</note> And he indeed fell thus. But if these [the elders] fall, let them fall so that they do not *fail*. One is humbled with Christ so as not to be dashed down with the prince of this world. It follows:

<margin>Text 3</margin>
**And** a voice came out from the throne, saying: Give praise to our God, all you His servants, and you who fear Him, small and great. <note>Revelation 19:5</note>

It has often been said in this book that the four living creatures <note>original: "animalia"; the four creatures of Ezekiel and Revelation, often interpreted as the four Gospels or four spiritual orders</note> signify spiritual orders, while the throne of God signifies the Church in general. We have also said that the four spiritual orders

<column-break/>

receive only those who are perfect and proven; however, the throne embraces the perfect in such a way that it does not exclude the "little ones" in Christ, as the Lord says of these same little ones: *Whoever offends one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and be drowned in the depths of the sea.* <note>Matthew 18:6</note> Thus, indeed, the common life is tempered by the three holy fathers <note>likely referring to the traditional founders of monastic life or the three grades of the faithful</note> so that the strong who desire it may dwell within it, and the weak do not flee from it. For this life has in itself a hundredfold fruit, a sixtyfold, and a thirtyfold. <note>A common medieval reference to the different rewards for virgins, widows, and the married</note> For it has contemplatives in cloisters, laborers in ministries, and teachers in schools. Yet there will be one joy for those whose will is equal, even if a difference in virtue creates an inequality of rank. Therefore, the elders will sing "Alleluia" to you: either for that joy which we described before, or (as is more widely believed) because that "fullness of the Gentiles" of which the Apostle writes <note>Paul in Romans 11:25</note> will then be complete or nearly complete. "A voice shall go out from the throne"—that is, from the order of general joy, or rather of a great cry; for the *voice of exultation and salvation is in the tents of the righteous* <note>Psalm 118:15</note>—so that now not only those contained in the four orders rejoice (namely the apostles, martyrs, confessors, and virgins, whom we trust are saints and already reign with Christ), but even all the servants of God who have left everything and followed Christ: both the small and the great. This is because the time of their consolation has begun to arrive. Whence Truth itself <note>Christ</note> says: *But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads: behold, your redemption approaches.* <note>Luke 21:28</note> For not all who left everything and followed the Lord were made perfect by God in such a way that, immediately upon leaving their bodies, they would reach the fatherland <note>Heaven</note> without delay; for what is granted to the "great" alone is certainly denied to the "small." Furthermore, on that day, the small and the great will praise their God together: the small because they shall enter the kingdom of God, and the great because they will rejoice in their company. By these things it can also be understood regarding the present Church: that the four living creatures, the seats, and the successions remain in the world through the propagation of their lineages until that day, and that the saints will continue to offer praise.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the "sixth age" of history and the songs of praise in the book of Revelation. It explains how different types of believers—the "small" and the "great"—are called to join in the heavenly liturgy following the judgment of Babylon.</meta>

# Part of the Exposition

Again: the holy mother church, represented on the throne, will command that she be imitated by both the small and the great. But why by the small and the great? Because those who are small in Christ will cease to be small from then on, and those who are great will receive a reward according to their labor. And not without reason were the small preferred in this place, so that what was written might be understood:
<margin>Matthew</margin>
*Whoever humbles himself like this little child, he is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.* <note>Matthew 18:4; original: "Qui se humiliauerit sicut parvulus iste"</note> Those who are great are not excluded if they fear God, but those who refuse to be "great" <note>in a worldly or prideful sense</note> are preferred, for the Lord says: *Every one that humbleth himself shall be exalted.* <note>Luke 14:11</note> But when will this be? Without a doubt, after the fall of Babylon. There are indeed two types of the "perfect" in the Church, which began almost together: one which is designated (as we have often said) in Peter; the other in John. That is to say: one of those who preach, and the other of those who contemplate. And that one which labors <note>the "active" life of service</note> goes first with Peter; but that which contemplates follows with John. The preceding one gives birth to a male, like a warlike soldier; but the following one gives birth to a female, adorned with virginal whiteness. Because the fourth day signifies (as we have already said) this laborious age, for that reason the fourth day, with two added, makes six weeks; and in them are signified the six times of this sixth age. Like a mother with her son, on the fourteenth day she will be received into the temple, because all the fullness of the righteous will be completed, who through a laborious life have pleased the Lord until now—indeed, even until that day in which this laborious time shall receive its consummation. It is for this reason that in this sixth part, at the voice which came out from the throne exhorting the children of God and saying to them: "Give praise to our God, all you his servants, and you that fear him, little and great," immediately there was heard the voice of many saying: Alleluia <note>Praise the Lord</note>. Certainly, this is because through the judgment of Babylon which preceded it, it will be understood that the time of the joy of the saints and the marriage of the Lamb has arrived. Hence it is added immediately:

<margin>Text 4</margin>
¶ **And I heard as it were the voice of a great trumpet,**

<column-break/>

**and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of great thunders, saying: Alleluia.** <note>Revelation 19:6</note>

¶ First, the voice itself is compared to the voice of a great trumpet; then to the voice of many waters; and finally to the voice of great thunders saying together: Alleluia. Previously, Saint John had said that he heard something like the voice of many trumpets in heaven saying: Alleluia. But now he says he heard a voice like a great trumpet, and like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of great thunders saying: Alleluia. Why is this? Because the first voice of praise will be heard almost suddenly in the mouths of many, on account of the just and manifest judgment that the Lord is about to perform. Then, beginning with some man of God, the praise will begin to be orderly in the mouths of many, so that what was thought to be simple in the beginning—and confined in some short space—gradually appears to be manifold. It is as if the turning of many waters to that praise represents peoples and languages; and finally, having become even more powerful, its sound reaches to the ends of the earth like great thunders. But why is this?

> ¶ **For (he said) the Lord our God the Almighty hath reigned: let us be glad and rejoice, and give glory to him; for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath prepared herself.** <note>Revelation 19:6–7</note>

¶ See why those who fear the Lord give praise; see why they sing the song of the Lord: because, namely, that great Babylon will be swallowed up, she who corrupted all nations with the wine of her prostitution. For it seems to be a matter of right, entirely agreeing with reason, that once the great harlot is destroyed—she who committed fornication with the prince of this world <note>Satan</note>—the happy marriage of the Lamb should be celebrated, and the kingdom of Babylon having been handed over.

### The Explanation of the Part

my God for eternity: And again. *As the deer longs for the springs of water: so my soul longs for you, O God. <meta>This page continues the commentary on the visions of the Apocalypse (Revelation), specifically focusing on the interaction between John and the angel in chapter 19. It transitions from the second major division of the text to the third, moving into a discussion of liturgical time and the Passion.</meta>

### John's Sixth [Part] on the Apocalypse

In his day, those to whom it is given to understand these things will marvel at their majesty; to those who open these very things, they will show what reverence they can. This Angel (as I judge) is one of those having the seven vials <note>The "vials" or bowls represent God's judgments in Revelation 16.</note>, of whom it was said above: *One of the seven angels who had the seven vials came and spoke with me, saying: Come, I will show you the damnation of the great harlot,* etc. <note>original: "Uenit vnus de septē angelis q hēbāt septē phyalas: & loquutus est mecū dicēs. Ueni ostēdā tibi dānationē meretricis magne"</note> I have already sufficiently explained according to my capacity who this angel signifies. John, however (as we have said elsewhere), represents the type of the proper listeners: those who, through the words explained more clearly than usual, are ready to understand; to those (as we have said) who open the meaning, they will humbly show reverence. But what follows there?

<margin>Chapter 11</margin>
**And he said (he says) to me: See that you do not do it. I am your fellow servant and of your brothers who have the testimony of Jesus. Worship God.** <note>A translation of Revelation 19:10, where the angel prevents John from worshiping him.</note>

<margin>Term 8</margin>
If we say this refers literally to an angel who was speaking to John, there is a reason why the angel did not permit himself to be worshiped by John. For the Son of God, having become man, assumed human nature into himself; by this, He not only made humanity equal to the angels but even exalted it above the angels. For this reason, the angel did not allow himself to be worshiped by a man whom he recognized to be his fellow servant and equal. But let us return to the mystery. The angel forbids John to worship him, saying he is his fellow servant; God does not reveal deep hidden mysteries to those who think highly of themselves, but through the murmur of their hearts, he reveals them to your fellow servants and fellow citizens. To those whom that grace is not given, they consider themselves unequal; but those not unmindful of their own nature imitate Moses and Paul. One of these judged himself unworthy to be made a leader among the people, so that he resisted God so as not to be sent:
<margin>Exodus</margin>
the other, though he gave the greatest thanks for grace, professed himself to be the least,
<margin>Chapter 10</margin>
saying: *I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.* <note>1 Corinthians 15:9</note> Not only that, but he testified that he was the servant of those to whom he preached, saying: *But we are your servants through Jesus.* <note>2 Corinthians 4:5</note> And in another place: *What then is Apollo? What is Paul? Ministers of Him in whom you have believed.* <note>1 Corinthians 3:5</note> He who said this, Paul, was saying that

<column-break/>

God, and not men, is to be worshiped. It should be noted what is said: *I am your fellow servant and of your brothers who have the testimony of Jesus.* For perhaps those designated by John seem to be above the rank of dignity, while those called John’s brothers are entirely unequal; yet even so, the angel testifies that he is the fellow servant of them all. I believe those "brothers of John having the testimony of Jesus" are designated as those who cannot penetrate mystical words on their own, nor fully grasp them when others explain them; yet they retain the prophetic words which are suitable with most upright faith. Like the blessed Apostle Peter, they stand more by faith than by relying on wisdom and prudence. Therefore, those who are caught up into the third heaven and granted to hear secret words which it is not lawful for man to speak think those others are unequal; but they rather hear with the ear of the heart what the Lord says: *If you do these things, you will be blessed if you keep them.* Well added also is: *The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.* Scripture never commends those more than those who believe the spirit of prophecy—that is, those who believe the words of the prophets written about Christ—who turn to Him through struggle and patience. For it is of much greater merit to believe what is not known than to seek understanding in Scripture through which one might arrive at faith.

->Here ends the second division. The third begins.<-

After that solemn joy which follows the week titled "of the Passion"—I mean that in the way we Latins write "fifth," the Greeks "sixth"—there remains yet another week: which among us Latins is written "sixth." This is the week in which the mysteries of the Passion of Christ are celebrated by both churches; and so, having completed both weeks of the Passion, we arrive at the Easter feasts. Why we perceive the mystical institutions of the Greeks to be in many things not inconsistent regarding the mysteries is that each is a "sixth week": one in respect to the week which among us is written as **Quinquagesima** <note><term>Quinquagesima</term>: Traditionally the Sunday/week fifty days before Easter, marking the transition into the Lenten fast.</note> in which the abstinence of the Greeks solemnly begins; the other in respect to the first week of **Quadragesima** <note><term>Quadragesima</term>: The forty-day period of Lent.</note> which we call sacred. Thus, in a certain way, each week is called "the sixth," as it is fitting for there to be a double tribulation in the "sixth time": so that the one which you have as the sixth, as if it were the first, is seen to pertain to the passion of Saint John the Baptist, who went before; the other to the passion of the Lord, which followed. Which is also fitting on the sixth day on which the Lord suffered.

It then transitions into a technical explanation of how the Latin and Greek churches count the weeks of Lent and Passiontide leading to Easter.</summary>

# The Abbot's Exposition: Part [VI]

it is signified: in which, after the darkness of that very night in which the Lord was captured, light was restored to the earth until the sixth hour; and again from the sixth hour until the ninth hour, darkness fell over the whole earth. <note>This refers to the biblical account of the Crucifixion, where darkness covered the land (Matthew 27:45).</note> According to this book, it is most clearly demonstrated that there is a double tribulation of the "sixth time." <note>The "sixth time" refers to the sixth age of the world, often associated in medieval thought with the time of the Church and the arrival of the Antichrist.</note> Since after that *new song* which the elect of God sing so solemnly, the battle of the beast follows, stirred up by the army of the infidels. In this battle, it is necessary for the King of Gifts <note>original: "regem munerum"</note> to triumph more solemnly over his enemies, and for that saying of the Apostle to be fulfilled: *He must reign until he puts all enemies under his feet.* <note>1 Corinthians 15:25.</note> Therefore, the "Alleluia" that is sung by the saints in the sixth part of the book—surrounded by tribulation both before and after—signifies that the tribulation of the sixth time is double. This is also well-designed in the liturgy of the Easter Vigil, where after several tracts <note>A "tract" is a specific type of chant used in the Mass.</note> that precede, an "Alleluia" follows; and again after the "Alleluia," a short tract follows, after which comes great affliction even until the vigil of Pentecost. Therefore, even if in this sixth part—which is not discussed until after the ruin of Babylon (which cannot happen without the suffering of the elect who will be found in it)—the "Alleluia" will be sung solemnly, nevertheless, after the "Alleluia" itself, a very hard battle will follow. In this battle, whatever seems lacking in the labor of the Church must be completed. For a seventh passion must still follow, so that what is written may be fulfilled: *I will strike you seven times for your sins.* <note>original: "Per curiam vos ſeptis" likely a corruption of "Percutiam vos septies" from Leviticus 26:24.</note> For if in five ages she [the Church] sustained five passions, and two in the sixth, she is shown to be struck seven times in total because of her sins, before that which the Apostle says is perfectly fulfilled in her: *Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.* <note>2 Corinthians 3:17.</note> These things having been passed over as necessarily as they were briefly, let the pen be directed back to its proper course. Let this first be carefully noted: because of the height of the mysteries to which we are invited from this place 

<column-break/>

forward—as if we were to be snatched up in ecstasy—it is necessary for us to iterate the reading of this entire sixth part and run through it in order. We do this so that, having considered the first and last things, we might gain full understanding from it—or at least as much as He grants, who demonstrates that He began at the beginning and finishes at the end. For there follows:

<margin>Chapter 19</margin>
**And I saw heaven opened: and behold, a white horse; and he who sat upon it was called Faithful and True, and with justice he judges and fights. His eyes were like a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns, having a name written which no one knows but himself. And he was clothed in a garment sprinkled with blood, and his name was called The Word of God. And the armies which are in heaven followed him on white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean. And from his mouth proceeds a sharp sword on both sides, so that with it he may strike the nations. And he himself shall rule them with a rod of iron, and he treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God Almighty. And he has on his garment and on his thigh written: King of Kings and Lord of Lords. And I saw an angel standing in the sun, and he cried out with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that flew through the midst of heaven: "Come and gather for the great supper of God, that you may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of tribunes, and the flesh of the strong, and the flesh of horses and those sitting on them, and the flesh of all free men and slaves, both small and great." And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies gathered to face...** <note>A translation of Revelation 19:11–19, describing the "Rider on the White Horse" and the call to the birds of prey.</note>

<meta>This page continues the discussion from the previous page regarding the "sixth time" of history and the impending battle with the Antichrist. It transitions from the liturgical symbolism of the Alleluia to the specific scriptural prophecy of the final confrontation described in Revelation and Zechariah.</meta>

->**Joachim’s Sixth Part of the Apocalypse**<-

...during the battle with him who sat on the horse and with his army, and the beast was captured, and with it the false prophet: and he who performed signs before it, by which he led astray those who received the mark of the beast and those who worshipped its image. These two were cast alive into the lake of fire burning with sulfur; and the rest were killed with the sword of him who sat on the horse, which proceeds from his mouth; and all the birds were filled with their flesh. <note>This is a direct translation of the Latin Vulgate for Revelation 19:19-21, describing the defeat of the Antichrist's forces.</note>

¶ All these things have been set forth, but not yet explained. We have put them forward so that we may know what is being dealt with in this specific point: in which no mere saint is shown to be the leader of the war, but he who died for us and redeemed us in his blood, so that what was written by the prophet Zechariah might be fulfilled: *Behold, the days of the Lord are coming: and I will gather all nations to Jerusalem for battle; and the city shall be captured, and the houses plundered, and the women violated. And half of the city shall go forth into captivity, and the remainder of the people shall not be taken from the city. And the Lord shall go forth and fight against those nations, just as he fights in the day of conflict.* <note>Zechariah 14:1-3.</note> Saint John had said earlier that the beast that *was and was not* would ascend from the abyss and go into destruction; and that the *seventh king* who had not yet come was going to come, and when he came, he must remain for a short time. <note>Refers to Revelation 17:8-10. Medieval commentators often tried to identify these "kings" with specific historical persecutors of the Church.</note> Therefore, what he had then said would be in the future, he presents here in this part of the book as if it were present; and except for that king, he makes no mention, so that he may be shown to be that wicked one who is called the <term>Antichrist</term> <note>The ultimate enemy of Christ expected to appear at the end of time.</note>, in whose most foul body the red dragon <note>The dragon is a traditional symbol for Satan.</note> will dwell personally. It is written that after this repeated battle of the beast, he is to be imprisoned

<column-break/>

in the abyss, so that he may no longer seduce the nations until the time of his imprisonment is completed. However, we say this by way of opinion rather than by absolute assertion, whether here or in other places. Namely, we wonder whether this seventh king—or perhaps the preceding one of whom it is said above "one is"—is the one who is called <margin>Gog</margin> **Gog**, or if someone else is the one properly called the Antichrist. <note>Gog and Magog are mysterious enemies mentioned in Ezekiel and Revelation, often associated with the apocalyptic invaders of the end times.</note> One thing we say securely: that the sixth king will be worse than the five preceding him, and the seventh worse than the sixth; and each will be filled with the dragon's gall; and they themselves are the two last heads of the dragon itself, in which he will fight most fiercely in this <term>sixth time</term> <note>In Joachim's theology, the "sixth time" is the penultimate age of the world, characterized by extreme trial and the rise of the Antichrist.</note>. And as I think, the first of these will be king over the beast that ascends from the sea; the second over the beast that ascends from the earth—namely, that beast which was defeated here, the false prophet. Now, since it is clearly evident that he who sits on the white horse is Jesus Christ, it is asked what might be thought or believed about him: whether he might deign to appear visibly in person in a time of such great necessity to fight against those nations with the sword of his mouth, just as he did in the time when he came into the world; or whether he will not appear visibly in himself, but rather will fight and prevail through his saints, just as he has from the time he ascended into heaven.

And indeed, we are certain and the whole Church of the righteous holds unshakably that he is going to come in the glory of his Father to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire. But whether this happens during the time of the Antichrist, or afterward, is doubted by many. For some of the saints seem to assert that the Lord himself comes in person to destroy the Antichrist and his kingdom, following the authority of the Apostle who says: *And then that wicked one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the rush of the breath of his mouth, and will destroy by the brightness of his coming.* <note>2 Thessalonians 2:8.</note> Yet some have preferred to doubt rather than to assert whether he himself does this, or his messenger. I, however, think that he comes in person to destroy him, because of what he himself says in the Gospel: *But immediately after the tribulation of those days...* <note>Matthew 24:29.</note>

### ->Abbot Joachim: Part of the Exposition<-

of others: *the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.* <note>original: "sol obscurabitur: & luna non dabit lumen suum" from Matthew 24:29.</note> For if he did not say "immediately," a rather doubtful question would remain regarding this. But because this was said, it may seem that while the Antichrist is still reigning, Christ will come so that he himself may impose an end upon his reign and blasphemy. However, this does not force one to understand these signs as happening specifically in the time of the Antichrist and shortly after; nor does it mean that Christ comes as soon as the signs appear, because there could be some delay between the showing of the signs and his most hidden arrival, which is inscrutable to all. But if he himself will come against the Antichrist with his army, what can we think of the fact that he was seen sitting upon a white horse, except that in his body—which is clean from sin—he will appear visibly before the good and the evil, to execute vengeance upon the nations and rebukes upon the peoples?
<margin>Psalm</margin>
This also compels us to understand the following parts, especially because of what follows: *And the armies which are in heaven followed him on white horses.* <note>Revelation 19:14.</note> Truly, if this is so, how do we say it is possible for the saints who are to come with Christ to appear with their bodies—unless perhaps we take a part for the whole? In this way, the saying might be understood concerning those
<margin>Zechariah</margin>
who, after the resurrection of the Lord, came into the holy city and appeared to many. And indeed, it is written in the aforementioned prophet: *Behold, the Lord my God shall come, and all his saints with him.* <note>Zechariah 14:5.</note> But nevertheless, it is not written that they come having been resurrected—unless perhaps it is understood (if indeed it can be understood soundly) as that which the Apostle says: *This we say to you in the word of the Lord: that we who are alive, who remain until the coming of the Lord, shall not precede those who have fallen asleep; for the Lord himself, at a command and at the voice of the archangel, and at the trumpet of God, will descend from heaven, and the dead who are in Christ will rise first.* <note>1 Thessalonians 4:15-16.</note> For we do not know—and Augustine confesses that he himself does not know—whether the resurrection of the dead will be near the beginning of that time which he calls the "Day of Judgment," or at the end, speaking thus: "In that judgment,

<column-break/>

or around that judgment, we say these things are to come: <term>Elijah the Tishbite</term><note>A reference to the prophet Elijah, who was expected to return before the Great Day of the Lord.</note>, the faith of the Jews, the Antichrist who is to persecute, Christ who is to judge, the resurrection of the dead, the separation of the good and the evil, the conflagration of the world, and its renewal. All these things indeed must be believed to be coming; but in what manner and in what order they come, the experience of the events will then teach better than human intelligence is now able to attain perfectly. I think, however, that they will come in the order in which they were mentioned by me." These are the words of Augustine. Paul, however, seems to intend that the resurrection of the dead ought to happen at the time of the seventh angel sounding the trumpet (that is, in the final time of the Antichrist), saying thus: *Behold, I tell you a mystery: We shall all indeed rise, but we shall not all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet.* <note>1 Corinthians 15:51-52.</note> But to this opinion, that which follows in the seventh part seems contrary, where only the saints are said to live. How that can be understood—and if it can be—we will take care to investigate when we come to that place. However, in the place we have now begun to treat, I judge one of two things must be held: either that the dead who are in Christ will appear living with him immediately, according to the authority of the Apostle written above; or those will appear resurrected with him who rose from the dead at the same time as he did. Although perhaps I have not meditatively erred, I rather think that those following the Passion of their Lord will thus fight by surrendering their bodies for the name of Christ in the "sixth time," just as he himself on the "sixth day" on that white horse of his overcame and conquered. What may please others, I do not know; but to me, this is more pleasing. Yet truly, even if the Lord himself will not be present in bodily presence, he will nevertheless be invisibly present to his soldiers so that he may conquer in them in this most recent time, just as in the days of old. But although we are compelled concerning his bodily presence...

<meta>This page continues the exposition of Revelation 19, shifting from the general signs of the end to the specific vision of Christ as the Rider on the White Horse. It interprets the opening of heaven as the opening of the deeper meaning of Scripture and provides a dual interpretation of the blood on Christ's robes: both as his own sacrificial blood and the blood of the judged.</meta>

### JOACHIM: SIXTH PART ON THE APOCALYPSE

...to happen: <note>original: "contingere"</note> nevertheless, all this pertains to the Day of Judgment, as is demonstrated from that place in the fifth part of the sixth chapter <note>Joachim of Fiore typically divides his works into "parts" and "books"; this refers to his earlier discussion of the seven vials/bowls of wrath.</note> where mention of the gathering of these kings to the beast was made in this way: *I saw coming out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits in the manner of frogs; for they are the spirits of demons performing signs, and they go forth to the kings of the whole earth to gather them for battle on the great day of God Almighty.* <note>Revelation 16:13-14.</note> 

As for what he says here—*I saw heaven opened,* etc.—it is to be referred to the opening of Sacred Scripture. From the clear light of its opening, this very thing, and everything that follows, is shown to be about to happen. 

*He who sat upon the horse*—that is, Christ Jesus—*was called Faithful and True,* because just as he promised concerning this victory, so in the preordained time he will show himself to be faithful and true. He is also rightly said to *judge and fight in justice,* because he does not seek another's right, but his own, which was certainly usurped unjustly by the Devil; therefore, the Devil himself and his army shall be punished by a just judgment. Moreover, He will judge the wicked and the authors of such a great crime; the rest he will overcome and subject to his scepter, so that what the Apostle says may be fulfilled: *It is necessary for him to reign until he puts all his enemies under his feet.* <note>1 Corinthians 15:25.</note> For he alone can do what no one else can. 

*His eyes,* he says, *were like a flame of fire, and on his head were many diadems,* <term>diademata: royal crowns or headbands symbolizing sovereign authority</term> *having a name written which no one knows but himself; and he was clothed in a garment sprinkled with blood, and his name was called The Word of God.* <note>Revelation 19:12-13.</note> The eyes of the Lord coming to judgment are claimed to be like a flame of fire because there will be no one who can hide himself from his heat. Hence it is also said by the Apostle: *Do not judge before the time until the Lord comes, who will illuminate the hidden things of darkness and make manifest the counsels of hearts.* <note>1 Corinthians 4:5.</note> He is also rightly said to have many diadems on his head because he will triumph in that contest over all his enemies, whom he has not wished to destroy until now; surely because he is *true God from true God,* <note>original: "deus verus est de deo vero," a phrase from the Nicene Creed.</note>

<column-break/>

and it is necessary that the creative Divinity, designated by the "head," should conquer and triumph over all creatures. 

Hence it is also well said: *having a name written which no one knows but himself.* For while many are able to believe that he is the Word and the Wisdom of the Father, no one can truly *know* it except himself, who is what he is. In him, only the spiritual and the faithful—who, since they are his body, participate in all that he has—can share in this. 

But why are the unfaithful unable to know? Because they are weakened in their faith on account of his sufferings <note>original: "passiones." Referring to the "stumbling block" of a crucified God.</note>. Both of these points are well demonstrated when he adds: *And he was clothed in a garment sprinkled with blood, and his name was called The Word of God.* It is as if he were saying: For this reason the unfaithful and the impious are unable to know his name, which is "The Word of God," because in the assumed form of our mortality he deigned to be sprinkled with blood shed by the hands of impious men. 

We can also understand the *garment sprinkled with blood* as the justice of Christ, which impious men defile and pollute by blackening it with blasphemies when they run into judgment, saying: "It is the Lord’s will that the wicked act wickedly, and it is necessary for them to perish in their sins." Although they do this incessantly at all times, they do so especially on that day in which the Lord will render to each according to his works. 

Hence the same Lord speaks through the prophet, saying: *I have trodden the winepress alone,* <term>torcular: a winepress, here symbolizing the crushing of enemies in divine judgment</term> *and of the nations there is no man with me. I have trodden them in my fury and trampled them in my wrath. And their blood is sprinkled upon my garments, and I have stained all my clothing. For the day of vengeance is in my heart; the year of my retribution has come. I looked around and there was no helper; I sought and there was no one to aid. And my own arm saved me, and my very indignation helped me.* <note>Isaiah 63:3-5.</note> 

Behold, here it is openly hinted what the sprinkling of blood on Christ’s clothing means: that it is to be referred to the day of vengeance, <note>original: "vltionis."</note> in which it is necessary for the grape to be trodden in the vat of wrath.

<meta>This page continues the exposition of Revelation 19, shifting from the opening of heaven to the specific description of the Rider on the White Horse and his celestial armies. It explores the theological significance of Christ's titles, his dual role as Savior and Judge, and the symbolic meaning of his white horse and the "sword" of his mouth.</meta>

### ABBOT JOACHIM'S EXPOSITION: PART SIX

...of the matter until the blood flows out even to the bridles of the horses. <note>original: "usq; ad frenos equorum"; a reference to Revelation 14:20, describing the depth of the blood from the winepress of God's wrath.</note> For to him belongs the decree of judgment, according to what he himself says: *For neither does the Father judge anyone, but has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son as they honor the Father.* <note>original: "Neque enim pater iudicat quenq; : sed omne iudiciū dedit filio"; John 5:22-23.</note> Wherefore it is not incongruously added: *And his name was called the Word of God,* so that what he says elsewhere may be understood: *For I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world. The word that I have spoken, that will judge him on the last day.* <note>John 12:47-48.</note> 

And these things are indeed concerning Christ the King. What of the army? *And the armies,* he says, *which are in heaven followed him on white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.* <note>original: "byssino mūdo"; Revelation 19:14.</note> If the white horse on which Christ sits designates his body in which he rose from the dead, it is certainly clear that by the white horses on which the armies in heaven follow him, spiritual bodies are designated. <note>Joachim interprets the horses not as literal animals but as the glorified, resurrected bodies of the saints.</note> Although it can also be rightly understood as referring to chaste bodies delivered to torments for the love of their Lord, especially since they are still shown as horses so that the battle may be joined—a battle which no one is believed to join except in an animal body. <note>He suggests the "horses" represent the physical, suffering bodies of martyrs who fight through their endurance.</note> 

As for what the white, clean fine linen signifies, John himself explains when he says: *For the fine linen is the justifications of the saints.* <note>Revelation 19:8.</note> But that which follows—*And out of his mouth comes a sword, sharp on both sides*—we took care to explain in the first part of this book. For he is the Word of God that proceeds from the mouth of Christ; he is the spirit of his mouth by which he will slay the wicked, as it is written: *And with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked.* <note>Isaiah 11:4.</note> It is well called "sharp on both sides" because on one side it cuts down the sterile tree so that it perishes forever, and on the other, it prunes the fruitful one so that it bears more fruit. Here he strikes so that he may destroy sinners from the earth; there he strikes so that he may bring to life those predestined for life. Wherefore concerning the same sword it is subsequently added: *That with it he may strike the nations.* That he does this not only to condemn those foreknown for death, but to save from among them those predestined for life, the following discourse makes clear 

<column-break/>

when it says: *And he himself shall rule them with a rod of iron.* <note>original: "virga ferrea"; Revelation 19:15.</note> For those who do not wish to be converted by kindness and humility must feel the strength of his discipline, and be subjected even for his scepter’s sake—hearing, even they, with hearts slow to believe like the people of the Jews: *Because you have seen me, you have believed; blessed are they who have not seen and have believed.* <note>John 20:29.</note> For it is as if they did not see the Lord and yet believed in the Crucified One—those who sought to scrutinize his majesty as much as his ineffable goodness, saying humbly with the people of Israel: *Let Moses speak to us and we will listen; let not the Lord speak to us, lest we die.* <note>Exodus 20:19.</note> 

But those who think it foolishness to believe in the Crucified One must feel the fury of him as he approaches for judgment, so that at least distress alone may provide understanding to the hearing. Wherefore it is soon added: *And he himself treads the winepress of the fierceness of the wrath of Almighty God.* <note>Revelation 19:15.</note> It is as if it were said: "For this reason the nations shall be restrained under the discipline of his rod: because they will see the judgment he is about to perform on the wicked, and the mighty hand he will exercise upon them." Moreover, this word agrees with the word placed above from the prophet, so that the sprinkling of blood <note>A reference to the "garment sprinkled with blood" from Rev 19:13.</note> may be understood to pertain to the rigor of judgment. For it behooves him to exercise judgment and to reign until he puts all his enemies under his feet. <note>1 Corinthians 15:25.</note> 

Wherefore it is soon added: *And he had on his garment and on his thigh written: King of kings and Lord of lords.* <note>Revelation 19:16.</note> In the garment, justice is designated; in the thigh, the natural propagation of offspring. <note>In medieval exegesis, the "thigh" often represents lineage or humanity.</note> For there are some who are granted power over others because they are found worthy by their deeds; others because they are the children of nobles and the heirs of the powerful. To Christ, however, dominion and the honor of the kingdom are owed in both ways: either because he earned the kingdom through the passion by which he conquered the prince of this world through his endurance, or because he is the Son of the Highest King, to whom all highness of creature is and ought to be subject. Now this was said in this sixth part of the book, which he has until now patiently endured, and willed to be subject in his members...

Joachim emphasizes that Christ's authority as 'King of kings' is derived from both his divine lineage as the Son of God and his human victory through the Passion.</summary>

### JOACHIM’S EXPOSITION ON THE APOCALYPSE: PART SIX

<margin>The Proclamation</margin>
...to his own powerful ones of the world: in that moment of the sixth period <note>Joachim of Fiore divided history into "status" or ages; the sixth age represents the time leading up to the Sabbath of the saints.</note> in which he will perform these things in those same members of his, he shall be elevated above all hills, fulfilling in them what was written in the prophet Daniel: *The judgment shall sit, that the power may be taken away*—it is understood this refers to the beast of whom the discourse spoke—*and that it may be destroyed even unto the end. But the kingdom and the power and the greatness of the kingdom, which is under all the heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High.* <note>original: "Iudicium sedebit vt auferatur potentia... Regnum autem 7 potestas 7 magnitudo regni... detur populo sanctorum altissimi"; Daniel 7:26-27.</note> It follows: *And I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that flew through the midst of heaven: Come and gather yourselves together to the great supper of God, that you may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of the strong, and the flesh of horses, and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all freemen and slaves, both small and great.* <note>Revelation 19:17-18.</note>

<margin>Elijah</margin>
I believe this angel who stands in the sun is the prophet Elijah, to whom was given the quality of the <term>contemplative life</term> <note>The "contemplative life" focuses on prayer and mystical union with God, as opposed to the "active life" of service and labor.</note>, just as the <term>active life</term> was given to John the Baptist. For just as the moon sometimes designates the active life, so the sun designates the contemplative life. Furthermore, because in his first coming Jesus Christ came humble and mild, John the Baptist was sent as a gentle one before his face, so that he might go before the Savior who was coming indeed in the water of redemption. And because in his second coming he will come in majesty, Elijah is to be sent like a sun before his face, so that he may precede the Judge who is to come in the terrible fire of judgment, of which the Apostle speaks: *But a certain terrible expectation of judgment and a rage of fire which shall consume the adversaries.* <note>Hebrews 10:27.</note> He will cry out with a "great voice" because he will preach publicly and solemnly. Moreover, he will invite the birds of heaven to the "great supper of God" because he will call spiritual men and contemplatives to the spiritual banquet of Christ, in which the entirety of the flesh that is doomed to die shall be slaughtered, so that what is carnal may pass away and what is spiritual may remain. And it is well that this banquet is called a *supper* <note>original: "cena"</note> and not a *lunch* <note>original: "prandium"</note>, because such a banquet is to be celebrated near the end of this world. Now, just as the birds of heaven that feed on flesh delight in the carcasses of the dead, so the souls of the just find joy in the failure of carnal concupiscence and

<column-break/>

in the abolition of carnal desires that war against the soul. This is why God himself required the sacrifice of goats, calves, and rams in the Old Testament, and ate (metaphorically) in those same sacrifices: for just as carnal men rejoice in the slaughter of the flesh, so the saints of God rejoice in the abolition of carnal desire. For we know that a banquet of flesh cannot occur unless the animals themselves, from whose carcasses the banquet is prepared, cease to exist. But also, a banquet is usually commended among men when animals of various kinds are slaughtered. From this fact, it is clearly evident that different kinds of men will stand together against the Lord on that day, to be overcome equally by Christ the King. Indeed, the birds of heaven are commanded to eat the flesh of kings and <term>tribunes</term> <note>Joachim uses "tribunorum" to denote high-ranking military or civil officials.</note>, of the strong and of horses and those sitting on them (that is, subjects and prelates), of freemen and slaves, of small and great. The text follows: *And I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered together to make war with him who sat on the horse and with his army.* <note>Revelation 19:19.</note> We must not place the appearance of the one sitting on the horse and his army first, and the gathering of the kings with the beast to make war later; rather, first comes the gathering of those kings, and afterward the revelation of Christ. For first, the kings of the earth—seduced by the signs of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophets who will be with him—will conspire as one; and afterward, the Lord will appear to destroy the kingdom of the devil and those who are on his side. Whether he will then appear visibly, or rather perform this victory by the invisible power of his Spirit, we entrust to him who said: *Of that hour no one knows, except the Father alone.* <note>Matthew 24:36.</note> However, in whatever way it may happen, the kingdom of the devil will nonetheless be scattered on that day—some being punished terribly, others slain by the sword that proceeds from his mouth. Whence it is immediately added: *And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet who performed signs before him...* <note>Revelation 19:20.</note>

<summary>Joachim interprets the angel in the sun as the prophet Elijah, the herald of Christ's second coming, who calls the spiritual "birds" to celebrate the destruction of carnal desires and worldly powers. He argues that the spiritual victory of the saints over the flesh coincides with the literal defeat of the worldly kings who oppose Christ at the end of the sixth age.</summary>

# THE EXPOSITION: PART SIX

...by which he seduced those who received the mark of the beast and worshipped its image. These two were cast alive into the lake of fire burning with sulfur, and the rest were killed by the sword of the one sitting upon the horse, which proceeds from his own mouth; and all the birds were filled with their flesh. Previously, he had said that he saw an angel in the sun calling the birds of heaven to the great supper of God: that they might eat the flesh of kings, and commanders, and the strong, and horses, and those sitting upon them. Now he shows of whom he had said this, lest anyone should think it was said of everyone. Finally, the beast and the false prophet, who together with the red dragon will be the inventors of such great crimes, shall be cast together alive into the lake of fire—either because they shall descend alive into hell, just as once happened to Dathan and Abiram <note>Dathan and Abiram were biblical figures who rebelled against Moses and were swallowed by the earth (Numbers 16).</note>, or because they will have already been judged and condemned by their own judgment, according to what was said of certain ones: *And they descended alive into hell.* As for those whom he calls the kings of the earth and their armies: they shall be killed by the word of Christ, specifically in that part of them in which they live wickedly. The faithful souls will rejoice in their slaughter because the judgment of God pertains to the just: so that the deceivers of others may receive a punishment worthy of their merits, and so that, by the height of His goodness, those who simply follow them—ignorant of the craftiness of their deception—may be confounded by their own error; and, being confounded, they may be converted to the living and true God, who washed us from our sins and deigned to redeem us in His own blood. Furthermore, on that day when this occurs, that which was written by the prophet shall be fulfilled:

<margin>Zephaniah</margin>
> Wait for me, says the Lord, on the day of my resurrection in the future: because my judgment is to gather the nations and collect the kingdoms. And I will pour out upon them my indignation and all the wrath of my fury. For in the fire of my jealousy all the earth shall be devoured: because then I will restore to the peoples a chosen lip <note>original: "labium electum"; often translated as "pure speech" or "purified lips."</note> so that they may all call upon the name of the Lord and serve him with one shoulder. From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, from there my suppli-

<column-break/>

ants, the children of my dispersed, shall bring an offering to me. In that day you shall not be confounded because of all your inventions by which you have transgressed against me. For then I will take away from your midst the malicious ones of your pride, and you shall no longer be exalted on my holy mountain. And I will leave in your midst a poor and needy people, and they shall hope in the name of the Lord. The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak a lie; and a deceitful tongue shall not be found in their mouth. For they themselves shall feed and lie down, and there shall be no one to make them afraid.

That which was written in the prophet Daniel shall also be fulfilled, as he said in one of his visions:

> And I said to the man who was clothed in linen, who stood upon the waters of the river: "How long until the end of these wonders?" And I heard the man who was clothed in linen, who stood upon the waters of the river, when he had lifted up his right hand and his left hand to heaven and sworn by Him who lives forever: "That it shall be for a time, and times, and half a time; and when the dispersal of the hand of the holy people is completed, all these things shall be fulfilled." <note>Daniel 12:6-7. In Joachim's system, "a time, times, and half a time" usually signifies three and a half years or three and a half ages.</note>

And also that which was written in the third part of this book:

> And the angel whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the earth lifted his hand to heaven and swore by Him who lives forever and ever: "That time shall be no more"—it is understood to mean time for labor—"but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when the trumpet shall begin to sound, the mystery of God shall be finished, just as he announced through his servants the prophets." <note>Revelation 10:5-7.</note>

Now that the parts of the book of the Apocalypse have been completed, in which six laborious periods <note>original: "tempora laboriosa." This is Joachim's famous "Age of the Holy Spirit," a future era of monastic peace and spiritual understanding.</note>, or even the seventh age of the world, designated and...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Sixth Vision of the Apocalypse, focusing on the timing of the Final Judgment and the transition from the fall of the Antichrist to the end of the world. The author is reconciling the "last hour" mentioned in the Epistles with the long duration of history.</meta>

->John’s Sixth [Vision] in the Apocalypse<-

> ...on that first day of which scripture says: And God rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And he blessed the seventh day and sanctified it. <note>original: "Et requieuit deus die septimo... Et benedixit die septimo & sanctificauit illum." Referring to Genesis 2:2–3.</note>

Regarding this final time designated by the Sabbath, Saint Augustine wrote in his book *The City of God* (as we have already mentioned in this work). This is a truth held in the confession of the entire Church of the true God: we believe Christ will come from heaven to judge the living and the dead. We call this final day of divine judgment the "last time." For it is uncertain through how many days this judgment will extend; but no one who has read the Holy Scriptures (however carelessly) is ignorant of the fact that "day" is customarily used to mean "time." <note>The author explains that "day" in prophecy often represents a longer era or age, rather than a 24-hour period.</note> The blessed Remigius <note>Remigius of Auxerre (c. 841–908), a Carolingian scholar and commentator.</note> also teaches that the space of time which will exist after the fall of the Antichrist is uncertain. He himself destroys the opinion of those who think that with the fall of the Antichrist, worldly time passes away and the consummation of the age is immediately at hand. Such people are ignorant that the "last days" or the "end of the world" should not always be understood as the final moment of the world’s end, but rather as the "time of the end" (that is, the last age of the world). This is especially true since more than a thousand years have already passed since the blessed John said: *Little children, it is the last hour.* <note>1 John 2:18. Medieval theologians had to explain why the "last hour" had already lasted ten centuries.</note> Therefore, there will be a time after the fall of the Antichrist; and whether the Lord is to come for judgment at the end of that time, or at the beginning, some have judged it better to remain in doubt than to define it, until the Lord himself should make it clear. For he says:
> But immediately after the tribulation of those days—namely, that tribulation which the beast and the false prophet shall bring about—the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be moved. And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Man in heaven. And then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn; and they shall see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven with great power and majesty. And he shall send his angels with a trumpet and a great voice, and he shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the highest point of the heavens even to the earth's

<column-break/>

borders. <note>Matthew 24:29–31.</note> And the Apostle <note>Paul</note> seems to intend this very thing in that place where he speaks of the Antichrist:
> And then that wicked one shall be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming. <note>2 Thessalonians 2:8.</note>

We have stated in this book why we are dealing with the dragon: because once his six heads—in which the dragon fought through six continuous periods against the faithful—have been checked and overcome, he is destined to fight in the seventh head more desperately than usual, <margin>however</margin> and more fiercely, pouring out all his poison through his mouth, knowing that the time of his damnation is near. This is because that which the Lord says must be entirely fulfilled:
> And the prince of this world shall be cast out. <note>John 12:31. The "prince of this world" is a common title for Satan.</note>

This was not explicitly stated in the sixth part which we have treated until now; however, it is understood as a consequence: that in the aforementioned battle which the beast, the false prophet, and the kings of the earth shall have with Christ, the Antichrist himself (as we believe) will be the prince whom the most wicked dragon will clothe. By his most iniquitous scheming, that terrible clash of the kings of the earth shall rise up to wage war against the King of Kings. This is shown in the sixth angel pouring out the seven bowls of God's wrath, where it is said:
> I saw from the mouth of the dragon, and from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits go out like frogs. For they are the spirits of demons performing signs, and they go out to the kings of the whole earth to gather them for battle on the great day of God Almighty. <note>Revelation 16:13–14.</note>

Therefore, the beast and the false prophet are not acting on their own; they act by the instinct and command of the dragon speaking through the mouth of that seventh king who is written of in this book. And since the blessed John taught in the above writings that the beast and the false prophet must be sent alive into the lake of fire burning with sulfur, while the others are to be killed by the sword of the one sitting upon the horse (which proceeds from his mouth), it was necessary to suggest also what must become of the dragon. For he is the author of evils, by whose seduction and deceit the kings of the earth and the princes shall likewise stand and breathe together against the Lord and against his Christ, so that the Lord may speak to them in his anger and trouble them in his fury. Thus he says:

### Part of the Explanation

<margin>Scripture 1</margin>
> **And I saw** (he said) **an angel coming down from heaven, having the key to the abyss and a great chain in his hand: and he seized the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the Devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years: and he cast him into the abyss and shut and sealed it over him: so that he should no longer seduce the nations until the thousand years were completed: and after this, he must be released for a short time.** <note>original: "Et uidi (ait) angelum descendentẽ..." quoting Revelation 20:1-3.</note>

The things written above seemed clear enough, as they were brought down in order from the beginning of the book without any obstacle until reaching a fitting end—not only regarding the six ecclesiastical ages <note>The "six ages" refers to a traditional medieval way of dividing world history, often corresponding to the six days of Creation.</note> but also the six parts of the book. But now, having heard that Satan is to be bound and then released again, the understanding of many is dulled, for this seems far removed from the common opinion. However, this interpretation would be more effective if the number of a thousand years were not referred back to the whole time of the Church through recapitulation. <note>Recapitulation is a method of biblical interpretation where the narrative is seen as looping back to describe the same period from a different perspective, rather than following a linear timeline.</note> By this, I mean I set aside the opinion of those who think these thousand years refer to a literal Sabbath, and instead suggest they signify the whole duration of the Church. Even if a certainty on this matter cannot be given, a reasonable opinion can be offered that does not go against the faith. For look: the dragon and the beast are described as having seven heads, and we have written in this work that these seven heads represent seven times, or as if seven ages were to be ground down. When all these are crushed, it stands to reason and mystery that the Sabbath of the seventh age should follow. But who knows how brief that Sabbath itself might be? If the time of the Sabbath is brief, and indeed the Antichrist will already be present when the beast and the false prophet are overcome, what prevents us from thinking that he is to be removed for an hour from the sight of the elect? This is because what he could not win in the first

<margin><insert>the present time of the antichrist[...]</insert></margin>

<column-break/>

<margin>Note where Gog is</margin>
and second war of the sixth age, he still hopes to achieve through the Scythian nations. <note>The Scythians were historically nomadic people from Central Eurasia, often identified in medieval prophecy with the wild, destructive forces of Gog and Magog.</note> Thus, having called upon Gog with his army, whose number will be like the sand of the sea, he might complete the evil which the patience of God permits him to do. Indeed, the passage itself seems to suggest this: it says the beast and the false prophet will fight and be handed over to the pool of fire, but it does not say the dragon himself is handed over to the pool of fire then; rather, he is to be imprisoned for a time and released again for a short time. According to this, the opinion of those who say a period remains after the fall of the Antichrist could be true. That is, when he loses the beast and the false prophet in battle, the truth is victorious for those who say he is to be "slain by the breath of Christ’s mouth" and "destroyed by the brightness of his coming." <note>original: "interficiendũ illũ spiritu oris christi..." quoting 2 Thessalonians 2:8.</note> Perhaps the first of these happens in the penultimate victory, when those in the service of the beast are killed by the sword proceeding from Christ's mouth; but the second happens in the final victory, when the Lord himself appears manifest. For the text of the book seems to intend that, once the sixth age has begun, the Devil will bring forth the Saracens against the Christian Empire. After many evils, he is to be overcome by the soldiers of Christ, of whom it is said: *These shall fight with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them, for he is Lord of lords and King of kings, and those with him are called, elect, and faithful.* <note>Quoting Revelation 17:14.</note> Then Babylon shall be delivered into their hands to be judged. Once this battle is settled, there will be peace and joy in the Church of Christ. When this part is finished, in a short time he will again stir up the "dead beast" (that is, the pagans) and add false prophets to help them. Again, the harder he fights, the more powerfully he will be overcome by the army of Christ. The beast and the false prophet will be delivered into the pool of fire burning with sulfur, and the rest will be converted to the Lord. When that battle is finished, there will be a great peace such as has not been since the beginning of the world, the end of which remains in God's judgment. Finally, when that peace is complete, the devil, having gone out again with the army of Gog, will engage in a third battle, more grievous than the first two. After these, when all who came with him are punished, he himself, after all the others, will be delivered into the pool of fire. Thus, the three battles will perhaps be so close together that that man...
