->Joachim: First [Book] of the Ten Strings<-

...in divine scripture: there are ten strings because there are ten understandings which specifically pertain to the knowledge of God and to his great works, which he has performed and continues to perform until the end according to the counsel of his will. But the two lower ones <note>original: "due inferiores," referring to the literal and moral senses of scripture</note>, which proceed from the letter for the instruction of every individual, are known to belong [to us] as we said above. For through those two we are taught what we ought to do; through those others [the ten] we are taught to recognize those things which have been done by God. Therefore, there is a great <note>The OCR reads "Stultum" (foolish), but the context and the next sentence's parallel structure confirm this is "Multum" (much/great).</note> difference between those things which God did in his wisdom—through which he himself is known—and those things which each of us ought to do or avoid in order to live. It is just like the great difference between material fire, which is divided into parts to be given to individuals, and this general light which illuminates the world. I say this so that what we are about to say may be noted more diligently, and so that we may understand the height of the mystery contained in the one hundred and fifty psalms (about which we began to speak). Indeed, fifteen sets of fifteen portions are found of things that signify and things that are signified together, in which fifteen steps <note>original: "gradus," often referring to the "Songs of Ascents" or Gradual Psalms (120-134)</note> can be assigned. However, five of these are to be considered separately from the ten for the reason prescribed: so that whether through ten times fifteen portions, or through fifteen times ten, we can arrive at the number one hundred and fifty.

### Concerning the fifteen and fifteen men set apart in the mystery often written about, and concerning the twelve understandings which proceed from the threefold fountain of the letter.

Therefore, the steps themselves must first be assigned according to history and according to the harmony <term>harmony: "concordia," Joachim’s method of showing how persons and events in the Old Testament correspond to those in the New Testament and the future Age of the Spirit</term> of the three states within those three states. Although we can assign them according to harmony in the first and second states, in the third state we cannot yet do so at all, for we have not yet arrived at the day and hour in which the Jewish people shall be converted to God. But if, as the opinion holds, Enoch and Elijah—and according to some, Moses, or someone else in the spirit of Moses—are to be revealed, who could better be understood in harmony than they: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; or Zechariah the priest, John the Baptist, and the man Christ Jesus who baptizes in the spirit? 

<column-break/>

For it is clear that Enoch was the father of all the sons of Noah, and in this he had a likeness to Abraham, who is the father of all believers, and to Zechariah, the father of John the Baptist. But Moses was also similar to John the Baptist, because the former baptized in the sea and the latter in the river; each did so to go before him who baptizes in the spirit. Elijah also has a likeness to Christ Jesus, because Elijah received power over fire, and of Christ, John says: <margin>John</margin> "He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire." <note>Matthew 3:11, though the margin notes John [1:33]</note> For the appearance of fire appeared when the Holy Spirit was sent to the apostles. I think, moreover, that when Elijah comes, others will also be chosen by the Holy Spirit to be sent to preach the gospel of the kingdom, just as happened at the start of the second state, when the Son of God came into the world. If, then, there were fifteen men: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and their twelve sons; and fifteen: Zechariah, John the Baptist, the man Christ Jesus, and his twelve apostles (whether in the way we said, or another); then in the beginning of the third state, fifteen similar to them will exist in the future. It is clear that according to history, three steps can be assigned: because what happened in the first state is one thing, what happened in the second is another, and what will happen in the third is another. 

<margin>First step</margin> Thus, in the first step, those fifteen men from the Old Testament are to be taken according to the letter. <margin>Second step</margin> In the second, fifteen from the New [Testament], among whom the Lord Jesus was made as one of them to fulfill all righteousness (as he himself bears witness). <margin>Third step</margin> In the third, fifteen others who are to be revealed in their own time, and who are to be written in the book of the Holy Spirit according to what God knows best. <margin>Fourth step</margin> In the fourth step, historical understanding holds its place, which is the first among the twelve preceding from the fountain of the letter. ### Abbot. Book of the Psalter

...what is or is recognized to have been made in the likeness of those things which were ordained by God: so that while the likeness is maintained, the merits may also be sought. This is why, in the likeness of the twelve patriarchs <note>The twelve sons of Jacob who founded the tribes of Israel.</note> and the twelve apostles, the custom has prevailed that twelve regular monks are directed to a new monastery; which the blessed Benedict <note>St. Benedict of Nursia (c. 480–547), the father of Western monasticism.</note> is described as having done individually in twelve monasteries. But if this is said of the "twelve and twelve," what should be thought of the three fathers? Can a likeness of them be given? I say it can. For the abbot who presides over a monastery owes filial reverence to the bishop. The bishop, in turn, owes it to his father who begot him according to the flesh. Thus, by a fitting enough mystery, these fathers themselves are evaluated: if the first of them is a layman, the second a cleric, and the third a monk, so that no one may glory over the other. Indeed, the three patriarchs are treated simultaneously in this way: Abraham signifies the carnal fathers in the order of the married; Isaac signifies the bishops in the order of the clerics;

and Jacob signifies any prelates <note>High-ranking church officials or superiors.</note> in the order of the monks. In the fifth degree, **moral understanding** holds its place, in which Abraham signifies the outer man; Isaac the inner man who is covered by the flesh; and Jacob the free choice of the will. The five patriarchs <note>Likely referring to the lineage from Abraham to the sons of Jacob.</note> represent the five outer senses: namely, Sight, Hearing, Smell, Taste, and Touch. The remaining seven represent the seven motions of the mind, by which the soul is moved to obtain the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit. For these seven motions are like seven aptitudes by which those gifts can be grasped, just as light is caught by the eye, the word by the ear, an odor by the nostrils, and food by the throat. Finally, those five outer senses are like little vessels of the five virtues: since, indeed, **humility** is exercised in the touch of harsh things; **patience** is exercised in the taste of a bitter drink and tasteless food; **faith** in hearing; **hope** in sight—because through that which is seen, that which is not seen is hoped for; and **love** in smell—because there is nothing that so affects the human mind toward loving as a fragrance 

<column-break/>

that is good and sweet. Hence it is that even if something appears beautiful, and even if it is sweet in the mouth and delightful to the taste, if it is nevertheless foul-smelling, it cannot be loved; but if it is fragrant, even if it is deformed and bitter, it is loved. Whence it is also said in the Song of Songs <note>Song of Solomon 1:3-4.</note> by the voice of the bride: <note>original: "Trahe me post te curremus in odorem vnguentorum tuorum."</note> *“Draw me after you; we will run in the fragrance of your ointments.”* In the sixth degree, **theological understanding** holds its place, which is the third from the historical level. According to this, Abraham signifies the law and ritual; Isaac the Word of God; Jacob the spirit of understanding; and the twelve sons signify the twelve species of that spiritual intellect—that is, the five understandings we wrote of above and which we are speaking of now, and the seven special understandings that were noted in the preceding chapter. In the seventh degree, **contemplative understanding** holds its place, which is known from the historical level. Here, one does not deal with the word that is heard by the ears, but with the affection of vision which is fixed in the eyes of the mind. For it is one thing to hear the teaching of an apostle, and another to contemplate his way of life. According to this understanding, therefore, Abraham signifies the spiritual man; Isaac the Holy Spirit itself; and Jacob the effects of that same Spirit. However much this understanding can also be assigned otherwise: for since the elect of God are named and truly are the children of the Almighty God—especially in that heavenly homeland where there is no servile work, but a service as blessed as it is free—so indeed in Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob we must understand the three persons of the Deity. This is provided that in the twelve sons we understand the one hundred and forty-four thousand who were sealed <note>A reference to the Book of Revelation 7:4 and 14:1-3.</note>, along with the rest of the multitude of saints which belongs to the walls of the city of Jerusalem; especially since it is written in that same place: *“I heard the number of those who were sealed, one hundred and forty-four thousand from all the tribes of the children of Israel.”* That this same number belongs to the walls of the city of Jerusalem is shown elsewhere where John says: *“The angel measured the walls of the city at one hundred and forty-four thousand cubits, by the measure of a man, which is that of an angel.”* <note>Revelation 21:17. Joachim uses the number 144,000 symbolically for the wall's measurements here.</note> And because...

# John, Book One, The Ten-Stringed Psalter

The number twelve is the basis of this, which is divided into five and seven, containing the perfection of two solemn numbers within itself. A little earlier, the same John <note>Referring to St. John the Apostle, the author of the Book of Revelation.</note> had alluded to this, saying: *He measured the city with a golden reed, at twelve thousand stadia.* <note>Revelation 21:15-16. Joachim uses these biblical measurements to justify his numerical symbolism.</note> But this is an **anagogical understanding** <note>original: *intellectus anagogicus*; a method of interpretation that explains how earthly things point toward heavenly realities or the afterlife</note>; and the one we established previously is similarly anagogical. It seems that this understanding has many forms, just like the **typical** <note>original: *typicus*; an interpretation where historical figures or events are "types" or symbols of future ones</note> understanding. However, it should be known that it is one and the same understanding that is called "anagogical"; it does not only touch upon God, but also frequently upon the holy angels and even the souls of the saints established in that eternal fatherland. Finally, the last "typical" form of understanding encompasses the people of the three states <note>Joachim's famous "Three Ages" or states: the Age of the Father (Laymen), the Son (Clerics), and the Holy Spirit (Monks).</note> all together as one. And yet, that form is itself one. In this matter, one should consider that just as Joseph and his two sons were similarly endowed with patriarchal honor—and yet Holy Scripture is accustomed to list twelve tribes—so too are these three <note>Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.</note> mentioned to whom the anagogical understanding is assigned. Nevertheless, that understanding itself is one of the twelve; there is no doubt that this is because of the supreme unity that exists there between God and the holy angels, or men, as the Apostle says: *He who adheres to God is one spirit with Him.* <note>1 Corinthians 6:17.</note> Furthermore, among men, it is one thing to have three kingdoms and three possessions, but quite another for many men to reign with one who presides over all in a single kingdom. Therefore, where there is no variety of character, will, or even of possessions and times, the whole is one, whatever it may be—even if a distinction of "mansions" <note>A reference to "In my Father's house are many mansions" (John 14:2).</note> is not lacking there.

# Father. The Book of the Psalter

...nor was the other church founded by Paul, just as many others were. The seven churches written about in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> are known to have flourished under the blessed John the Evangelist. It is no wonder if seven similar monasteries—representing the seven tribes and seven churches—have not yet flourished in the world. This is because, while the "Time of Peter" <note>Joachim associates the Apostle Peter with the Second Age of the world (the era of the New Testament and the organized Church), which must precede the spiritual era.</note> still remains, John cannot yet exercise his "fierce powers" (if I may put it that way) while Peter survives. However, when that which Peter signifies has passed away, following God with his cross, that which John designates will clearly succeed him.

degrees
</margin>
In the twelfth, thirteenth, and fourteenth degrees, two "states" <note>Joachim’s *status* refers to the three great epochs of history: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.</note> are to be joined two by two: specifically, the first with the second, and this happens twice because of the "twin church." Then the second is joined with the third. This is done so clearly that in the first joining, Israel and the people of Asia (where John rested) are accepted together. In the second, the people of Israel and the Latin people <note>The Western/Roman Church.</note> are joined. In the third, the Latin people and the "people who shall be created" (whom the Lord has made) are joined. 

In the twelfth degree, therefore, we should understand the patriarchs and apostles in **Abraham**; the pontiffs and bishops in **Isaac**; and the prophets and Greek teachers in **Jacob**. In the five sons, we see the five tribes with the five churches. In the remaining seven, we see the seven tribes with the seven churches. This is fitting, because the first of the seven tribes was Benjamin; and Paul, who was from the tribe of Benjamin, fathered children in Christ for the Ephesian church, which was the first 

<column-break/>

among the seven. Thus, the tribe of Benjamin and the Ephesian church seem to be one tribe in spirit—and the same should be understood for the others in a spiritual sense. 

In the thirteenth degree, we find **Abraham** and **Isaac** as described above; but in **Jacob**, we find the prophets and teachers of the Latins. The five tribes and five churches remain as above; but the seven tribes are joined with the seven bishoprics that belong specifically to the Roman Church. 

In the fourteenth degree, **Abraham** signifies the apostles and the prelates of certain monasteries. **Isaac** signifies the successors of both in the second stage. **Jacob** signifies the successors in the third stage. Furthermore, the five sons signify the five patriarchal churches <note>The traditional "Pentarchy": Rome, Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch, and Jerusalem.</note> along with five monasteries; the seven remaining sons signify the seven churches that were in Asia along with seven monasteries near the end of the coming age. 

In the fifteenth degree, which is general, the entire human race is gathered into one. **Abraham** signifies the prelates of the first state. **Isaac** signifies the prelates of the second. **Jacob** signifies the prelates of the third. The five patriarchs signify the five tribes with five churches and five monasteries. The remaining seven signify the seven tribes from the seven churches of Asia and the same number of monasteries in the coming end-times. These things have been said briefly regarding the fifteen degrees so that we may know either which "goods" we lack, or what kind of gifts have been given to us by Him who does all things according to the counsel of His will.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "fifteen steps"—likely referring to the fifteen "Psalms of Ascent" (Psalms 120–134)—and applies a complex allegorical framework to the biblical matriarchs Sarah, Rebecca, and Rachel to explain the different stages of sacred history and spiritual understanding.</meta>

->Abba. Book of the Psalter<-

### On the Significance of Sarah, Rebecca, and Rachel.

**A**mong the great mysteries that have been spoken regarding the fifteen steps <note>The "fifteen steps" or degrees traditionally refer to the fifteen Psalms of Ascent, which were said to be sung on the fifteen steps of the Temple in Jerusalem.</note>, something occurs which must not be passed over in silence. We must ensure we do not say too little, or speak otherwise than we ought; rather, we should assign each part to its proper place through the three and twelve patriarchs. We also provide the significance of those three great women, the wives of the three patriarchs: Sarah, Rebecca, and Rachel. Just as mothers precede their sons, so these three mothers of the faithful people designate three specific understandings within each of the twelve steps <note>original: "singulis gradibus 1 2"</note>. To speak thus, they are to be preferred to the sons. But to return to the matter at hand:

In **History**, Sarah is to be understood as a certain good matron; in Rebecca, a certain good kinswoman; in Rachel, a certain nun <note>original: "sanctimonialis"; referring to a woman dedicated to a holy life.</note>. **Morally**, in Sarah one should see good works; in Rebecca, reading; in Rachel, jubilation. **Tropologically** <term>Tropology: The "moral" or figurative sense of scripture, explaining how one should act.</term>, Sarah represents the <note>original: "litera"</note> letter of the Old Testament; Rebecca, that of the New; and Rachel, the <note>original: "regula"</note> rule or institution of monks. **Contemplatively**, in Sarah is prevenient grace <note>Prevenient grace is the divine grace that precedes human decision.</note>; in Rebecca, cooperating grace; in Rachel, consummating grace. **Anagogically** <term>Anagogy: The spiritual interpretation of scripture that points toward heaven or the end of time.</term>, Sarah is that part of the heavenly city designated by the streets of Israel; Rebecca, that part designated by the suburbs; and Rachel, the city itself. These are the five understandings of Sarah, Rebecca, and Rachel. Leah and the two handmaids are to be taken in other significations. 

According to a **typical** <term>Typical: An interpretation where Old Testament figures "foreshadow" New Testament realities.</term> understanding, the people are distinguished by 14, 14, and 14 generations: that is, from Abraham to David; from David to the Babylonian captivity; and from the Babylonian captivity to Christ. In the first distinction, we see the significance of Sarah; in the second, Rebecca; in the third, Rachel. This is similar in the second and third states. Furthermore, in the fourth, fifth, and sixth types, the times must be doubled according to their concordance: either the times of the first and second state, or the times of the second and third. Let him who fears God know this: it should not be brought forward everywhere, for those without firm understanding cannot carry it. It suffices to speak of the seven types of typical intelligence when dealing with brothers: to assign the first three,

<column-break/>

which pertain to the property of the three Persons <note>Referring to the Trinity: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.</note>, and the last, which regards the unity of the substance. In the seventh type, Sarah signifies the whole Synagogue—not in regard to those rejected, but to the elect. Rebecca signifies the whole Church of the second state. Rachel signifies the future Church of the third state <note>The author is likely Joachim of Fiore, who predicted a "Third Age" of the Holy Spirit, characterized by monastic contemplation.</note>. And this indeed concerns the mystery of the three pious women.

In these things which were said concerning the fifteen steps in the type of the past, this must be especially noted: the "letter," which we said was triple, is not to be included in the number of the "intelligences" <note>The "intelligences" are the spiritual layers of meaning.</note>, because the letter is a simple and brief thing. Spiritual intelligences, however, apply to many things. Therefore, the triple letter is the source of the intelligences; and so it is as valid in each individual case as it is in the three together. For each one fully possesses the intelligences, no less than the three together—just as one Person of the Godhead is no less powerful than the three are together. This must be set apart in the significance of the Psalter. 

Nor should it seem unequal if we say that while some persons represent these general mysteries, the rest of the multitude of the faithful are set apart—whether at the beginning of the first state, the second state, or (as we believe will happen) the beginning of the third. For it is shown that those who were elected at the beginning of the first state were the people of Israel according to the flesh, and those elected at the beginning of the second were the Christian people according to the spirit. Nevertheless, through those who are to be called at the start of the third state, we believe the remnants of the Jews and the Gentiles shall be called to the faith. Because the triple letter is separated from the twelve intelligences, the question remains in this manner: are the ten or the twelve intelligences the same? But it should be known that just as the two elders <note>Refers to Eldad and Medad from Numbers 11:26.</note> were separate from the seventy, though they were not of the number of those who ascended the mountain; and just as Barnabas and Paul were added to the twelve apostles, yet do not belong to the number of the twelve whom the Lord chose from the beginning; so the two "lower" intelligences—the historical and the moral—are added to the other intelligences for the sake of those who receive the inheritance of salvation. Now, regarding these two...

->Joachim, Book One: The Ten-Stringed Psaltery<-

...gathered for the instruction of the faithful: all the other understandings are ten in number. Three of these are superior: namely, the first is **tropological** <term>Tropological: The "moral" sense of scripture, interpreting the text as a guide for how a person should act.</term>, the second is **contemplative**, and the third is **anagogic** <term>Anagogic: The "mystical" or "heavenly" sense, dealing with the soul's journey toward eternal life.</term>. There are also seven species of **typical** <term>Typical: Referring to "types" or figures in the Old Testament that foreshadow the New Testament.</term> understanding, which have been discussed so far. Within these, a special mystery is summarized. Three of these understandings are signified by the three daughters of Job, while seven are signified by his seven sons. Each of these, as shown above, has fifteen proportions; together, they all total one hundred and fifty <note>The number 150 corresponds to the 150 Psalms in the Bible.</note>. And in these ten strings are shown the "great works of the Lord, sought out according to all his wills" <margin>Psalm 111:2</margin>. In those two understandings which were added, it is shown to man what he ought to do and what he ought to avoid. 

But if the ten understandings are distinguished from the two—since there are twelve understandings in total—how is it that there are twelve patriarchs and twelve apostles? Do two of the patriarchs and two of the apostles not belong to the mystery of the ten-stringed psaltery? I say they do indeed belong, and these two also signify something higher than the ten. Certainly, it was said above that five men are to be accepted into the mystery of the Trinity because of the five modes of relationship, and especially so that the Father may be shown as the principle, the Son as the principle, and the Holy Spirit as the principle. If this must be held, no fewer than fifteen men would suffice for the summation of the psaltery. For if the Father is designated in Abraham, the Son in Isaac, and the Holy Spirit in Jacob; and again, the Father in Isaac, the Son in Jacob, and the Holy Spirit in Joseph; and again, the Father in Jacob, the Son in Joseph, and the Holy Spirit in Ephraim; or, as the cause of harmony requires here: the Father in Jacob, the Son in Judah, and the Holy Spirit in Joseph—it is clear that there are only ten remaining to whom the mystery of the sacred strings must be adapted. Therefore, if we wish to hold to the first arrangement, Levi and Dan must be separated from the number of the others. If the second: Dan and Joseph. If the third: Judah and Joseph. As for Levi, there is no question that he is sometimes separated from the number of the twelve <note>In some biblical lists, Levi is omitted as the tribe dedicated to the priesthood, who held no land.</note>. That Dan should also sometimes be omitted is clearly shown by John...

<column-break/>

...in that place where he says: "I heard the number of those who were sealed from every tribe of the sons of Israel" <margin>Revelation 7:4</margin>. When he came to the list, Dan was omitted and Manasseh was written in his place. Therefore, in the New Testament, the mystery of the Trinity must be understood in the same way sometimes: in Christ Jesus and the two great apostles, namely Peter and John. In the true man Christ Jesus, we perceive the likeness of the Father; in Peter, that of the Son; in John, that of the Holy Spirit. In the remaining ten apostles, we find the mystery of the ten strings. 

Alternatively, as in the Old Testament, where the likeness of the Son is sometimes in Benjamin and the Holy Spirit in Joseph, so it is in the New: the likeness of the Son is in James and the Holy Spirit in John. Indeed, just as the ten brothers were once jealous of those two <note>Referring to the Joseph and Benjamin, sons of Rachel.</note>, here the ten apostles were at one time indignant toward the two <note>Referring to Matthew 20:24, where the ten were angry with James and John for seeking the highest seats.</note>. Therefore, just as Joseph and Benjamin, the sons of Rachel, were in a certain way separated from the company of others for a specific reason, and just as James and John seemed to have asked the Lord for a certain private glory apart from the rest (causing the ten who heard it to be indignant), so it is that one thing is required by the likeness of the psaltery itself, and another belongs to the ten strings. 

But if James and John are to be accepted in this way with Christ as a likeness of the psaltery, and the ten remaining disciples as a likeness of the strings according to the three types of teachers—then the ten understandings belonging to the ten strings appear fitting. And to the likeness of those two understandings that do not belong to the strings, two "last" apostles were chosen outside of that solemn number of the twelve <note>Likely referring to Paul and Barnabas.</note>. "Oh, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are His judgments, and how unsearchable His ways!" <note>original: "O vere altitudo sapie z sciētie dei: qᷓ icōp̄hēhibilia sūt iudicia eius: z inuestigabiles vie eius." Romans 11:33</note>. "In the sea," says David, "are Your ways, O Lord, and Your paths are in many waters, and Your footsteps will not be known. You led Your people like sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron" <note>Psalm 77:19-20</note>. 

But it is necessary for us to adapt those things said about the five men and the threefold assignment of the psaltery into a **figure** <term>Figure: A visual diagram or symbolic drawing used by Joachim to explain his complex theological systems.</term>, according to our custom. Thus, by bringing the image of the psaltery before the eyes of the flesh, the spiritual eyes of the mind may be opened to understanding—the mud (so to speak) having been cast aside.

->John the First: The Ten Strings<-

# Concerning the one hundred and fifty proportions of spiritual understandings.

It was not our original purpose to enter through so many narrow ways of God, or to take up wings like an eagle to complete everything that has been said; for many more things have occurred to me on this journey which I did not know before. It was not our intent to speak of these fifteen understandings in a serial order. But because we have touched the "Key of David"—which He holds who opens and no one shuts—we have <margin>Revelation <note>original: "Apor."/Apocalypsis</note></margin> seemed, at least in part, to have entered His tabernacle through an open door, and to have reached the places of the treasures of the wisdom and knowledge of God; yet we have brought forth only a small portion of what we were able to find. Now, therefore, giving thanks to Him who freely bestows both Himself and His gifts upon the chosen, let us return to ourselves and finish the rest of our journey by a single brief path, especially since a long road still remains for us in the other small works to which we are committed. We began to treat the number of the Psalms in this second book, and simultaneously, because of them, the fifteen steps and the ten strings. On that occasion—with the encouragement of Him who invited us to His banquet—we presumed to fly toward the contemplation of the perfection of the <term>number ten<note>The "denarius," representing the Ten Commandments or the completion of the literal Law.</note></term> and the <term>number fifteen<note>The "quindenarius," representing the spiritual ascent or the "Gradual" Psalms of the Temple steps.</note></term>. We have seen what pertains to the psaltery, what to the ten strings, and even what to the fifteen steps. We see how Jacob with two sons and ten other patriarchs, or even the man Christ Jesus with two disciples and the remaining ten apostles, possess within themselves the fullness of this <term>sacrament<note>Here used in the broader sense of a "holy mystery" or "sacred sign."</note></term>. Thus, they themselves also appear to be a kind of spiritual psaltery designed to signify all the things we have mentioned, according to the words of the <margin>Psalm</margin> Psalmist: *Awake, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp*, etc. Now it is pleasing to consider whether the one hundred and fifty proportions <note>Refers to the 150 Psalms interpreted through various spiritual lenses.</note> which fall under these understandings—according to the number of the fifteen men who were given at the beginnings of the two testaments to designate so great a mystery, among whom is the man Christ Jesus, who did not despise becoming all things to crush the arrogance of our presumption—pertain to the fifteen

<column-break/>

steps; and if this is so, what the cause of such a secret and venerable mystery might be. That it is indeed so is sufficiently organized in the writings above. For if there are ten understandings pertaining to the psaltery, and each one receives its own individual testimony regarding the matter at hand, those ten understandings cannot fail to show the one hundred and fifty proportions for which the fifteen persons were assumed into the cause of the mystery. For if one treats of the <term>tropological<note>The moral sense of Scripture, explaining how the reader should act.</note></term> understanding, it is clear it has fifteen proportions. If one treats of the **contemplative** understanding, it is the same, and so with the rest. Yet this is done in such a way that the three women, the wives of the patriarchs, are taken up to complete this number, so that they appear as twelve and twelve, as if being born from the mothers. For example: the tropological understanding has fifteen proportions; three of these, which consist in the letter of both testaments and the mysteries of the Church, are signified in **Sarah, Rebecca, and Rachel**. The twelve understandings of spiritual intellect are signified in the twelve sons. And note that the **letter** <note>The literal or surface meaning of the text.</note> seems to be a "feminine" thing because it is weak, while spiritual understandings require a more masculine mind, robust in the integrity of faith. The cause of the mystery, however, is that this number—which consists of three <term>Jubilees<note>A Jubilee is 50 years; 3 x 50 equals the 150 Psalms.</note></term>—embraces almost everything by a certain most hidden art of God. Therefore, if we intend to assign the fullness of the cause by the gift of Almighty God, we cannot do so if a diversity of causes brings about forgetfulness. For the fact that the psaltery has ten strings is due to the cause that the first two understandings do not pertain to the joy of the psalms, but rather to the mourning of penance which must be set before <term>neophytes<note>New converts or beginners in the spiritual life.</note></term> and those recently converted from the vanity of the world. But that there are fifteen steps, for which there are proper songs in the Book of Psalms, and that we have accepted fifteen named men to intimate the sacred mystery, is for this cause: that every single thing over which this mystery hangs can be propagated in the aforementioned understandings up to the number fifteen, but it does not proceed beyond that same limit. For example: **Moses** and **Aaron** led the children of Israel out...

### ¶ On the one hundred and fifty proportions of the spiritual intelligences.

**I**t was not our intention to enter through such narrow ways of God, nor to take up wings like an eagle to fulfill everything that has been said; for many things occurred to me on the path which I did not know before. It was not originally our purpose to speak of these fifteen <term>intelligences</term> <note>Ways of understanding scripture spiritually</note> in sequence. But because <margin>Apocalypse <note>Revelation 3:7</note></margin> we have touched upon the "key of David," which He holds who opens and no one shuts, we have seemed (at least in part) to have entered his tabernacle through an open door, and to have reached the places of the treasures of the wisdom and knowledge of God; yet what we have been able to bring forth is but a small thing. Now, therefore, giving thanks to Him who freely bestows Himself and His gifts upon the elect, let us return to ourselves. <meta>Continuing the discussion from the previous page regarding the fifteen "spiritual intelligences" (ways of interpreting scripture) and how they relate to the structure of the Psalter and the progression of sacred history.</meta>

# Abbot: Book of the Psalter <note>This likely refers to Joachim of Fiore, often called "Abba" or "Abbot" in medieval manuscripts</note>

<margin>Psalm</margin> ...from the land of Egypt. According to the harmony of the reigns, there are two <note>referring to pairs of figures</note> at the beginning of the second state, and two at the beginning of the third state. In the beginning of the second state <note>Joachim’s "Second Status" or Age of the Son/New Testament</note> were **Paul** and **Barnabas**, who went before the faithful by preaching, so that they might show them the way; having left behind the synagogue, they entered into the deserts of the Gentiles. Those in the beginning of the third state <note>The Age of the Holy Spirit</note> will be recognized in their own time. Behold, we have three historical levels: **Moses** and **Aaron** signify certain faithful men who come together as one and give their effort to liberating the helpless from the hand of one stronger than him <note>Original Latin: "manu fortioris eius" – a reference to Psalm 35:10</note>. Moses fights; Aaron signifies the one who works well. Moses is a man devoted to prayer, insistent upon it; for when these two kinds of good come together in action and prayer, they liberate the affections of the soul from the power of vices. They remove those affections from the carnal desires which war against the soul, and they prepare the way which leads to life, leading them to tranquility of mind.

**Tropologically** <note>In a moral sense, applying the text to the individual's soul</note>, while Moses signifies the spiritual teacher, Aaron signifies the scholarly man who has a learned tongue. When these two come together in the bond of peace—so that what one understands, the other speaks—they rescue spiritual understandings and those who have been given the ability to grasp them from the power of heresies; through many labors of writing, they lead them to the knowledge of the truth.

**Contemplatively**, Moses and Aaron signify any two spiritual men living in solitude, such as were **Elijah** and **Elisha**. The love of God snatched one of them to the stars <note>referring to Elijah's ascent</note>; the love of his neighbor compelled the other to preside over the multitude of the sons of the prophets. For the life of Moses seemed to pertain to the love of God, and the life of Aaron to the love of neighbor; because one of them attended to divine things, and the other to human things. Furthermore, these two given roles liberate spiritual men—the "Israelites" who carry spiritual virtues in the vessels of their hearts—from the slavery of the Egyptians. They do this so that they do not perish among secular men through human flatteries and favors, but are rather drawn into the solitudes of monasteries. There they may exercise their virtues, where only the love of God and the charity of religious brothers is the cause; without which (as the Apostle witnesses <note>Referring to St. Paul in 1 Corinthians 13</note>) whatever other gifts of the Holy Spirit one possesses are idle. Knowing that those who fight against vices in this way quickly obtain the reward of peace. And it should be noted that in the moral understanding, it deals with the battle of bodily 

<column-break/>

vices. In the **tropological** sense, it deals with the battle against heresies. In the **contemplative** sense, it deals with the battle against the spiritual attacks of the devil.

And indeed, that battle which pertains to morality is designated in the crossing of the Red Sea; that which pertains to the tropological is in the temptation of the desert; and those which pertain to the contemplative are designated in the bitter wars of the **Philistines**.

According to the **anagoge** <note>The mystical or heavenly sense</note>, Aaron—which is interpreted as "mountain of strength"—signifies the **Son**; Moses signifies the **Holy Spirit**. The children of Israel who were in Egypt signify the children of the Holy Spirit, who are in this world and are afflicted by those who are not "according to the flesh" <note>Original: "non sunt f[oris] m[undum] carnem"</note>. They liberate them from the Egyptians, and lead them through the hardships of the wilderness to the land of promise; because through death and the fire of purgation, they lead them to rest. These are the five understandings. What of the seven?

### ¶ On the seven spiritual understandings

In the first type of the **typical** <note>Symbolic/Figurative</note> understanding, Moses signifies the prophets; Aaron, the priests. Egypt signifies the multitude of carnal Jews who were zealous for the Law according to the letter and the sacrifices which the Lord confesses to detest. The children of Israel signify spiritual men, such as those who dwelled in Bethel and Jericho; and indeed, following the examples and admonition of Moses and Elisha, departing from the company of the carnal synagogue, they aspired with all their strength to the society of the just.

In the second type, Aaron signifies the priests of the Church; Moses, the teachers. The children of Israel, who at the voice of Moses and Aaron exited Egypt and entered the desert, designate those pious Christians who, having left behind the pleasure of the flesh, offer themselves to the company of the **canons regular** <note>Priests living in a community under a religious rule</note>. Their vow is to live in chastity and abstain from carnal desires which war against the soul.

In the third type, Moses signifies men of contemplation; Aaron signifies spiritual abbots. These indeed pertain to this state, but are not exempt from labor. Following those contemplatives and abbots who are in [the world], they shall be as if on a journey to enter into the land...

# Abba: The Book of the Psalter

<margin>Genesis</margin> That man was Jacob: who after seven and seven years <note>fourteen years</note> of his servitude, when Joseph was born to him, decided to return to his own country: and yet, having renewed the pact, he served again for the flocks for six years. But also the temple of the Lord, first built by Solomon and destroyed by the king of Babylon: the children of the exile <note>original: "transmigrationis," referring to the Babylonian Captivity</note> indeed began to rebuild it a second time, and a little later they stopped; then, having received permission to build, it reached completion in six continuous years. Therefore, as I think: just as the first state after long labor deserved to have a brief sabbath, and the second state after a similarly long labor is nonetheless to have a brief sabbath: so, on the contrary, the third state—of a brief time indeed even if not of brief labor—is to have a transition, but a whole and perfect sabbath. And enough has been said about these things for this place. In the fourth species of symbolic understanding <note>original: "typice intelligentie"</note>: the Greeks are to be taken together with those who believed from the circumcision <note>Jewish converts</note>: because they too had received the law until Christ came into the world: from which Paul commands them to "sabbatize" <note>original: "sabbatizare," meaning to keep a spiritual rest or Sabbath</note> in his epistle addressed to the Galatians. In the fifth species, the Latins are to be taken with those who believed from the circumcision, as sons with their fathers. According to how Sarah signifies both at once: that is, the one Church of the righteous from the time of Sarah herself until the end of the second state, in which her childbirth also accelerates. Indeed, her conception was in the advent of the Lord; her birth, either in the time or around the times of the Antichrist. Moreover, there will also be a sabbath for her after the tribulation which the unfaithful nations shall cause; when also all the power of Babylon shall be scattered and shall be scattered forever. In the sixth species, the people of the third state must be joined with the people of the second: as those who fight together under one New Testament: although that last one is as if in one hour, so that it may receive one reward of eternal retribution. And according to this, that time is to be taken as the sabbath, which we called the third arising from the two. In the seventh species, the people of God shall have a general sabbath, with respect to the six ages of the world: and especially that sabbath of which the Apostle says: There remains

<column-break/>

a sabbath rest for the people of God <note>Hebrews 4:9</note>. And if we know the matter well, the mystery of the sabbaths is assigned in fifteen ways; so that through the three or four examples <note>original: "pla," likely an abbreviation for "exempla"</note> which have been given by us, the reader may say: "By this door let me enter into the tabernacle of my God," and gratefully draw what is free, in joy from the fountains of the Savior; as the Lord said to the Samaritan woman: "Whoever drinks of this water will thirst again; but whoever drinks of the water which I shall give him, it shall become in him a fountain of water springing up into eternal life" <note>John 4:13-14</note>. But let us repeat the propositions: how from the three patriarchs there arose the twelve sons of Israel; so from the threefold beginning of the letter, there arise twelve ritual understandings for all. And just as from the twelve sons of Israel proceeded the twelve tribes, a multitude like the sand of the sea: so from the ten understandings <note>original: "intelligentijs"</note>, innumerable expositions go forth; so much so that the world would sooner fail than a mortal man could exhaust the depth of such fullness. Truly, because according to the ten strings of the psalter <note>the decachord or ten-stringed harp mentioned in the Psalms</note>, there are ten understandings by which we comprehend a certain fullness of the works and gifts of God: therefore surely these things are extended even to the number fifteen; so that all things or modes which are dealt with are 150. Because even if the words of the letter reach a limit, the number remains in those things which are designated. For there are neither more nor more authoritative species concerning which one deals in the "tropic" <note>moral or figurative</note> understanding than fifteen, nor more parts concerning which one deals in the contemplative understanding than fifteen, and so with the other eight. Now if there are ten understandings, and each one has fifteen proportions <note>the math of 10x15=150</note>: it is clear that both ten times fifteen and fifteen times ten are the proportions; through this there are ten strings, and fifteen steps <note>likely referring to the 15 Psalms of Ascents or "Gradual" Psalms</note>, and the psalms numbering 150. Let something now be done concerning the way of this exile, according to the boundaries of the fifteen steps, the number of the ten strings, and the 150 psalms: it is pleasing to consider the generations from the beginning of the age until the end, so that we may know that which the Psalmist says: "Great is our Lord, and great is his power, and of his wisdom there is no number" <note>Psalm 147:5</note>.

<meta>This page continues Joachim of Fiore’s mathematical and symbolic exploration of history. # Joachim, First Book of the Ten-Stringed Psaltery

If indeed we count the generations of the ages in order, beginning from Adam—who was the first parent of all—the beginning is found in almost every decade <note>original: "decadum," referring to groups of ten generations</note> of generations; and everywhere the mystery of the sacred Trinity is manifest and clear. Yet, so that there are not many Trinities but only one, it was not necessary for each individual step to have thirteen persons, as if the mystery of the Trinity were assigned to the first three, and the ten perfections to the ten following—for there are three "horns" of the psaltery and ten strings <note>The "psaltery of ten strings" is Joachim's primary symbol; the triangular frame represents the Trinity (the three corners or "horns"), and the strings represent the Ten Commandments or ten virtues</note>—but in one step alone, three remain in which the mystery of the Trinity is primarily assigned. This is to show that there are only three who work all things together in all: namely Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For although it is believed that Adam performed true penance for his guilt, and although God himself testified that Noah <note>original: "Moe," an OCR error for "Noe"</note> was a just man, it is never read that God said: "I am the God of Adam," or "I am the God of Noah." Instead, He said: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob."

However, these three alone remain because they cannot be limited to individual decades; rather, it was necessary for the same mystery that appeared in Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to appear in other persons in every step <note>original: "gradu," often translated as "degree" or "stage" of history</note>, so that the mystery of our salvation might be present in all things. This ensures that no one thinks God remains only in one private dwelling of the righteous, such that others cannot enjoy the presence of His vision. Therefore, while the sacred mystery of the Trinity shines more clearly in those three than in others, it is nonetheless contained in every step—just as it is in the third step, over which they preside. In all steps, a uniform number of persons is found to complete the mystery.

It was brought about in a wonderful way that the first three persons of a subsequent decade would also be the end of the preceding decade. This mirrors how Zechariah the priest, John the Baptist, and the man Jesus Christ were the mediators between each Testament, so that under them the time of the Law was completed and the time of Grace began. Hence Christ is called the "cornerstone," because He willed the precepts of the Law to be observed in Himself as they appeared, yet He also, through Himself,

<column-break/>

gathered some disciples into whom He would pour the freedom of grace, sending them through the whole world to preach to all nations and baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Thus, these three persons who are above the number of the decades and seem segregated from the rest must be understood within the mystery of the Trinity. It is as if they can be found in every step and yet cannot be held by any single one; so that when we deal with the first step only, they are thought to be at the beginning and not at the end, and similarly when we deal with the second.

For example, from Adam to Arphaxad <note>The grandson of Noah</note>, there are twelve generations. In their beginning and in their end, they contain the mystery of the Trinity. However, when we discuss this step, that mystery is not to be sought at the end of those generations, but at the beginning. We have said that the last three generations are to be taken as both the end and the beginning, just like the man Christ Jesus, John the Baptist, and Zechariah his father. For this reason, when we pass to the second step, we must not begin from the son of Arphaxad, but from the third generation before him—that is, from Noah, his grandfather. Thus, from Noah to Jacob, there were thirteen generations. Indeed, so many were necessary for the consummation of the mystery.

As for the fact that from Adam to Arphaxad there are not thirteen generations but twelve, the reason is this: Abel—in whose place God set another "seed" for Eve, from whom the "children of God" proceeded—must be accepted in the place of one generation. This follows the cause of a great mystery pertaining to this matter, which we shall speak of in the following pages, as God grants. But if the last three generations are to be repeated in each individual step, it appears that there are only ten generations that determine each step, while three are added from the following one to complete the sacred mystery; and again, those same three are repeated to be written as the first in their own step, so that they seem to be both first and last. This is surely because God himself says: "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end." <margin>Revelation</margin>

For if we assign the mystery of the Trinity to Adam and his two sons, it is like the psaltery of ten strings having within itself the "horns" of the Trinity. In the likeness of the ten virtues which are signified by the ten strings, the ten must be accepted...

Having established the "ten-stringed psaltery" as a model for time, he now details how the lineages from Adam to Jacob fit into this Trinitarian structure, assigning specific patriarchs to represent the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit across three distinct "degrees" or stages of history.</meta>

# Father. The Book of the Psaltery

The subsequent generations—the names of all of which we shall write in the following—are to be understood in this way: in the first degree <note>Joachim uses "degrees" (*gradus*) to mark major shifts in the revelation of the Trinity through time.</note>, Adam, Abel, and Seth are to be taken as representing the mystery of the Trinity. Then Noah, Shem, and Arphaxad are to be taken in the likeness of the three last strings. I say "other" because these three strings signify Faith, Hope, and Charity, so that in this very thing a likeness of the Trinity itself may be seen to exist in some measure; for these are the three virtues without which the Triune God cannot be possessed. Furthermore, in the second degree, Noah, Shem, and Japheth carry the mystery of the Trinity. The ten generations that follow from Salah, son of Arphaxad, down to Jacob, carry the type of the ten virtues, and so on for the others. But here too, for the sake of the mystery of life, Arphaxad and Japheth are placed; why this was done will appear below when we deal with the third degree—namely, because mysteries are recognized even in the "third heaven" <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 12:2, implying a state of high spiritual revelation.</note>. These things having been necessarily tasted beforehand as a little preface, we must now come to the unweaving of this web of generations, so that each thing may be shown within its proper limits.

<margin>Genesis</margin>
Adam, who was the first parent and the primitive root of this line, fathered Abel, whom Cain killed, and Seth, of whom the mother [Eve] said: "God has appointed for me another seed in place of Abel, whom Cain killed." <margin>Genesis</margin> Adam signifies in this mystery Him from whom all fatherhood in heaven and on earth is named <note>The Father; reference to Ephesians 3:15</note>. The just Abel, who was killed for his righteousness by his own brother, represents the one who was to suffer at the hands of his brothers for the sake of righteousness, as it is written. Seth, who was given to the mother in place of Abel, represents Him of whom the Son spoke at the time of His passion: <margin>John</margin> "I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Comforter" <note>original: "aliū paraclitiū"; referring to the Holy Spirit.</note>. Behold, in these three is the likeness of the psaltery. The names of those which signify the ten strings are these: <margin>Joshua?</margin> First, Enos; second, Cainan; third, Mahalalel; fourth, Jared; fifth, Enoch; sixth, Methuselah; seventh, Lamech; eighth, Noah; ninth, Shem; tenth, Arphaxad. These are in the first degree. In the second, however, it is thus: Noah, a just man who was the father of all succeeding peoples—for all who were not his sons died in the flood, except for his wife and the wives of his sons—signifies God the Father, who made and rules the fabric of the entire 

<column-break/>

world. Shem truly, from whose seed Christ was born according to the flesh along with the Jewish people, signifies Christ himself, who is the father of Christians. Japheth, in whose seed the grace of the Holy Spirit was poured out and from whom the Church was chosen to be the spirit of Christ, signifies the Holy Spirit, who appeared in the likeness of a dove, so that the Church might show it has His special likeness, according to what is written in the Song of Songs: "One is my dove" <note>original: "Una ē colūba mea"; Song of Songs 6:9</note>. And by the blessing: "May God enlarge Japheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem" <note>Genesis 9:27</note>; for it is the part of the bride to enter the house of the husband and dwell in it, just as Rebecca, coming from afar to her husband, entered and dwelt in the tent of Sarah. Behold, in these is the likeness of the psaltery. The names which signify the ten strings are these: First, Salah; second, Eber; third, Peleg; fourth, Reu; fifth, Serug; sixth, Nahor; seventh, Terah; eighth, Abraham. In the third degree: Abraham, ninth Isaac, tenth Jacob. The Father of the faithful <note>Abraham</note> signifies the Father; Isaac the Son; Jacob the Holy Spirit. Now it is time for us to release ourselves from the first degree: in the first degree, Abel, because he was outside the line <note>Abel died without heirs, so the physical "line" of descent continued through Seth.</note>, signified the Son. Seth, however, the brother who remains in the line, signifies the Holy Spirit. In the second degree it is different: Shem, who remains in the line, signifies the Son. Japheth, who remains outside the line and was his brother, signifies the Holy Spirit. In the third, it is thus: Isaac signifies the Son, and Jacob his son signifies the Holy Spirit, and both remain in the line. **A Great Mystery:** in the first degree it is shown that the Son and the Spirit proceed from the Father in the time of justice; but nevertheless, only he who signifies the Holy Spirit remains in the line. This is because in the time of justice, the Son remained hidden and was sacrificed daily in mystery and was not known; but they spoke more manifestly through the Holy Spirit, especially in the prophets, and He was shown to remain and work with the Father, even if those carnal people did not understand what they read. In the second degree, the same is shown: that both proceed from God the Father, yet both remain; because Jesus was recognized in this second state as being the Son of God, and the Holy Spirit as proceeding from the Father. The line of generations remains here in the Son, because in the Latin people to whom he was sent, Peter, who held...

Joachim is specifically addressing the controversy of the "Filioque" (the Western belief that the Holy Spirit proceeds from both the Father and the Son), using the lineage of the patriarchs—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—as a symbolic proof. # Joachim, the Second [Book] of the Ten-Stringed [Psaltery]

held the suffering of Christ <note>original: "passi xpī"</note>: rather than in the Greek manner. To this John went, who signifies the Holy Spirit. The succession of the patriarchs remains so that the only-begotten of God, who in the time of the first state <note>The "first state" refers to the age of the Old Testament / the Father.</note> did not receive honor from that people, might receive it from another in the second state; as he himself said: *For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.* <note>John 5:22–23</note> Furthermore, that in the third degree Jacob, who signifies the Holy Spirit, proceeded from Isaac, signifies that which the Greeks deny proceeds: namely, that the Holy Spirit [proceeds] from the Son and is given by him just as by the Father. This was designated in the third degree rather than in the first or second, so that in the third state of the age <note>The "third state" is Joachim’s predicted future age of spiritual peace and monasticism.</note>, the truth of this sacrament might become clearly known to Greeks and Latins, Jews and Gentiles, all professing with one voice and saying that Jesus is the Son of God, and that the Holy Spirit proceeds no less from him than from the Father. As the Son himself says of him: 
<margin>John</margin>
*He will glorify me, because he will take from what is mine and announce it to you.* <note>John 16:14</note> And in another place: *If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink,* etc. <note>John 7:37</note> Therefore, as is fitting for the mystery, both remain together in the line: those peoples who are now divided will be made one people and one flock, so that they may truly be *a chosen race and a holy nation*, and there may be *one fold and one shepherd.* <note>1 Peter 2:9; John 10:16</note> For it shall not be as it was with Shem and Japheth—which was fulfilled in the Greeks and Latins—where two lines proceeded; instead, there shall be one nation and one people created for the praise of God, knowing their God perfectly from the least to the greatest. It seems that this first degree pertains to the villages, the second to the suburbs, and the third to the city, especially because city-dwellers are wise; and among them, Paul speaks wisdom. But enough of these things; having discharged our debt, let us return to our path and carry out what we began. Abraham, as we said, signifies God the Father; Isaac the Son; Jacob the Holy Spirit. Truly, the descendants of those who signify this, which are the ten strings, are these: **First, Judah; second, Perez; third, Hezron; fourth, Ram; fifth, Amminadab; sixth, Nahshon; seventh, Salmon; eighth, Boaz; ninth, Obed; tenth, Jesse.** Here also, something must be considered according to what was said above concerning the Holy Spirit, lest

<column-break/>

anyone should think (since Seth, Japheth, and Jacob are not born of their fathers alone <note>The author is clarifying the nature of "procession" versus "birth" to avoid a literal, biological misunderstanding of the Trinity.</note>) that the Holy Spirit was born of the Father and the Son, as if from a father and a mother; on the contrary, the Holy Spirit is shown in certain places of the Scriptures to have the likeness of a woman. Therefore, lest he be thought to be born in the same way as the Son of God, the likeness of him was changed from this point forward and transferred into a specific person who was neither the brother nor the son of that person who signifies the Son, but only his contemporary. Therefore, in the third degree, we must begin from Boaz, who was the grandfather of Jesse and the great-grandfather of David. Now, this Boaz was a merciful and good man who, among other works of mercy, did not despise taking a foreign woman <note>A reference to Ruth the Moabite.</note> who was poor and needy as his wife; for which reason God also blessed him, giving him a son named Obed, who was the father of Jesse and the grandfather of David, from whose seed Christ was born. Now, Naomi, who went away to sojourn—or rather, departed because of the famine in the land of Judah—signifies that part of the Synagogue of the Jews which, because the prosperity promised to the children of Israel by the prophets did not happen according to the letter, suffered a famine regarding faith. As if in despair, she went to sojourn among the Gentiles, and especially among the Greek people, who from the days of Alexander [the Great] had dominated Israel as well as other nations in those parts. The two sons of Naomi designate the two peoples into which the kingdom of David had been divided: namely, Judah and Israel; or certainly the two tribes that remained when the ten were carried away to the Assyrians: namely, Judah and Benjamin. Moreover, they themselves died, as did their father; 
<margin>Kings</margin>
because both the priests, who were of the tribe of Levi, and the people themselves failed in faith, since even among those nations things did not go well for them, but were always adverse. For they did not seek after any prosperity of the spirit, but only of the flesh; nor did they long for the heavenly homeland, but for the earthly one, because *as the earthly man is, so also are the earthly.* <note>1 Corinthians 15:48</note> The woman remained alone after the men died; because when the fighting men and those who comforted her in the Lord regarding the prosperity of the world failed, she herself remained like a widowed woman without any hope, and she decided to return to her own land: that is, to the ancient humility in which they had lived.

### Abbot. The Book of the Psaltery

his fathers from the beginning not having here a lasting inheritance, but seeking one to come <note>original: "non habentes hic manentem hereditatem: sed futuram inquirentes"; a reference to Hebrews 13:14</note>. Now two women, the wives of her sons who had died, clung to Naomi; yet one turned back, because she was not strong in faith. Because of those who were translated into the midst, and those who were in Egypt—the land in which the Greeks were reigning—some from the nations joined the Jews so that they might keep the law of the one God. However, the Easterners, as if having no foundation, went backward. But among the Greeks, after the translation of the Law which Ptolemy <note>Ptolemy II Philadelphus, the king credited with commissioning the Septuagint, the Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note>, king of the Greeks, caused to be translated, many clung firmly to the Jews. Thus, in the primitive Church, which was once loathed by the Gentiles, it is established that many Greeks were present from the beginning. It is manifest that these were proselytes <note>term: proselytos (converts to Judaism)</note>; otherwise, the zealots of the Law would not have allowed them to participate with them. Therefore, Ruth the Moabite designates that portion of the Gentiles which had clung to the Jews in faith and had been made one people with the Jews when Christ came into the world. Whence she responded appropriately to her mother-in-law 
<margin>Ruth</margin> who was opposing her and saying that she should return to her own gods and her own people; Ruth said: "Your God shall be my God, and your people shall be my people" <note>Ruth 1:16</note>. For the Jews always held the Gentiles as hateful, and when the Gentiles wished to follow them, the Jews resisted them with harsh words, saying: "We are the people of God who are of the seed of Abraham." Yet the Gentiles prevailed in faith, and many fled from the very beginning to the worship of the one God. Among their number was Rahab, the mother of this Boaz, and this Ruth of whom we speak, and many others. For now the Jews cannot say that Christ was to be born only from their patriarchs, since besides these, Rahab and Ruth were from the Gentiles; and yet from them was born David, from whose seed Christ was to be born, just as they themselves confess with one voice alongside us. Whence Obed appeared to have, as it were, two mothers in a common house: because the only-begotten Son of God—whom Obed designates, as appears clearly from these words—was born from the Jews and the Gentiles. 
<margin>Isaiah</margin> Whence also the prophet says: "Send forth the lamb, O Lord, the ruler of the earth, from the rock of the desert to the mountain of the daughter of Zion" <note>Isaiah 16:1</note>. And indeed this Obed

<column-break/>

was not the son of Naomi, but was like a son; to Ruth he was not "like" a son, but truly a son. For Christ esteemed the Church more as a mother, which in faith brings forth his members, than the Synagogue of the Jews, from whom he was born according to the flesh. Truly, the birth of the Spirit was not replaced by the birth of the flesh; rather, the birth of the flesh preceded as a figure for the birth of the Spirit. For when it was said to him by a certain person: "Behold, your mother and your brothers are outside seeking you," he responded, saying: "Who is my mother and who are my brothers?" And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said: "Behold my mother and my brothers. For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother and sister and mother" <note>Matthew 12:47–50</note>. Therefore, Boaz bears the type <note>term: typum (a symbolic figure or foreshadowing)</note> of God the Father, and Obed of the only-begotten Son of God, born of the Virgin. Truly, the likeness of the Holy Spirit—who is neither the generator nor the generated, and seeks a spiritual union rather than a carnal one—is received clearly from this point: that it was designated neither in a brother, as in the brothers Abel and Seth, nor in his own son, as in Jacob the son of Isaac. Rather, it was designated in the king, by Samuel the prophet, who anointed the grandson of this Obed <note>David</note> as king by the Lord’s command. This was to signify in him the rule of the priests, which was given to the people of the nations, while the proud people of the Jews were rejected—which was signified in Saul. For Sophon <note>Likely Zuph or a reference to the ancestry of Samuel (1 Samuel 1:1).</note> was the father of Samuel, in whom the histories of the kings were initiated; he was a contemporary of this Obed, the father of Jesse. Samuel was a contemporary of Jesse, who was the father of David. Therefore, although Samuel was not the son of Boaz (in the way that Seth was the son of Adam and Japheth the son of Noah), nor the son of Obed (as Jacob was the son of Isaac), he is clearly recognized in a similar generation according to the course of time. For from this hour the likeness of the Spirit began, even though until Christ there was a certain fierce struggle between the house of Saul and the house of David; for while certain prophets were tending toward higher things, the multitude of the carnal people tended toward lower things. Therefore, Boaz signifies Almighty God, and Obed the only-begotten Son of God.

## ->Joachim: Second Book of the Ten Strings<-

...is the Son of Man, so that He may yet be true God from true God <note>original: "verus deus de deo vero"; a phrase from the Nicene Creed</note>. Samuel, however, represents the Holy Spirit. Now, the names of those who signify the ten strings <note>The "ten strings" refers to the *Psalterium Decem Chordarum*, the ten-stringed psaltery mentioned in the Psalms, which Joachim uses as a symbolic framework for the Trinity and history.</note> are these: first, David; second, Solomon; third, Rehoboam; fourth, Abijah; fifth, Asa; sixth, Jehoshaphat; seventh, Joram; eighth, Ahaziah; ninth, Joash; and tenth, Amaziah. Here are completed the forty-two generations from Adam; in their fulfillment, the New Testament was initiated in the prophets, beginning with Hosea and Isaiah. From this point, the "likeness of the flesh" <note>original: "similitudo carnis"</note> began to weaken entirely, while the "likeness of the spirit" <note>original: "similitudo spiritus"</note> began to be strengthened—not only regarding the Holy Spirit, but also regarding the Father. Nor should we pass over in silence why, from the beginning, when men still seemed to be carnal, God wished to be likened to some of those born of the patriarchs according to the nature of the flesh—because flesh proceeds from flesh—and then, in the course of time, to remove the carnal likeness and exhibit a spiritual one, which is far more blessed than that of the flesh. But first, we must show how that which is natural <note>original: "animale," often translated as "soulish" or "of the natural man" in a Pauline context</note> gradually failed and was succeeded by that which is spiritual, so that when this becomes fully clear, we may also see why it shines forth. So that this may be possible, leaving the order of the narrative, we must run ahead to what follows: from Obed to Ahaziah, who was the grandfather of Amaziah, there were likewise ten generations. However, this Ahaziah was not like Noah, who was tenth from Adam; or like Abraham, who was tenth from Shem; or like Boaz, who was tenth from Isaac; for those men were just, but this one was impious and a sinner. Therefore, he was not worthy to signify God the Father, nor was Amaziah worthy to signify the Holy Spirit. For this reason, they were omitted by Matthew <note>Matthew 1:8 skips three kings between Joram and Uzziah: Ahaziah, Joash, and Amaziah.</note>. But why is this? Is it because those others attained their status by their own merit, or did these lose the grace of this honor through their own fault? Far be it! If that were so, the purpose of the wisdom of God would seem capable of change. But He who, by His just and hidden judgment, makes one vessel

<column-break/>

for honor and another for dishonor <note>original: "aliud quidem vas facit in honorem: aliud vero in contumeliam"; a reference to Romans 9:21</note>, permitted certain reprobate men to be held in the genealogy of the fathers at the time He willed. He did this to show the difference between flesh and spirit, between the justice that is of the earth and comes to an end, and that which is of heaven and remains forever. Ahaziah was therefore slain in his iniquity, and Jehoiada the High Priest rose to prominence; because of the merit of his justice, he received a burial in the company of the kings of Judah. But his son, Zechariah by name, though he was himself just like Abel, was murdered by the impious king Joash, just as the only-begotten Son of God was, in whose type these men—namely Zechariah and Abel—were slain. These are the ones whom those who sought to kill Him were seeking, as He says in the Gospel: "Behold, I send to you prophets
<margin>Matthew</margin>
and wise men and scribes; and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city, so that upon you may come all the just blood that has been shed upon the earth, from the blood of Abel the just to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar" <note>Matthew 23:34-35. Joachim links the Zechariah of the Old Testament with the one mentioned by Jesus.</note>. Thus, Noah is known to be a just man, being the tenth from Adam; Abraham was just, being the twentieth from Adam; and Boaz was merciful, being the thirtieth from Adam. Thus, in the name of the Trinity which is God, that initial image of God was completed around the end of the number thirty—namely, thirty generations in the propagation of the flesh. However, so that the justice which was to be revealed in its own time might be established (at least in part), the justice that was in the propagation of the flesh failed in some part at the fortieth step, and like the temporary brightness of the moon, it came to an end. For what good was found in this Ahaziah, who was the fortieth from the first parent, except that the number forty signifies either a fulfillment or a failure? It is not without cause, therefore, that the first of the kings of Judah was slain by the sword, through the zeal of the prophet Elisha <note>original: "Helisei"; usually referring to Elisha, though the zeal against the house of Ahab was initiated by Elijah and carried out via Jehu.</note> poured out upon Jehu to destroy the house of Ahab; this was the zeal of Elisha—nay, rather of the Holy Spirit, who hates the things of the flesh and loves the things that are His own.
